## 5. The moon calculation

### 5.1 Geometry

`moon_astro.c` computes, for a UTC epoch (ERFA `eraEpv00` + `eraMoon98` — the
same models the validated astropy pipeline uses internally):

- barycentric positions → Moon→Sun **S** and Moon→geocenter **E** (unit, ICRF);
- the **calibrated IAU_Moon body frame**: pole (RA 269.839977°, dec 68.110423°)
  and prime meridian `W0 + 13.17617251°/day × (JD - 2451545)` — this is where
  the **libration** enters: the body-frame basis carries the Moon's full
  libration in latitude/longitude automatically;
- the **camera basis** (celestial-north up, east left) rotated by the exact
  **posangle** — the on-screen orientation of the lit limb;
- outputs in `moon_geom_t`: S, E, right, up, sub-solar/sub-earth lon/lat,
  posangle, phase angle, illumination `(1 + cos i)/2`, distance.

Gate validation vs NASA: max **0.43°** sub-solar / **0.51°** sub-earth /
**0.44°** posangle over the 32-frame gate set — well inside the panel's 1-px
angular scale.

### 5.2 The bake (per pixel of the disk)

`moon_bake` (and the row-range `moon_bake_rows`) does, per panel pixel:

1. **Base-sphere direction** `r = u·right + v·up + w·E` from the on-screen (u,
   v) of the pixel (disk radius = MOON_PX/2: 200 px on the S3's 466 px panel,
   325 px on the P4's 720 px panel);
2. **Equirect albedo** (864x432, LROC WAC, row 0 = north, 180° longitude
   offset) gathered through the _live_ camera basis (libration + posangle exact
   per frame);
3. **Displaced-normal Lambert**: the surface normal is perturbed by the LOLA
   relief (2048x1024 int8 DEM, -8518…+10416 m, 254 steps) — a 4-neighbor
   central-difference gradient, pre-baked once into a packed uint16 slope cache
   (4,096 KB PSRAM, ~2.9 s at boot; one 16-bit load per pixel instead of a
   4-neighbor DEM gather) — and lit with the **unclipped** model
   `L = clip(lns, 0, 1)` with `lns = (d - G·S)/sqrt(1 + |G|²)`: mountain slopes
   brighten, crater walls shadow, exactly as the relief dictates;
4. **Night side (the backlit far side)**: on the device the unilluminated side
   is the **computed surface, not a flat overlay** — the real lunar surface
   (albedo + displaced relief) lit faintly from the _anti-solar_ direction
   (`moon_backlit_night`: `A · clip(−lns, 0, 1) · MOON_NIGHT_BACKLIT_K` with
   `K = 0.20`, peak ≈ 51/255). K is an **ARTISTIC** level, not a physical one:
   calibrated (2026-11-02) so the device's computed dark side matches the NASA
   SVS render's dark side — dark-region mean 8.0 vs 8.9 gray on the 2.1 %
   crescent frame (4.4 at the old `K = 0.10` — the sim's dark side was ~half as
   strong as the reference it should beat), within ~0.5–0.9 gray of NASA on the
   other three gate frames; plain linear gray, deliberately NOT the tone LUT,
   whose bin-1 shadow lift would over-brighten it). It is body-frame constant
   (the epoch's S is fixed), so the shade map and the spin stay a static image
   and only the projection rotates. The validated earthshine path
   (`dark_zero = 0`: `TONE_LUT[0] + earthshine(d)`) is byte-identical to the
   old model — it is what the gate and the host film run; `pole_test` proves
   BOTH the earthshine path and the backlit one (§12.2);
5. **Soft terminator (display only)**: on the display bake the hard 0 →
   tone-LUT-floor step at `lns = 0` is replaced by a smoothstep blend between
   the lit value and the backlit value across `±MOON_TERM_SOFT` (0.03 lns ≈ 6
   px either side at the 400 px disk) — the same blurred day/night boundary the
   NASA SVS render carries (a measured smear of a few pixels, not a hard step).
   Gated on `dark_zero && dk_sup == 0.0f` (the plain display bake): the dusk's
   `dk_sup` shade map and the gate's `dark_zero = 0` path keep the original
   hard terminator, so the gate's numbers stay byte-identical across the
   artistic pass;
6. **`dk_sup` dark-side bound (dusk only)**: the pole spin never changes the
   view latitude, so the _endpoint_ view still carries a geometrically lit rim
   sliver (d up to `sqrt(1 - E·S(φ*)²)`) which would linger on the dark sleep
   screen as a bright arc hugging the disk edge (the user-reported "white ray"
   — the true root cause was the shade map's ±y mirror folding mirrored
   lighting onto the seam columns). The kill is now baked into the _map_: the
   shade map writes the backlit night side for `d < dk_sup + MOON_DK_MARGIN`
   (margin 0.010 — the re-project's nearest-neighbor gather can round a
   boundary pixel to a cell up to ~half a theta-cell + half a lat-cell away in
   d, ≈ 0.0073 at 864x432, so a lit-center cell would re-light the sliver
   without the erosion), and `moon_reproject` is a **pure gather** (no `dk_sup`
   parameter). The final bake writes the backlit night side for `d < dk_sup`.
   The sliver itself is sun-lit (lns > 0), so the backlit color clips to **pure
   black** there — exactly the old flat-floor kill, and the white ray stays
   dead. At the endpoint the visible disk is entirely d < dk_sup, so the band
   between the two bounds is never on screen (no pop). Every non-dusk caller
   passes `0.0f` (the margin is inert there — the night test reduces to
   `lns ≤ 0`, byte-identical to the pre-fix code);
7. **Tone LUT**: 256-entry 8-bit → 8-bit curve (generated, in `moon_consts.h`),
   then 8-bit → RGB565. The final 8-bit → RGB565 LUT is **warm by default** (an
   ARTISTIC display choice, `moon_render.c` `g565_build`): the NASA SVS
   render's lit region is measurably warm (lit-region RGB ≈ (164,160,153)
   across the 2025 set, R/B ≈ 1.07, R−G +3.9, G−B +6.7 — the SVS white
   balance), and a warm moon reads as a real moon photo against the AMOLED's
   true black. Multipliers R ×1.038 / G ×1.000 / B ×0.933 reproduce that
   balance at every gray level (the 6-bit green field is used in full, so the
   gray stays balanced — capping green to the 5-bit value would render every
   gray magenta on the panel). `moon_gray565_set_warm(0)` rebuilds the neutral
   LUT; the image gate runs the simulator with `--neutral` so the tint never
   enters the gate's metrics (which validate the gray physics, not the display
   color).

**View-independence** (the key architectural fact): a pixel's color depends
only on the body-frame surface direction and the epoch's fixed body-frame Sun —
the camera basis selects _which direction is visible_ but never enters the
color. Consequences: the free spin and the boot sweep need no lighting
recompute (fixed-point gather only), and the dusk is a **constant projection**
— one body-frame shaded equirect map (`moon_shade_map_build`, 864x432, PSRAM,
~1.6 s on the S3 / 282 ms on the P4, 2026-11-01) is re-projected through the
folded camera basis per frame (~50 ms, `moon_reproject`); the final dark-side
frame is the one pixel-exact full `moon_bake` at φ\* = `atan2(-B, -A)` (today
+134.78° orbit-folded).

### 5.3 Rotation (the free spin)

`moon_rotate`: a fixed-point nearest-neighbor in-plane gather ("ball in hand"),
int4-quantized 10°-step orientation applied per screen, angle integrated per
frame with the rate smoothed (EMA) toward the target — active period (default
300 s/turn) while in use, **constant slow spin** (600 s/turn,
`UI_MOON_SPIN_SETTLED_PERIOD_S`) when settled, so the moon never reads as
frozen before light sleep. ~8 ms gather per frame, then the composited MOON_PX²
composite is written **straight to the panel** (one continuous 400×400 QSPI
window write on the S3; 10×65-row DSI strips on the P4) at 8 fps
(`UI_MOON_SPIN_FPS`) — the render bypasses LVGL's re-render path (the wrapped
`esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap`), so the frame cost is gather + one panel write,
not the ~175 ms re-render.

### 5.4 The clock

PCF85063A (I2C behind the TCA9554): time-of-truth source; 1.3 s software poll
(the board's RTC interrupt does not reach the MCU — §3); minute alignment
drives the display update, the deep-sleep countdown (`clock_timer`), the alarm
scheduler, and the hourly NTP trigger. SNTP (`clock_sntp`, `pool.ntp.org`, 10 s
timeout) syncs at boot (blocking) and on demand (background task) —
wake/manual/hourly — after which the modem drops back to airplane.

---

## 6. Design-driven language

The UI's design system is a deliberate reduction to what the hardware is: a
round AMOLED showing the Moon.

- **Palette — moon grey / white on black, only.** `SETTINGS_GREY` (mid grey,
  unselected/inactive/structure) and `SETTINGS_WHITE` (active/value) on black.
  No other hue: the Moon has no color, so neither does the UI. Blue exists in
  no themed state (an early design's blue knob dots was explicitly removed —
  task #55). The clock digits and the moon share the white; the grey carries
  the "you can press this" affordance.
- **Type — Montserrat**, generated subsets (`lv_font_conv`, 4-bit,
  uncompressed; the S3's `fonts/` is the source of truth): 96 px digits (the
  clock), 48 px (rollers/labels), 32 px general text (SSID rows/captions/_
  password entry_ — full printable ASCII 32–126, so one font serves the list
  and the wheel keyboard; it was widened from an `A-Z`/digits subset for the
  keyboard; the wheel's centre preview runs at this size too — the 48 px font
  is the digits-only subset, no letters) + a 32 px range subset (the "Mo-Fr"
  day summary, whose font needs only digits-free lowercase + hyphen); plus
  LVGL's **built-in** `lv_font_montserrat_14` (Kconfig
  `CONFIG_LV_FONT_MONTSERRAT_14`) for the small captions — the WiFi-list
  header, the wheel's SSID caption, the register-key labels and the "release
  commits" hint. The P4 builds the _same six subsets_ from the same Opts at
  ×720/466 (148/74/50 px) in `fonts_p4/` with identical symbol names (§2.3b M4
  state) — two of them widened in M5.6 for the P4-reached time entry: the FA
  Regular now also carries the clock glyph (U+F017) and the 74 px numbers the
  `.` date separator, S3 `fonts/` untouched (the built-in 14 px font is the
  same on both panels). Font Awesome 7 Free (Solid 96 px:
  circle-xmark/moon/wifi/stopwatch; Regular: moon/alarm-clock + clock on the
  P4) — the icon set is the same weight-and-color logic as the type.
- **Geometry — concentric circles.** The home screen _is_ the moon: disk center
  = screen center. The settings hub mirrors it: a central circle-xmark exit
  (the fa-circle-xmark glyph alone — the glyph _is_ the button, U+F057) with
  the sub-screen icons on a 45° diagonal ring at radius ~165; every
  sub-screen's exit is the same glyph, smaller, top-center. The alarm day range
  is a two-ended range arc with draggable handles — the same thin outer ring as
  the home seconds arc (outer radius 223, 10 px from the panel edge), the range
  in the moon colour.
- **Motion — the moon's own.** Screen switches **fade to black and back** via
  the panel's own hardware brightness (dim to black, load, brighten back —
  §10.4); the moon screens themselves switch atomically as always. The base
  +90° orientation is an LVGL root transform, so "screen center" is the panel
  center. Sleep is motion with meaning: the dusk _is_ the terminator
  travelling, not a fade.
- **Interaction — touch-only, gesture-honest.** Taps open; drags on rollers
  (persist only on RELEASED — SPIFFS/I2C stay off the drag path); the day-range
  handles snap; an idle timeout (runtime) dims into light sleep; waking shows
  the _current_ phase statically — the device never re-animates history.

---

## 7. Screens — every live screen with its settings

All 15 screens, exact panel pixels from the UI simulator at both panel sizes
(all 15 live on the S3; the manual time entry, §7.15, now renders at 466 and
720 alike). The "settings displayed" column lists what the screen shows and
what each control changes live.

### 7.1 Airplane (modem sleep) — the home screen

![airplane](img/screens/modem_sleep.png)

- The moon disk at the current phase (the free spin animates it), the clock (96
  px HH:MM, two-digit), the live seconds arc around the disk, and **below the
  clock the next alarm** — the HH:MM of the next scheduled fire, preceded by
  the two-letter weekday of that fire ("Mo 07:00", 32 px range font, grey)
  whenever the fire is more than 24 h away; within 24 h the prefix drops and
  the time stands alone (the weekday only carries meaning across a day the rule
  skips).
- **The clock digits sit in fixed-width slots** (the "no wobble" fix): the 96
  px numbers font is _proportional_ — "1" advances 37.6 px, "4" 66.1 px, the
  colon 25.1 px — so one label reading HH:MM ran 175.6 px wide at "11:11" and
  289.6 px at "44:44", and the whole string hopped sideways on every minute
  change. Each character now has its own centred `lv_label` of fixed width (67
  px per digit — the maximum digit advance; 26 px for the colon — its own
  advance; `UI_PX`-scaled for the P4's 148 px font, where the maxes are 101.9 /
  38.7 px against the 103 / 40 px slots), so the string is a constant 294 px
  (at 466) and only the ink moves. `objects[16+1]` stays the slot row — the P4
  unsynced-clock dim still targets it with `lv_obj_set_style_opa` and the style
  cascades to the five labels — and the minute tick updates only the
  character(s) that changed, not the whole string.
- **ONE shared clock widget** (2026-11-04 bugreport): the five moon screens
  (airplane / WiFi / light sleep / deep sleep / alarm) used to each carry their
  own clock widget (five sets of HH:MM slots + alarm label) and only the
  _active_ screen's set was ticked — so a wake showed the pre-wake value held
  by the newly revealed screen's labels until the next minute tick (the "quick
  adjustment" on wake). There is now exactly one widget, created once on the
  airplane screen (`objects[16/17/18]`); the other four screens' bases
  (`objects[21/26/30/35]` +1/+2) **alias the same three objects** (the layout
  contract in `screens.h`). The minute tick (`action_update_clock_display`)
  ticks it from the vars regardless of the active screen, and the `loadScreen`
  choke point reparents it onto the new moon screen and refreshes the vars from
  the RTC _before_ the switch's atomic flush (`ui_clock_attach_to`), so every
  switch — the wake in particular — shows the current minute in the one frame.
  Settings screens are moon-less: the widget stays where it was, computed but
  not rendered.
- **No icons** — the moon stays in the foreground (user decision).
- Tapping anywhere (the clock container is non-clickable so the tap falls
  through to the screen root) opens the settings hub.
- This screen is also the **sleep state**: idle timeout → light sleep. While it
  hosts the boot, the synodic sweep plays here.

### 7.2 WiFi (transient)

![wifi](img/screens/wifi.png)

- Shown only while a sync is in flight (wake / manual / hourly / NTP-failed
  boot); drops back to airplane on completion.
- Same moon + clock as airplane, plus the **connection indicator below the
  clock** (grey = connecting, white = connected; non-clickable).
- The boot sweep plays on this screen when the boot clock is still being
  acquired (the seamless hand-off: both screens share the one moon image).

### 7.3 Light sleep — the dusk

![light sleep](img/screens/light_sleep.png)

- The pole-axis spin to the fully unilluminated side (constant projection,
  1°/frame, shade map baked once — S3 ~1.6 s / P4 282 ms, 2026-11-01; final
  frame a pixel-exact bake at φ\*; the dark side is the **faint backlit
  surface** — the real lunar terrain lit from the anti-solar direction, peak ≈
  51/255 (K = 0.20, §5.2 item 4), so the far side stays visible on the AMOLED
  without a flat overlay).
- The clock's **opacity is a compile-time option**: the light-sleep entry sets
  the shared clock widget's container to `UI_CLOCK_ALPHA_PCT` (Kconfig, int,
  range 0–100, **default 100** = full opacity) and the wake restores it to
  full. The old hard-coded ~20 % alpha is gone: light sleep now dims the
  _whole_ panel via its own hardware brightness (the line below), so the clock
  no longer needs the low alpha to read as "barely visible" — the alpha is the
  option to dim the clock _further_ relative to the moon (e.g. 40). One
  application point (the light-sleep entry) covers every moon-background clock
  display because the clock is a single shared widget (§7.1). The moon image is
  a sibling of the clock container, so it stays at full contrast.
- The **whole display glows down too**: the panel's own hardware brightness
  (the CO5300 0x51 / the P4 backlight PWM) ramps from its current level to
  `UI_LIGHT_SLEEP_DIM_PCT` (default 25 %, Kconfig) over `UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE`
  ms — the same 0x51 steps the fade uses, serialized on `s_panel_mtx` and held
  against the spin's panel writes (`s_fade_busy`, §10.4) so a brightness write
  is never queued behind a strip DMA. The dusk keeps spinning at the new level
  (the frames display from the same LVGL task, so they simply resume after the
  ramp). The wake / an alarm ring ramps back to 100 (`moon_ui_panel_dim_ramp`);
  a re-entry ramps from the already-dimmed level, and the fade-out before a
  screen switch now starts from the _tracked_ level (not a hard-coded 100) so a
  dimmed→black switch never flashes brighter first.
- On the last frame the deep-sleep countdown arms (runtime
  `deep_sleep_countdown_sec`, default 60 s).

### 7.4 Deep sleep

![deep sleep](img/screens/deep_sleep.png)

- The dark side at φ\* (the final dusk bake, its backlit far-side surface),
  **the clock hidden**, and the **backlight off** after the countdown — the
  panel is genuinely dark (AMOLED), the RTC keeps counting; an alarm can fire
  from here and restore the backlight. Clock updates are gated while the
  backlight is off (no live minute updates in deep sleep). The backlight off/on
  (here, on wake, and at boot) goes through `moon_ui_panel_brightness_set` —
  the 0x51 write is serialized on `s_panel_mtx` so it is never queued behind a
  spin strip DMA that could stall the bus (§10.4).

### 7.5 Alarm (fired)

![alarm](img/screens/alarm.png)

- Shown when the scheduler fires (RTC-minute-poll; also from deep sleep,
  backlight restored). Touch dismisses and re-arms. The screen carries the
  alarm indicator icon and the time; there is **no automatic sleep transition**
  while it is up (task: the alarm must not dusk-sleep mid- dismiss).
- **P4: the ring** (`components/ui/alarm_audio.c`, M5.5). The fired alarm also
  rings through the board's ES8311 codec + speaker amp (the codec joins the
  GT911 on the shared I2C bus; `bsp_audio_codec_speaker_init` at boot, soft
  fail → display-only). A per-fire ring task streams a pre-baked A5/E5 two-tone
  loop (mono 16-bit @ 22050 Hz, MCLK = 256×FS — the ES8311's PLL pair) through
  the **blocking I2S write** (it paces at the audio rate, so the loop is
  real-time) while the volume **ramps up gradually** over the first ~2.5 s (no
  startup click at a full level). The touch dismiss **snoozes**: every dismiss
  path runs through `action_wake_screen`, which sets the stop flag; the ring
  task fades the volume out over ~150 ms and closes the codec (DAC + I2S TX
  disabled — the next alarm re-opens it). The S3 has no audio hardware: the
  ring functions are no-op stubs there and its alarm path is untouched.

### 7.6 Settings hub

![hub](img/screens/settings_hub.png)

- Central **circle-xmark exit** — the fa-circle-xmark glyph alone (U+F057; the
  glyph is the button, no ring chrome; 150 px tap box) → back to the **home
  (airplane) screen**, no sync kicked off.
- **Icon ring, equal-arc** (2026-11-01): the entries sit on a circle of radius
  `UI_PX(117)` at **equal 360/n arc distances** — 5 icons (72°) on the S3, 6
  icons (60°) on the P4 — with deep sleep pinned at 6 o'clock (the bottom).
  Clock positions: **S3** — top-left globe (U+F0AC, solid; the timezone / UTC
  offset picker, §7.16), top-right alarm (alarm-clock, regular), mid-right
  light sleep (moon, regular), bottom deep sleep (moon, solid — the weight
  distinguishes the two moons), mid-left WiFi (wifi, solid). **P4** — the same
  five plus a sixth icon at 12 o'clock: clock (regular, U+F017, the glyph the
  FA regular set regenerated for it, §2.3b) opening the manual time entry
  (§7.15; the S3 has no clock icon — its time comes from the PCF85063A). The
  globe glyph was added to both boards' FA solid subsets (regenerated with
  U+F0AC = 61612 — the earlier regen used 61516 = U+F04C "pause" by mistake, so
  the hub showed a missing-glyph box).
- Grey = present/available, white = selected; the sub-screens' bottom-centre
  exit is the same glyph at 96 px and returns to the **calling level** (the
  hub, or the alarm screen for its two sub-screens). The exit is a plain
  (non-scrollable) `lv_obj` — LVGL 9 defaults objects to scrollable, and the
  glyph's label line-height exceeds the box, which drew a vertical scrollbar at
  the box's right edge (the thin line crossing the circle) on every sub-screen;
  the `LV_OBJ_FLAG_SCROLLABLE` is cleared on the shared
  `settings_create_exit_button` helper.

### 7.7 Alarm settings

![alarm settings](img/screens/settings_alarm.png)

- Header (alarm-clock, grey). Three glyphs: the **large central alarm-clock**
  is the master deactivate-all toggle (white when any rule exists, grey when
  none; tap → `clock_alarm_deactivate_all()` — the 0-rule boot also disarms the
  PCF85063A's persistent ALM); the **stopwatch** (pomodoro) and the
  **alarm-clock** (real alarm) are mutually exclusive — activating one replaces
  the other's rule. Colors refreshed on entry and after every save.

### 7.8 Pomodoro

![pomodoro](img/screens/settings_pomodoro.png)

- Two `lv_roller`s (hours 0-23, minutes 0-59) in the **96 px bold numbers
  font** (the home-clock digits — these read as the clock's HH:MM),
  `visible_row count(1)`, grey text / white selected row (LV*PART_INDICATOR),
  transparent bg. Each roller box is **140 px wide**: Montserrat's digits are
  \_proportional*, not tabular, so the worst-case "44" pair advances 132 px at
  the 96 px font (204 px at the P4's 148) — the old 120 px box clipped the
  right digit flat at its edge. 140 px leaves a margin for the full pair. The
  two rollers read as the clock's HH:MM — a `:` (the bold 96 font carries the
  colon) sits between them and the whole display is centred on the home clock
  label's position (task #68).
- `RELEASED` persists `minutes_total = H*60+M` (reject 0) via
  `clock_alarm_set_pomodoro_interval()` → the cron rule `*/N * * * *` (N up to
  1440 — the scheduler's total-minute grid across the day). Seeded from the
  current interval rule.
- **Settings displayed:** the current interval (HH:MM), which the two rollers
  edit; the write + scheduler re-parse are logged
  (`Parsed alarm rule: every N minutes`, `Next alarm scheduled for ...`).

### 7.9 Alarm time (the day-range arc)

![alarm time](img/screens/settings_alarm_time.png)

- **Day range**: a two-ended range arc on the **same thin outer ring as the
  home screen's seconds arc** (a 466×466 object at (0,0); ring outer radius
  223, 10 px from the panel edge) — the former 7 weekday letters are gone (task
  #91), so the ring owns the outer band. The dark track (LV_PART_MAIN) spans
  the upper half-circle (Monday left, Sunday right); the **moon-colour
  (SETTINGS_GREY) indicator** spans the range; two 34 px grey handles at r 218
  are the range endpoints (PRESS_LOCK; PRESSED/PRESSING snap the endpoint to
  the nearest of the 7 day angles 181+30°·d; RELEASED saves).
- **Day summary**: the "Mo-Fr" range text (32 px range font — lowercase +
  hyphen subset) above the time carries the day meaning (a single day shows
  "We"; wrap included, "Fr-Mo").
- **Time**: 96 px HH:MM at the clock position with two rollers in the **96 px
  bold numbers font** (hours 0-23, minutes ×5) and the colon between — 140 px
  wide boxes (the proportional digits' "44" pair runs 132 px; the 120 px box
  clipped the minutes at the right edge); RELEASED saves
  `clock_alarm_set_clock_alarm(h, m, dow_mask)` → the cron rule
  `M H * * <dow>`.
- A self-diagnosing **read-back log** prints after every save
  (`read-back: rule_types=0xNN fixed=ok got HH:MM mask 0xNN MATCH|MISMATCH`) so
  a device regression localizes to the write/re-parse layer vs the UI color
  refresh.
- **Settings displayed:** the fixed time (HH:MM), the day range (ring + "Mo-Fr"
  summary), and — via the save log — the parsed rule the scheduler re-loaded.

### 7.10 Light-sleep settings

![light sleep settings](img/screens/settings_light_sleep.png)

- Header moon (regular). One 48 px roller (in **minutes**, 1-30) + one
  icon-only animation toggle (96 px **regular (unfilled) moon**, white = on /
  grey = off; no switch widget) on one horizontal line. The toggle icon's
  weight tracks its hub entry — the idle-timeout screen reads the regular
  (unfilled) moon, the sleep-countdown screen (§7.11) the solid one, exactly
  the regular / solid pair the hub's two moon entries use. The roller is the
  **idle timeout** — `RELEASED` → `settings_set_idle_timeout_sec` + live
  `clock_idle_set_timeout_ms()`
  - store save (takes effect immediately). The toggle is the **sleep-transition
    animation** (the dusk) — `dusk_anim_enable` (the boot-sweep flag
    `boot_anim_enable` stays in the store but is not exposed here).
- **Settings displayed:** the idle timeout value + the dusk flag.

### 7.11 Deep-sleep settings

![deep sleep settings](img/screens/settings_deep_sleep.png)

- Header moon (solid). One 48 px roller (in **minutes**, 1-30) + the same
  icon-only dusk toggle (here the **solid** moon, the counterpart of the
  idle-timeout screen's unfilled one, §7.10). The roller is the **deep-sleep
  countdown** — `RELEASED` → `settings_set_deep_sleep_countdown_sec` + save
  (takes effect at the next dusk arming).
- **Settings displayed:** the countdown value + the dusk flag.

### 7.12 WiFi settings

![wifi settings](img/screens/settings_wifi.png)

- Header (wifi, solid). A **scan list** (background scan task: `esp_wifi_init`
  → STA → blocking scan → `esp_wifi_stop()` — scan only, credentials untouched,
  back to airplane): 7 rows at 24 px (the old 12 ran off the bottom of the
  panel), SSID upper-cased for font display (32 px font), grey = available /
  white = selected + a left-margin white bar on the selected row. **A tap on a
  row opens the circular wheel keyboard** (§7.13) with that AP's SSID prefilled
  (case kept — the upper-casing is display-only, the credential is written
  raw).
- **Settings displayed:** the live AP list from the radio (RSSI-ordered), the
  selection state.

### 7.13 WiFi password entry — the circular wheel keyboard

![at rest](img/screens/settings_wifi_password.png)
![touched down — the pressed sector's boxes revealed, the lit box inverted](img/screens/settings_wifi_password_touched.png)
![123 mode](img/screens/settings_wifi_password_123.png)

Reached by tapping an AP row on the WiFi screen (§7.12). A 13th screen
(`SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_WIFI_PASSWORD`) built around the panel centre (466×466
centre on the S3; the wheel's radii are `UI_PX()`-scaled, §2.3b M4 state); no
moon image (settings are moon-less by design). This is the **v2 "12-sector
hybrid"** (approved and implemented 2026-11-02; the operable 1:1 reference is
the lab's panel #1, §7.14) — the v1 two-frame wheel (grouped-in-threes inner
ring + a 2×-angle outer reveal) is the earlier iteration it replaced.

- **The at-rest ring.** The 26 slots of the active register at r 168 (32 px
  SSID font), 12 hairline sector dividers spanning r 150–226, and two band
  hairlines at r 150 / r 226. The grouping is the wayfinding device: the eye
  aims at 12 coarse sectors, not 26 targets. The SSID caption (case kept) sits
  in the upper centre.
- **Proportional sectors.** Every letter owns an equal
  `SHARE = 360/26 ≈ 13.846°` of the ring; the 12 frequency-grouped sectors
  `[ab][cd][ef][gh][il][jkq][mn][op][rs][tu][vxz][wy]` span `n·SHARE` (a
  2-letter sector 27.7°, the two 3-letter sectors 41.5°). The grouping is
  **fixed across all four registers**, so sector boundaries never move when the
  register changes — the muscle memory of the press position survives the
  `abc → 123` switch. (The digit/symbol registers are shorter than 26; their
  groups fill in order.)
- **The reveal.** On touch-down anywhere in the ring band (r 140–233, radially
  forgiving — a transparent `ADV_HITTEST` arc is the press target), **only the
  pressed sector's boxes appear**: one thick (76 px) non-rounded arc box per
  letter, tiling the sector edge-to-edge across r 150–226 — the ring band
  itself, so the reveal replaces the at-rest letters under the finger (no
  second cramped ring). The lit box **inverts** (white fill, near-black
  letter); the pressed sector's at-rest letters hide so the reveal letters do
  not double. The reveal is **sticky** to the pressed sector — sliding across a
  sector boundary sweeps over that sector's boxes, it does not re-key the set.
- **Hit-test.** The **exact box under the finger**: the finger's angle names
  the sector, the offset-in-sector (`floor(Δangle / SHARE)`) names the box — no
  nearest-centre tie-break (v1's 2× overlap is gone; the boxes tile the ring
  exactly). **Release commits the letter** under the finger; nothing commits on
  press or zone-crossing, so a slow sweep can never double-enter.
- **Centre preview (DTMF-style).** While pressed the lit letter is shown in the
  centre (32 px SSID font — the 48 px font is the digits-only subset, no
  letters) + "release commits"; on release the character commits and the full
  running entry re-appears, **unmasked** (the user is physically present): the
  last 6 characters with a `…` prefix when longer, `....` when empty.
- **Register/shift arc.** 4 individually-tappable 60° switch keys
  `abc / ABC / 123 / #$` on the top 240° arc (r 84–144, LVGL 150°–390° with a
  360/0 wrap; the active key lit at `150 + 60·m … 210 + 60·m`, the key labels
  at LVGL 180/240/300/360° r 114); a press resolves to the **exact 60° sector
  under the finger** (not the nearest key) and re-strings the 26 slots (digits:
  `0123456789#@._-+*?!/&%:;,` — 25 slots; symbols: `#$%&@!_=<>[]{}~^:,/?*+-.'`
  — 25 slots). Case is separate (lower/upper) because it matters for passwords.
  The lit key's **indicator carries the same pad as the track** (both
  `WHEEL_C − UI_PX(144)`), so the lit 60° arc covers the track's r 84–144
  annulus exactly; a 0 indicator pad pushed the lit key out to r 173–233, over
  the letter ring (the "big lit wedge across the letters" of the 2026-11-04 bug
  report — the "ABC highlights abc and 123" photos). Switching to a 25-slot
  register also **clears** the 26th letter label — leaving it would hold the
  previous register's "z" at its stale position (the stray "Z" after a register
  switch).
- **Bottom band — commit / discard.** The bottom 120° splits into the house
  circle-xmark **COMMIT** key (LVGL 31.5°–88.5°, icon at LVGL 60° r 114) and
  the trash **DISCARD** key (LVGL 91.5°–148.5°, icon at LVGL 120° r 114).
  Commit (with a non-empty password) writes `wifi_credentials_write(ssid, pw)`
  (two lines to `/spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt`, the password never logged) →
  `action_start_wifi_sync()` (the 6144 B background task) and the screen swaps
  to the transient WiFi screen (§7.2); on success the app leaves airplane mode.
  An empty password is not written. Discard clears the entry without writing —
  and **with an empty entry it exits to the WiFi list instead** (2026-11-04:
  backspace on an empty entry is a no-op, so the trash doubles as the
  zero-input exit; the centre long press is the other exit, §7.13 centre
  gestures). The circle-xmark is the house exit glyph **repurposed as the
  commit key** (a deliberate v2 deviation from v1, where it was the exit).
- **Centre gestures.** A plain tap on the centre (the 110 px tap box)
  **backspaces**; a **400 ms long press on the centre returns to the WiFi
  list** (no write, no sync) — v2 has no in-ring exit (the xmark glyph is the
  commit key), and the centre box (r ≈ 55) never overlaps the sweep band (r
  140–233), so the hold cannot start a letter. The screen's angular picking
  uses the inverse-transform idiom (`lv_obj_transform_point`,
  `LV_OBJ_POINT_TRANSFORM_FLAG_INVERSE`, the `alarm_time_point_to_day`
  pattern), so it stays correct under the 90° orientation roll.
- **Known interaction (stated, not suppressed):** the global 2 s press
  orientation re-sync also fires on long sweeps; it is pose-stability gated and
  only re-anchors the home reference, and the wheel is transform-aware, so a
  mid-sweep re-pose cannot move the letter under the finger.
- **LVGL notes.** The clickable arcs (press band, mode arc, commit/discard)
  carry `LV_OBJ_FLAG_ADV_HITTEST` — without it `lv_arc` falls back to a plain
  bounding-box hit test and the last-created arc wins the search. Every arc
  also gets the theme's blue circular KNOB (colour primary, opaque) — killed
  with `bg_opa TRANSP` on `LV_PART_KNOB` (on a full ring it lands at the centre
  as a blue disc). The radial hairlines/icons are thin `lv_obj` bars (LVGL's
  `lv_line` is not built) rotated with `lv_obj_transform_rotation` in **0.1°
  units** (pass deg×10 — v1 passed raw degrees and its ticks under-rotated 10×,
  a latent bug the v2 rewrite fixes). **The transform pivot defaults to the
  object's TOP-LEFT corner** (the style's `transform_pivot_x/y` start at 0), so
  every rotated bar — the 12 sector dividers, the per-box dividers, the four
  mode-arc ticks and the commit key's two X-bars — sets an explicit
  `LV_PCT(50)` pivot at creation, or its rotation would swing it on a long arc
  instead of spinning in place. That default pivot is what drew the stray line
  through "z" and disassembled the commit icon in the 2026-11-04 bug report.
- **Alternatives surveyed (2026-11-01):** the research note
  `docs/research/circular-keyboard-alternatives.md` evaluates the circular
  wheel against the published round-display text-entry literature (C-QWERTY,
  COMPASS, Crownboard, Tap'nSwipe, in-car dial studies) for this hardware — the
  sweep wheel is confirmed as the right family; a 12-sector DTMF-style
  multi-tap ring and hold-to-commit dwell are the ranked low-cost additions.
- **Settings displayed:** the prefilled SSID, the running password, the active
  register, the selected letter.
- **Device check (pending):** the 0.7–1.5 s/character estimate and the sweep's
  real-glass feel (touch latency, how far a finger actually travels in 0.7 s)
  are the pending bench verification (the research's open question 2).

### 7.14 The wheel's design choices — interactive lab, comparable layouts, and the v2 hybrid

The wheel is the product's one text-entry surface, so its design choices are
documented as a first-class section, with the **interactive design lab** as the
clickable reference instead of static mockups:

**The interactive design lab** — `docs/keyboard/round-keyboard-lab.html` (a
single self-contained page, no build, no server; open it straight from the
working tree). It renders **all 13 text-entry methods** researched for this
panel at **true 1:1 scale** (every mock is a 466×466 SVG — the device's own
panel geometry, the device's own black-on-black AMOLED palette), and the
feasible ones are **actually operable in the browser** (pointer events, the
device's timing constants) so the feel can be compared before any C is written.
Panels:

1. **Sweep wheel v2 — 12-sector hybrid (KEEP, the approved direction)** — the
   v2 spec below.
2. 12-sector DTMF multi-tap (1–4 presses, 700 ms window — the coarse-press +
   centre-preview model v2 inherits).
3. Hold-to-commit dwell (400 ms; the gesture-free fallback).
4. Auto-scan, Crownboard-style (the lit sector steps clockwise at 1/s; tap
   commits — the "setting" alternative).
5. 9×4 swipe sectors, Tap'nSwipe (press, drag, direction picks the char).
6. Fitted QWERTY 6×6 (operable, to make the rejection case by feel).
7. Ring glide / one-stroke (the over-swipe risk, made visible).
8. IMU twist (body rotation drives the ring — the gesture-vs-reorientation
   conflict).
9. Physical rotary encoder (12 sectors + side crown — the hardware-revision
   upgrade). 10–13. Off-hardware: voice, camera/OCR, QR/NFC/BLE handoff, T9
   dictionary decode (each with its infeasibility/rejection reason).

Every panel carries the research report's evidence rows (best published speed,
accuracy evidence with source, implementation cost on ESP32-S3 + LVGL,
verdict), and the page's verdict strip ranks them: the wheel family keeps, DTMF
multi-tap + dwell ship as additions, QWERTY / glide / voice / OCR / handoff /
T9-dictionary reject. **The lab is the documentation's interactive half**: the
static sections below describe the same choices; the page lets a user _operate_
them. It is committed to the repo (`docs/keyboard/`) so the documented design
choices and the operable reference cannot drift apart — the page is pure
vanilla HTML/SVG/JS with no external assets beyond a Google Fonts link (it
degrades gracefully offline).

**How the v2 hybrid works (user view)** — the panel #1 mock, in one paragraph:
press anywhere on the ring. The ring **reveals only the pressed sector's
letters**, on top of the rest of the wheel (the reveal spans the inner circle's
radius band, so the whole ring reads as one keyboard). Sweep to the letter —
the **centre of the disk previews the letter under the finger live**
(DTMF-style: while pressed you always see what you are about to commit; on
release the full running entry re-appears). **Release commits the letter.** The
top arc switches the register (`abc / ABC / 123 / #$` — four large 60° keys);
the bottom of the ring is a **⊗ commit** key and a **trash discard** key; a
**tap on the centre backspaces**. No double-entry is possible: the commit
happens only on release, and the hit-test is the exact box under the finger (no
nearest-centre tie-break). One firmware addition beyond the mock: v2 has no
in-ring exit (the ⊗ glyph is the commit key), so a **400 ms long press on the
centre is the only way back to the WiFi list** (§7.13) — the centre box never
overlaps the sweep band, so the hold cannot start a letter.

**The v2 geometry (shipped)** — what the mock specified and the firmware
implements (the device behaviour now, §7.13; measured against the mock and the
v1 it replaced):

- **Proportional sectors.** 26 letters, every letter owns an equal
  `SHARE = 360/26 ≈ 13.846°` of the ring; sector `k` (holding `n` letters)
  spans `n·SHARE` — a 2-letter sector 27.7°, the two 3-letter sectors (j/k/q
  and v/x/z) 41.5°. The grouping (12 sectors:
  `[ab][cd][ef][gh] [il][j k q][mn][op][rs][tu][v x z][wy]`) is fixed across
  all four registers, so **sector boundaries never move when the register
  changes** — the muscle memory of the press position survives the `abc → 123`
  switch. (v1 grouped the alphabet in threes; v2 groups by the keyboard's
  frequency pairs + the two 3-clusters, which is what makes the 12 sectors fit
  exactly.)
- **The reveal.** On touch-down the pressed sector's letters are drawn
  **edge-to-edge across r 150–226 — the inner circle's own radius band**, so
  the reveal _replaces_ the at-rest ring under the finger (no second, cramped
  ring, and no redrawing the rest of the screen: the reveal is the only new
  content, region-limited invalidation). Hairline dividers at the box edges;
  the lit box inverts (white fill, black letter).
- **Hit-test.** Exact box: `Math.floor(angle-in-sector / SHARE)` — the box
  under the finger is the letter. v1's 2× nearest-centre overlap is gone,
  because the boxes tile the sector exactly (360/26 per letter, so the target
  is as wide as v1's inner slot, drawn at the reveal radius).
- **Centre preview / handback.** While pressed: the lit letter large in the
  centre + "release commits". On release: the full running entry (last 6
  characters + `…`), as in v1.
- **Register arc.** Four 60° keys on the top arc (240°–480°, i.e. the top half)
  — wider than v1's 42°–138° 4-key arc, so a press is resolved by exact sector,
  not nearest key.
- **Commit / discard / backspace.** Bottom of the ring: ⊗ (24 px, the house
  exit glyph, v1's deviation kept) commits the entry (`wifi_credentials_write`
  - the background WiFi sync, §7.13); the trash key discards without writing;
    centre tap = backspace. The 400 ms centre long-press survives as the **back
    gesture**: v1's long-press would have competed with the sweep press (both
    in the ring band), but the centre box (r ≈ 55) sits clear of the sweep band
    (r 140–233), so the hold cannot start a letter — it returns to the WiFi
    list, the one path v2's exit-less layout requires (see the firmware
    addition above).

The mock's estimates (the card's own rows): **0.7–1.5 s/character** (≈4–8 CPM
for passwords), equal-share targets + big centre preview + release-only commit
as the accuracy story, **a few hundred lines of LVGL arcs** with region-limited
invalidation as the cost. It is a prototype mock, not a benchmark — the
real-glass CST9217 feel (touch latency, the sweep's angular velocity, how far a
finger actually travels in 0.7 s) is the pending device check (the research's
open question 2).

**Comparable layouts and where the ideas came from** — the full ranked survey
is the research note `docs/research/circular-keyboard-alternatives.md`
(2026-11-01); the table below is the compact version, with the idea source each
v2 element took from:

| Method                                              | Published evidence                                                                               | Status                  | What v2 took from it                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Sweep wheel (coarse press + sweep, release commits) | C-QWERTY (2020) — ring of keys on a circular watch face; the wheel shipped as v1, now v2 (§7.13) | **KEEP (v2 shipped)**   | the whole model: 12 coarse press targets, sweep to resolve, release commits (no auto-commit → no double-entry)                             |
| 12-sector DTMF multi-tap (1–4 presses, 700 ms)      | T9/DTMF multi-tap; Crownboard's commit-on-release                                                | SHIP as a register mode | the **centre preview** — the selected char shown in the middle until release commits, then the full entry re-appears                       |
| Hold-to-commit dwell (400 ms)                       | dwell-click literature; the gesture-free fallback                                                | SHIP as a setting       | the backstop for users who won't sweep: hold a box, it commits on its own                                                                  |
| Auto-scan (Crownboard)                              | Crownboard (CHI 2023) — rotation + commit on a 3D-printed watch                                  | SHIP as a setting       | the "hands-barely-move" mode: the lit box steps at 1/s, a tap commits the lit one                                                          |
| 9×4 swipe sectors (Tap'nSwipe)                      | Tap'nSwipe (IJHCI 2025) — 9 sectors × 4 chars, swipe direction selects                           | HOLD                    | the sector-count sanity check (9×4 ≈ 36 ≈ 12×3; coarse sectors win over 26 fine taps)                                                      |
| Fitted QWERTY 6×6                                   | smartwatch QWERTY trace/tap studies (SAGE 2019) — tap WPM on a round face                        | **REJECTED**            | keys land at ~3.5 mm, a quarter of a fingertip — below touch resolution; the lab panel makes it tappable so the case is felt, not asserted |
| Ring glide / one-stroke                             | —                                                                                                | REJECTED as primary     | no word model to recover an arbitrary password string from an over-swipe                                                                   |
| IMU twist                                           | QMI8658C is on-board (free)                                                                      | EXPERIMENTAL            | the body-roll conflict: a twist gesture fights the 90° orientation tracker (§10.3)                                                         |
| Physical rotary encoder                             | in-car dial studies (Brewster CHI 2017) — physical certainty, >94 % accuracy                     | v2 board (hardware)     | the strongest evidence-backed upgrade — a hardware revision, not firmware                                                                  |
| Voice / camera / QR / NFC / BLE / T9-dictionary     | —                                                                                                | INFEASIBLE / no fit     | the board has no mic/camera/NFC; a companion app for a once-per-network task is not worth it; T9 needs a word model, a password has none   |

The **idea sources in one line**: coarse press + sweep + release-commit is the
shipped wheel (itself confirmed by C-QWERTY/Crownboard-class work); the centre
preview is the DTMF panel (#2) lifted into v2; the proportional grouping is the
lab's own re-derivation (26 equal shares, 12 fixed sectors); the overlay reveal
is the lab's answer to "the outer ring is too cramped" (user direction — the
DTMF centre preview and the reveal-overlaying-the-inner circle);
⊗/trash/centre-backspace follow the house pattern (the circle-xmark exit glyph,
§7.13).

**Status.** The v2 hybrid is **shipped** (2026-11-02): §7.13 describes the
device behaviour, its screenshots are re-rendered from the v2 `screens.c`
through the UI simulator (466 ×466 + 720 ×720), and the only deltas from the
mock are the documented ones — the 32 px centre preview (the 48 px font is the
digits-only subset) and the centre long-press back gesture. The lab mock
remains the normative interaction spec and the geometry table above the
normative geometry; the v1 two-frame wheel is the iteration it replaced (its
screenshots and prose are the earlier revision of §7.13 in git history).

### 7.15 Manual time entry (P4)

![manual time entry](img/screens/p4/settings_time.png)

- **Why it exists:** the P4 has no RTC IC, and before its first SNTP sync the
  wall clock sits at its default (or the NVS-restored epoch after a power loss)
  — dimmed to 50 % and the alarm fire gate closed (M5.1/M5.2). This screen sets
  the clock by hand. The **date** must be settable, not just the time: a stale
  date keeps the moon phase and the alarm weekdays wrong for months (the
  2026-01-24 default is nine months off on today's wall clock).
- **Reach:** the settings hub's 12 o'clock clock icon (P4 only, §7.6). The
  screen itself is shared — the S3 build carries it structurally identical,
  simply unreachable (no icon; its time comes from the PCF85063A).
- **Layout:** a caption ("SET TIME / DATE", 32 px, grey) over two roller rows —
  the **time row** HH:MM (the 96 px clock font, at the home clock label's
  position; the `:` from the same font) and the **date row** DD.MM.YY (the 48
  px font; the `.` from the regenerated 48 px numbers subset — the S3's 48 px
  set now carries `-` and `.` like the P4's 74 px subset, §2.3b; the year as a
  two-digit 2000+YY). The same roller look as the other settings value displays
  (grey rows, white selected row, three visible rows; the time row's rollers
  are the 140 px boxes of the other 96 px-font value displays, §7.8/§7.9). **No
  seconds roller** (2026-11-01): adjusting seconds has no visible effect (the
  home label shows HH:MM) and the commit therefore writes second = 0.
- **Seed:** the rollers seed from `clock_sntp_get_system_time` on entry — the
  day/month option strings start at "01", so their selected index is value−1
  (hour/minute/year start at "00" and index = value).
- **Commit:** releasing ANY of the five rollers — **or pressing the X exit**
  (2026-11-01: the exit used to leave the value uncommitted; it now runs the
  same commit before returning to the hub) — commits the whole value (second
  = 0) — `clock_set_time` (mktime with `tm_isdst=-1` so TZ/DST resolves,
  `settimeofday`, and the software alarm one-shot re-armed via the scheduler's
  reload; `validate_time` rejects years outside 2000–2099), then
  `clock_sntp_set_time_trusted(true)` (the unsynced dim lifts + the alarm fire
  gate opens) and `moon_ui_day_tick()` (the moon re-bakes when the calendar day
  changed). The home clock label then converges on the next 1.3 s poll. The set
  persists in the RTC domain (the crystal keeps it) and the NVS epoch backup
  re-snapshots it.
- **Settings displayed:** the wall clock, editable hour/minute and
  day/month/year (seconds are set to 0 on commit).

### 7.16 Timezone / UTC offset (S3 + P4)

![timezone / UTC offset](img/screens/settings_tz.png)

- **Why it exists:** both boards previously ran a fixed Kconfig timezone
  (`CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` = Europe/Berlin, DST-aware). This screen
  makes the zone a runtime choice, identical on the S3 and the P4 (unlike the
  manual time entry, §7.15, which is P4-reached) — **reached by the hub's globe
  icon (§7.6)**.
- **Layout:** a caption ("TIMEZONE / UTC OFFSET", 32 px, grey) over a single 32
  px (ssid font) roller, width `UI_PX(380)`, height `UI_PX(110)`, centred — the
  same roller look as the other settings value displays.
- **Option list** (`clock_tz.h`): all **53 fixed 30-minute UTC offsets**
  (UTC−12:00 … UTC+14:00, displayed as `UTC±HH:MM`) **plus Europe/Berlin** as
  the final entry — the Kconfig default, DST-aware. The stored selection
  defaults to Europe/Berlin (`CLOCK_TZ_BERLIN_IDX`).
- **Seed:** the roller seeds from `settings_timezone_idx()` on entry.
- **Commit:** releasing the roller applies the zone via `clock_tz_apply(idx)`,
  then persists it (`settings_set_timezone_idx` + `settings_store_save`).
  `clock_tz_apply` maps the index to a POSIX `TZ` string (the fixed offsets as
  `UTC±H[:M]` with the **west** sign — `UTC+2` means UTC+2 is spelled `UTC-2`,
  matching the Kconfig's `CET-1`; Europe/ Berlin as
  `CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`), `setenv("TZ", …); tzset()`, and re-arms the
  alarm arming (`clock_alarm_scheduler_reload` — the next fire's local
  time-of-day + weekday depends on the zone):
  - **P4** (system-clock time base, M5.x): the epoch is untouched; the local
    digits re-derive from the same epoch through the new zone.
  - **S3** (the PCF85063A stores LOCAL digits): the current local digits are
    read, converted to the UTC epoch under the _old_ zone (`mktime`, run before
    the env var changes), then the new-zone local digits for the same moment
    are written back (`clock_set_time`) — the epoch is consistent across the
    zone change.
- **Settings displayed:** the active timezone, selectable across every 30-
  minute UTC offset + Europe/Berlin.

## 8. Burn-in

The product runs an always-on AMOLED with a mostly-static disk; burn-in is a
_design requirement_, not an afterthought. The statements, in the order they
were made and implemented:

1. **The lit pixels must move, continuously, at rest as well as in use.** The
   free spin is the burn-in mechanism: while the device is in use it rotates at
   the active rate (default 300 s/turn); once it settles the rate eases to a
   **constant slow spin** (default 600 s/turn) that never stops — the
   phase-true coast it replaced (one turn per synodic month) was effectively
   invisible and read as the moon _freezing a minute before light sleep_. The
   continuous slow rotation keeps moving the lit pixels around the panel
   forever while the device sits on a table.
2. **The sleep state must not park the disk either.** The dusk is a
   _constant-projection pole spin_: the terminator (and the lit crescent's
   relief detail) travels the disk for the whole light-sleep duration (14-95 s
   at 1°/frame), and the dark-side frame the countdown lingers on still carries
   the **computed backlit surface** (the far-side terrain lit faintly from the
   anti-solar direction, §5.2 item 4) — a moving _pattern_ during the sleep, a
   faintly textured (not flat) disk while dark. (The earlier flat variants were
   both rejected: `dark_zero = 0` → 0x0000 left the far side invisible, and the
   constant `MOON_NIGHT_FLOOR = 10` overlay it replaced had no surface
   structure; the backlit model keeps the floor's level with the terrain
   added.)
3. **Orientation is stepped, never ramped.** The screen base orientation is
   applied in **90° steps** (int4-quantized IMU roll, 100 ms samples, 1 s
   windowed mean, sustained confirmation, instant apply on the 12 roots) — a
   continuous ramp would have parked the clock's pixels in intermediate
   positions; the steps put every pixel in one of four known poses, and the
   spin + dusk keep moving them between the settle periods.
4. **The screen-switch fade does not add a static element** — the panel's OWN
   hardware brightness steps the whole panel to/from black (the CO5300 0x51
   command, the same dimming the deep-sleep backlight off/on uses); no overlay
   is drawn, and while the fade ramp runs the spin holds its panel writes
   (`s_fade_busy`) — the 0x51 ramp is the only panel-io traffic in flight, so
   the moon's image freezes for the ~240 ms ramp (its angle keeps integrating,
   so it resumes from the exact pose).
5. **Residual risk, stated plainly:** the _clock digits_ are the only truly
   static elements (they move with the 90° steps and with the tilt-driven roll,
   but between rolls they sit still). At the AMOLED's always-on duty cycle the
   digits are the long-term burn-in candidate; the mitigation is the stepped
   re-orientation (a roll of the device re-poses them) plus the panel dim in
   light sleep (`UI_LIGHT_SLEEP_DIM_PCT`, the whole display — the clock's own
   `UI_CLOCK_ALPHA_PCT` default is 100, so the panel brightness carries the
   readability) and the clock hidden in deep sleep (backlight off).

## 10. Implementation notes

### 10.1 Fixed point & PSRAM

All per-pixel hot paths are fixed-point or table-driven (the spin's
int4-quantized sin/cos; the slope cache's packed uint16 cells; the 256-entry
tone LUT). The large buffers (s_frame, the 8-bit frame, the shade map, the 4 MB
slope cache) live in **PSRAM**; LVGL's allocator is the C-library backend (the
built-in 64 KB pool cannot hold a full-screen transformed layer — the original
tilt-crash). PSRAM is **not SPI-DMA-capable** on this board → every display
strip is staged through internal RAM (§4.3).

### 10.2 The atomic-flush invariant & its history

Every moon frame is one whole-panel `lv_refr_now` under `s_rgb_mtx`. History:
the first design used LVGL's `FADE_IN` screen-load — the fade's pending
invalidation re-invalidated the panel for 200 ms and rode along in the spin's
atomic full-frame flushes, producing the "nasty top-to-bottom redraw artifacts"
on wake. Fix: plain `lv_scr_load` + one atomic flush. The wake path
additionally froze the display ~1.7 s when the _synchronous_ WiFi reconnect
blocked the LVGL task — fixed with a background reconnect task and the screen
upgrade from the UI tick.

### 10.3 Tilt & orientation

- **Tilt drives the clock roll** (orbit off on the S3 — the ~1.7-2.4 s relief
  re-bake cannot serve the tilt cadence): `clock_roll_apply` measures in-plane
  roll (shortest-path EMA a=0.2), keeps a settled-pose reference (updated only
  while the tilt monitor reports settled), dead- zones 1°, and counter-rotates
  the clock containers via LVGL style transforms. Wake fires on **departure
  from the settled-pose EMA** (two bars + a 2-sample streak), not raw
  per-sample deltas — the fix for "wakes right after sleep".
- **Base orientation** (task #59/T1): +90° step offset applied to the 15 screen
  roots (all of `enum ScreensEnum` — the manual time entry §7.15 and the
  timezone screen §7.16 joined the 13 original roots in the 2026-11-04 fix:
  both had been missing from the transform list and read flipped 90° relative
  to every other settings screen); the 180°-flip reference re-tracks only on
  `step == 0` (T4). A rotated root's panel-sized layer (~0.4 MB at 466², ~1.0
  MB at the P4's 720²) is allocated via CLIB malloc (the 64 KB LVGL pool OOM
  was the original "off-screen + crash").
- **2 s press re-sync** (2026-10-30): the home-pose anchor latches from the
  first 1 s of IMU samples after boot; if the device was flipped while that
  window filled, the anchor is 180° off and the UI stays upside down — and the
  T4 rule (re-track only on step 0) means no tilt recovers it. A deliberate
  press of 2 s or more (`action_register_orientation_touch`, the indev
  PRESSED/RELEASED pair) re-anchors the reference to the pose held while
  pressing and restores the base orientation on the next sample (~100 ms). The
  press is the user's "this pose is the home pose".
- **The re-sync gates (2026-10-30, the "flipping unreliable" fix):** the
  un-gated request re-anchored home to _whatever_ pose was held at the end of
  any ≥2 s press — a roller drag in settings, a palm resting on the screen
  while the device was being flipped. Mid-flip, that adopted the new pose as
  home and cancelled the flip correction. The request is now actioned only when
  the 1 s filtered gravity has been stable (within 1 int4 level per 100 ms
  sample for 15 samples ≈ 1.5 s) **and**, once an anchor exists, sits on the
  anchor's home axis (within ~35° of upright or upside-down,
  `|dot|² ≥ 3|cross|²` on the integer quantized vectors). The boot anchor seed
  got the same stability gate, so a device still being placed at boot cannot
  latch a transient pose as home.

### 10.4 The screen switch: fade-to-black (replaced the concentric reveal)

`CONFIG_UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE` (int ms, default 240, 0 = plain atomic):
**every** screen switch (home ↔ settings including the sub-menu switches, and
to/from the alarm screen) dims the panel's OWN hardware brightness to black,
loads the new screen, and ramps the brightness back:

- **The dimming** is the CO5300's brightness command (`0x51`,
  `bsp_display_brightness_set`) — the same hardware dimming the deep-sleep
  backlight off/on uses. It scales everything on screen at once (the moon, the
  labels, the spin's direct panel writes) and costs one ~100 µs SPI param
  transaction per step. A fade step therefore writes **no pixels**: the
  transition costs nothing on the panel bus and shows no strip crawl.
- **Fade-out** (`moon_ui_fade_out`, in `loadScreen` _before_ `lv_scr_load`):
  sets `s_fade_busy` (the spin keeps integrating its angle but **skips its
  panel writes** — see the freeze fix below) and ramps the brightness 100 → 0
  in `FADE_STEPS` = 12 steps paced `UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE / 12` ms (12 small
  luminance steps stay smooth), each step under `s_panel_mtx`. The flag
  `s_fade_pending` is left set.
- **Fade-in** (`moon_ui_screen_switched`): if `s_fade_pending`, the loaded
  screen is displayed as ONE atomic whole-panel `lv_refr_now` under `s_rgb_mtx`
  **while the panel is still black** (invisible — the invariant's one atomic
  display, off the visible path; the per-strip panel lock comes from the flush
  wrapper itself), then the brightness ramps 0 → 100 (under `s_panel_mtx`) and
  the fully rendered new screen comes up at once. `s_fade_busy` clears, and the
  spin resumes its panel writes from the exact pose it was at.
- **No fade:** the one exception is the both-moon switch (airplane / WiFi / the
  sleep screens share the one moon image), which keeps the plain atomic
  `lv_scr_load` + one whole-panel flush — a fade there would only dim the moon,
  which is the same disk on both sides. (The settings sub-menu switches fade
  too: a fade leg is screen-agnostic — the fade-in's atomic flush works on any
  loaded screen, moon or not.)

Why it replaced the old concentric reveal (the center-out strip reorder,
`9dad4fe`): the reveal's visible failure mode was "white bars updating the
screen" (the strip crawl at the panel's QSPI rate) plus a rotated ghost —
`lv_snapshot_take` renders the screen in its _local_ coordinates, NOT through
the root's LVGL transform, so the center-out write showed unrotated content
until the trailing atomic flush fixed it (the rotation fix `5550a6d` and its
direction bug `9c96a12` — "90° CW" computed 90° CCW, painting the previous
screen as a mis-oriented full-panel ghost; the alarm screen, visited every 5
minutes by the then-active `*/5` debug rule, showed it). The fade has no strip
ordering, no snapshot-rotation coupling to the orientation pipeline, and no
intermediate frames that aren't simply "the screen, darker", so nothing a user
can see is ever a ghost or a bar.

**The overlay fade → the hardware ramp (2026-10-31):** the first fade
implementation composited a full-screen black overlay in LVGL and re-rendered
the whole 466×466 screen for each of its 4 steps (one atomic `lv_refr_now` per
step). That was still a _display-bound_ transition: every step charged ~175 ms
of QSPI strip traffic, and the panel's RAMWR fill sweeps each 25-row strip
left-to-right — the user saw each grey step "update left to right for about a
second". The fix uses the panel's own brightness command instead, so a fade
step writes no pixels at all: the ramp is free, and the panel traffic of the
whole switch is the ONE atomic flush of the new screen (which happens while the
panel is black and is invisible).

**The settings-entry freeze → serialization + watchdog (2026-10-31):** the
first device field test of the hardware ramp found that the home → settings
switch could freeze the device PERMANENTLY (white stripes stuck mid-draw). The
coredump (UART, decoded with GDB against the app ELF + ROM ELF) showed the
mechanism: `lvgl` and `moon_spin` both parked in
`spi_device_acquire_bus(portMAX_DELAY)` on the SAME GPSPI bus-lock semaphore,
and NO task held the bus inside the driver — the bus lock's background (REQ/
PENDING) bit was stuck. A QSPI strip DMA's completion was lost, so the lock's
FSM (`spi_bus_lock.c`: task-acquire vs background-queued ownership) routed
ownership to a background owner that would never release: every later
`acquire_bus` blocked forever with the panel mutex held, and the parked tasks
kept the idle tasks alive, so no WDT ever fired. lvgl was inside the fade's
`0x51` write; the spin inside a RAMWR strip. The fix, all app-side (no vendor
files touched):

- **Serialize the 0x51 writes on `s_panel_mtx`** — the fade's ramp steps and
  the backlight paths (wake, deep-sleep off/on, boot) all take the panel mutex
  around `bsp_display_brightness_set` (the boot/wake/deep-sleep call sites use
  the new `moon_ui_panel_brightness_set` wrapper for exactly this), so a
  brightness write is never queued while a strip DMA is in flight.
- **The spin yields the bus to the fade** — while `s_fade_busy` the spin keeps
  integrating its angle but skips `moon_spin_write_panel`; the 0x51 ramp is
  then the ONLY panel-io traffic in flight during the ~240 ms ramp (the user's
  original ask: stop the heavy panel work before the transition).
- **A backstop against the next lost completion** — a `panel_wdg` task (core 0,
  prio 3, 4 KB) sleeps 3 s at a time, then probes `s_panel_mtx` with a 3 s
  bound: if it is still held, the log says
  `PANEL IO STUCK: … the QSPI bus lock is stuck (a DMA completion was lost); restarting`
  and the device `esp_restart()`s — the silent dead screen becomes a logged,
  recoverable reboot. Legitimate `s_panel_mtx` holds are <100 ms (spin
  composite + strip write; LVGL flush wrapper per strip), so the 3 s bound has
  ~30× margin.

Verified on device: the deterministic repro (home → hub fade with the free spin
active) passes cleanly, repeatedly; 4 light-sleep/dusk/wake cycles, the
deep-sleep backlight off and the wake-from-deep-sleep backlight on (now
`moon_ui_panel_brightness_set`), and a full settings demo all clean — 0
`PANEL IO STUCK`, 0 WDT, 0 panics, 0 reboots across ~18 min of runtime.

### 10.5 Alarms, settings store, cron

- **Alarm scheduler**: cron-like rules (`*/N * * * *` intervals incl. N > 59
  via a total-minutes grid across the day with `mktime` date rollover;
  `M H * * <dow>` fixed times), written to `/spiffs/alarm.txt` and
  re-parsed+re-scheduled on every write (`clock_alarm_scheduler_ reload`; 0
  rules → `clock_clear_alarm()` disarms the PCF85063A's persistent ALM — a
  stale armed time would otherwise fire a phantom alarm screen on a 0-rule
  boot; on no-PCF builds (the P4) the guard is `clock_alarm_disarm_esp_timer()`
  - dropping the scheduler's `s_next_alarm` cache — esp_timer is not
    persistent, but the cache is). Firing is the 1.3 s RTC minute poll (on the
    P4: the one-shot's flag + the wall-clock backup check, gated on
    `clock_sntp_time_trusted()`).
- **Settings store** (`/spiffs/settings.txt`, `key = value`):
  `idle_timeout_sec`, `deep_sleep_countdown_sec`, `boot_anim_enable`,
  `dusk_anim_enable`, `timezone_idx` — `#ifndef`-seeded from Kconfig, live
  overrides (idle timeout applies immediately; countdown at the next arming;
  animation flags at the next boot/dusk; the timezone index is read at boot by
  the clock init — `settings_store_load` runs before `clock_init` — and written
  by the §7.16 picker).

### 10.6 Power flow

Airplane = modem sleep (WiFi deinit'd). On-demand sync: wake/manual/hourly arms
a background task (LVGL never blocks on the radio — the wake-freeze fix); the
hourly trigger fires at the minute-0 tick **only at rest on the airplane
screen** (no waking a sleeping device, no interfering with the boot sweep or a
settings session). Deep sleep turns the backlight off; the RTC alarm (if any)
fires from there.

P4: `0x1819a0` = 1,579,424 B in the 9,437,184 B partition (7,857,760 B free — the net −456 B widget deletion is inside the linker's alignment slack)                                                                                                                           |

**Board performance indicators (S3 vs P4).** The table above is the extensible
anchor: whenever a stage is re-measured on either board, the row grows (board +
date named in the value, never a bare overwrite of the other board's number).
The standing invariants that shape the numbers: the S3's PSRAM is **not**
SPI-DMA-capable (flush strips stage through internal RAM — the 32 KiB S3
SPI-DMA cap, flush queue depth 1, buffer height 25) while the P4's PSRAM **is**
DMA-capable (the DPI FIFO runs PSRAM-backed; the spin's 10×65-row DSI strips
exist only because a 206-row strip underruns the FIFO at X16+XIP). The S3 panel
path is the QSPI CO5300 (one continuous 400×400 window write for the spin,
max*transfer_sz 23,300 B); the P4 panel path is the MIPI-DSI JD9365 (10×65-row
strips, one framebuffer, NONE tear mode). The S3 bakes at 240 px intermediates
/ 400 px final; the P4 at 240 px intermediates / **650 px** final (~595–599 ms,
the 720 px disk). The S3 keeps the PCF85063A RTC; the P4 runs the M5.1 software
clock (the 1.3 s poll + `esp_timer` one-shots). Both boards share the moon core
verbatim (`components/moon/core`), so the \_computation* is identical — the
difference is the panel, the DMA topology, and the disk size.

## 12. Test system (with the NASA reference files)

The product's physical-correctness claim is gated, not asserted:

### 12.1 The image gate — `host_sim/check_gate.py`

Full path: `host_sim/check_gate.py`. Run:
`host_sim/.venv/bin/python host_sim/check_gate.py [--sim host_sim/build/moon_sim] [--out /tmp/moon-sim-gate]`.

Two diffs over the 32-frame gate set, both at 5-bit panel fidelity (the
device's exact gray→RGB565 quantization):

1. **C vs NASA** — the runtime path (eraEpv00+eraMoon98 ephemeris, fixed-point
   rotation, gray→RGB565) against the **NASA SVS 5415** reference frames. Gate:
   per-frame MAE ≤ 12 (the prototype's metric); mean content SSIM reported.
2. **C vs Python** — porting fidelity against the validated Python prototype
   (float astropy ephemeris, the same banded relief-DEM lighting, 5-bit
   quantized). Gate: per-frame MAE ≤ 2. Both renders are pixel-aligned
   (identical disk geometry), so the diff is direct.

If check 2 passes, check 1 inherits the prototype's NASA agreement — the
residual is exactly the porting error.

**NASA reference files** (full paths, working tree; the set is 8,760 frames of
the SVS 5415 400x400 lunar image series, gitignored):

- `assets/images/moon/final_400x400/moon.0001.png` … `moon.8760.png` — the
  complete reference series (32 frames selected by
  `moon.validate.select_frames` for the gate, spread across phases).
- `docs/img/nasa/nasa_00000.png`, `nasa_02190.png`, `nasa_04380.png`,
  `nasa_06570.png`, `nasa_08759.png` — 5 committed samples (beginning / 25 % /
  50 % / 75 % / end of the series) so the hosted document shows the references
  the gate runs against.
- `assets/images/moon/moon/` — the Python prototype package (`astro.py`
  geometry, `renderer.py`, `textures.py`, `metrics.py`, `register.py`,
  `validate.py`, `constants.py`, `assets.py` — LROC/LOLA download + the
  `moon.assets` generator, `calibrate.py`, `animation.py`), and
  `assets/images/moon/moon_assets_gen.c` + `moon_assets.bin` — the generated
  device assets.

### 12.2 The host simulators

- `host_sim/main.c` (`moon_sim`) — the **exact device core** built for the
  host; writes PNGs at the real panel size (`--size 466` device / `--size 400`
  gate geometry; `--rot`, `--pole` (a 1:1 copy of the device's dusk spin),
  `--darkzero` (the device's computed backlit night side), `--neutral` (the
  neutral gray→565 LUT — the default is the display's warm tint, §5.2 item 7),
  `--list`/`--frames` batch modes). This is also the film renderer
  (`docs/gen_media.py`).
- `host_sim/pole_test.c` — the dusk geometry proof (ad-hoc build, not a CMake
  target): right-sign fold beats wrong-sign 2.5×; φ\* analytic == grid minimum
  to 1e-5; the dark-side frame keeps contrast; map-once vs per-frame re-bake
  spatial MAE with the no-flicker proof (temporal frame-delta within 0.02-0.14
  gray); and the **backlit night-side section** (the device's `dark_zero = 1`
  path): per epoch, the shade map (backlit night side + `dk_sup + margin`)
  re-projected through a fold must match the pixel-exact backlit bake to
  cell-center sampling (MAE < 7, endpoint folds at ~0.2–0.5), with zero lit
  pixels and > 50% backlit pixels at the endpoint — the no-pop proof for the
  computed dark side.
- `host_sim/uisim/` — the **real device `screens.c`** (unmodified) on host LVGL
  9.6 (SW renderer, RGB565, 466x466 by default, ESP stubs) → per-screen PNG
  snapshots (`build.sh run`); `build.sh run --panel 720` renders the P4's
  720x720 panel (its own `build-720/` dir, the 650 px moon disk, the panel-
  scaled UI + the `fonts_p4/` font set — the font dir and `-DPANEL_SIZE` both
  follow the `--panel` arg, mirroring the device's `CONFIG_BOARD_P4` switch) —
  the source of every screenshot in §7 (the P4 set under
  `docs/img/screens/p4/`). Two diagnostic probes from the reveal era
  (2026-10-30), kept as the verification record: `--rottest` proves
  `lv_snapshot_take` renders in the screen's **local** coordinates (the root's
  LVGL rotation is ignored — the fact the spin's UI keep-mask now relies on:
  the snapshot is rotated by the panel step in-place before it masks);
  `--reveal <q> [screen]` runs the former concentric-reveal permutation (copied
  verbatim into `main.c`) against the real rotated `lv_refr_now` flush and
  dumped the raw pre-rotation snapshot (`out/snap_raw_qN.png`) that exposed its
  direction bug.
- `host_sim/render_demo.py` — the README montages (PIL + `moon_sim` only).
- Venvs: `host_sim/.venv` (astropy, scikit-image, imagecodecs, numpy, PIL) and
  `assets/images/moon/.venv` — both gitignored; recreate with `uv venv` +
  `uv pip install`.

### 12.3 Device verification

Headless captures drive the state machine through the **Kconfig test hooks**
(all default off, §14.3):

- `TEST_SETTINGS_DEMO_SEC` — the scripted settings run (hub → pomodoro (90 min,
  the cron N>59 sanity) → alarm-time (12:35 Mon-Fri, the range-arc default) →
  light-sleep (store writes) → airplane, reading both SPIFFS files back); the
  settings stack's acceptance path, and the exercise of every screen switch
  (hence of the fade-to-black switch).
- `TEST_AUTO_WAKE_SEC` — fires the idle-wake transition after N s of sleep (the
  wake path: WiFi reconnect, screen switch, moon re-bake).
- `TEST_ROLL_TILT_SEC` — scripted tilt-roll steps (the orientation pipeline).
- `TEST_CPU_STATS_SEC` — idle-CPU stats loop (the 73-91 % root-cause probe;
  caveat: its idle-reset forces the ACTIVE spin, and its 1 s wait counts
  lv_timer ticks, ~510 s real).
- `TEST_BAKE_NO_RELIEF` — relief-free bakes (the PSRAM-load-latency floor A/B:
  bake ~1.3 s with relief vs ~0.95 s without).
- `TEST_SPIN_BANDS` — the spin's seam diagnostic (the direct panel write; one
  distinct gray level per strip, so a glitch at a strip seam — a stray line, a
  shifted boundary, a row that does not land — shows on a clean pattern with no
  moon texture or keep-mask to confound it; the write path is unchanged, only
  the content). `1` = the MOON_PX² moon area as horizontal bands written with
  the normal spin geometry (400-wide strips at x=33 on the S3). `2` = the same
  band pattern written as full-panel-width strips (x=0..465, the LVGL flush
  geometry) — the A/B that isolates the 400-wide strip window as the seam-line
  cause (the black edge margins cover the arc-ring slivers for the duration of
  the test). 0 (default) = the normal moon.
- `TEST_WIFI_SCAN_SEC` — opens the settings WiFi screen N s after boot (waiting
  out the boot sweep and disabling idle monitoring), then holds while the
  background scan completes — the headless scan-path check for the remote-C6
  board (the `esp_hosted` RPC scan through the C6, including 5 GHz APs).
- `TEST_ALARM_RING_SEC` — fires the real alarm path (the ring start + alarm
  screen) N s after the boot sweep, then drives the full ring lifecycle: stop
  (the touch-dismiss fade + codec close), re-fire (the codec re-open), and a
  final real dismiss — the headless check of the P4 ES8311
  open/stream/ramp/fade/close/re-open cycle (the speaker is audible). On the S3
  the ring functions are no-op stubs, so it exercises the alarm-screen path
  only.

Plus serial capture (pyserial 115200) of the boot/sleep/wake/alarm cycles (0
WDT/panic/NO_MEM is the pass criterion), and the **user visual pass** on the
physical device for the things only a human can judge (the fade-to-black
switch's smoothness, the day-range-arc handle gestures, the roller feel).

### 12.4 How the moon looks vs NASA — the committed side-by-side figures

The gate (§12.1) measures the agreement; these figures _show_ it. Four
committed figures — `docs/img/nasa/nasa_vs_c_p025.png`, `nasa_vs_c_p050.png`,
`nasa_vs_c_p075.png`, `nasa_vs_c_p090.png` — each lay out one gate frame as
three equal 400×400 panels:

|                                          |                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| ![phase 25](img/nasa/nasa_vs_c_p025.png) | ![phase 50](img/nasa/nasa_vs_c_p050.png) |
| ![phase 75](img/nasa/nasa_vs_c_p075.png) | ![phase 90](img/nasa/nasa_vs_c_p090.png) |

Every figure: **NASA SVS 5415 reference** (left) · **C runtime, 5-bit RGB565**
(middle) · **residual ×8** (right). The residual panel is computed with the
same sub-pixel registration (phase cross-correlation,
`moon. register.register_shift`) the gate uses for its MAE, so the picture is
the measured residual, not a naive pixel diff.

Reading the residual: the error concentrates exactly where a real moon render
is hard — **along the terminator** (the day/night boundary is a few-pixel-wide
feature and the two renderers' ephemeris precision differs at the sub-pixel
level there), **at the disk rim** (the disk mask edge), and **in the relief
texture of the lit half** (crater walls are where the banded DEM approximation
deviates from the full-resolution reference). The night side is the darkest
part of the residual — the computed backlit side (§5.2 item 4) is the least
constrained by the reference. **The gate validates the physics, not the display
tint**: `check_gate.py` runs the simulator with `--neutral`
(`moon_gray565_set_warm(0)`) and the dark_zero = 0 earthshine path, so the
artistic pass (§5.2 items 4–5, 7 — the K = 0.20 backlit level, the soft
terminator, the warm RGB565 LUT) is invisible to its metrics. The 2026-11-02
art-pass run is therefore byte-identical to the pre-pass run: per-frame MAE
4.90–8.90 (max 8.90 ≤ the 12 gate), content SSIM 0.838–0.951 (mean 0.908),
C–Python MAE 1.03 (max 1.31 ≤ 2) — **PASS**.

Regenerate: `host_sim/.venv/bin/python host_sim/check_gate.py` (fresh 32-frame
output in `/tmp/moon-sim-gate/`) then
`host_sim/.venv/bin/python docs/nasa_figs.py` (the committed figures; the PICKS
table pins the same gate frames). A new gate run with a different `mooninfo`
selection shifts the frame numbers — update `PICKS` to the new gate set's
positions.
