## 13. ESP32-S3: capabilities & limits

What this project uses, and what the chip/board would not do:

**Used to the edge**

| Capability                          | Use                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 240 MHz dual-core Xtensa            | core 0 = UI/display (LVGL adapter, pinned); core 1 = moon bakes + spin render (bounded, self-cancelling — the core-1 WDT idle check is disabled for it, core 0's stays as the hang net) |
| 8 MB octal PSRAM @ 80 MHz           | frame buffers, shade map, the 4 MB slope cache, LVGL layers (CLIB malloc backend → PSRAM); **not** DMA-accessible                                                                       |
| 16 MB flash                         | 2048 K app (the factory was widened 1392 K → 2048 K when the app outgrew the old ceiling — currently 646,752 B free) + 64 K SPIFFS + 2560 K assets                                      |
| QSPI @ high pclk + 16-bit QSPI data | the 466x466x2 B full-panel flush in ~175 ms (display-bound, not CPU-bound)                                                                                                              |
| FreeRTOS (100 Hz)                   | the 10 ms UI tick, the bounded bake tasks, the background sync task                                                                                                                     |
| SNTP + WiFi (on demand)             | the airplane-modem-sleep power model; the hourly 1-minute sync                                                                                                                          |

**Hard limits the design works around**

| Limit                                              | Consequence in this project                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PSRAM is not SPI-DMA-capable (below `SOC_DMA_LOW`) | every display strip is staged into internal RAM; the S3 SPI DMA transaction cap is **32 KiB** → `buffer_height` 25 (23.3 KiB) + flush queue depth 1; a 50-row strip (46.6 KiB) → `ESP_ERR_NO_MEM` on every full-panel flush (the vendored BSP fix)                                                                               |
| 2048 K app partition (widened from 1392 K)         | the flash budget is a standing constraint (current: 646,752 B free); the widening was forced by the app outgrowing 1,425,408 B and is what houses the circular wheel keyboard (the widened SSID font + the screen + the save→connect flow)                                                                                       |
| LVGL 8 KB task stack                               | whole-panel `lv_refr_now` overflows the 3.5 KB main task at boot → the atomic flush must run on the LVGL task                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 64 KiB built-in LVGL pool                          | a full-screen transformed layer (~0.9 MB) OOMs it → CLIB malloc (PSRAM); the original tilt crash                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Core-1 CPU starvation by long bakes                | the core-1 WDT idle-task check is off (bakes are bounded; core 0's check stays)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| No GPU / no hardware 2-D                           | the spin is a CPU fixed-point gather (~8 ms) + a direct panel write; the SW renderer owns everything else; the display, not the CPU, is the bottleneck (~175 ms/frame); LVGL's glTF 3D extension is unusable on this chip (and on the P4) for the same reason — investigated 2026-10-30, see `docs/research/gltf-feasibility.md` |
| FreeRTOS 100 Hz                                    | a 1 ms `vTaskDelay` floor is 0 ticks → the adapter's 1 ms minimum-delay made the LVGL task spin at ~3500 Hz (73-91 % of core 0) — the BSP `task_min_delay_ms = 10` fix (7-9 % now)                                                                                                                                               |
| RTC INT not wired to a GPIO                        | all RTC-driven behavior is software-polled (1.3 s); the PCF85063A ALM persists across boots → the 0-rule disarm                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| AMOLED burn-in                                     | the design-level constraint of §8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

**Not used (and why):** the ES8311 audio (no product need), PPA acceleration
(off — the spin's keep-mask snapshot is a SW render), LVGL themes other than
the custom grey/white, LVGL's built-in allocator, RTC interrupts, deep-sleep
modem (the modem sleeps; the MCU stays up — a true deep sleep would lose the
display and the spin's pose, which the wake path needs to resume seamlessly).

## 14. Configuration reference

### 14.1 The build defaults (three files; `sdkconfig` is gitignored)

The defaults are split shared / per-target — for each defaults file the build
also appends the `<file>.<idf_target>` variant if it exists (later file wins):

- **`sdkconfig.defaults`** (shared): target esp32s3, 16 MB flash, `SPIRAM=y`,
  the UI Kconfig block (`CONFIG_UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE=240`, the spin periods /
  fps), the LVGL block (`CONFIG_LV_USE_CLIB_MALLOC=y` — PSRAM layers,
  `CONFIG_LV_COLOR_DEPTH_16=y`, `CONFIG_LV_USE_SNAPSHOT=y` — the spin's UI
  keep-mask, `CONFIG_LV_USE_SYSMON=n` / `CONFIG_LV_USE_PERF_MONITOR=n` — dead
  weight removed for flash, `CONFIG_LV_USE_ROLLER=y`), the codecs-off block,
  `CONFIG_IO_EXPANDER_ENABLE_GPIO_API_WRAPPER=n`.
- **`sdkconfig.defaults.esp32s3`** (S3-only, moved out of the shared file):
  octal PSRAM 80 MHz, 240 MHz, `CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK_CPU1=n`
  (the bounded core-1 bakes — §13), `CONFIG_BSP_LCD_TRANS_QUEUE_DEPTH=1` (the
  32 KiB SPI-DMA strip staging — §13).
- **`sdkconfig.defaults.esp32p4`** (P4-only): `CONFIG_IDF_TARGET="esp32p4"`,
  `CONFIG_BOARD_P4=y` (the `BOARD` Kconfig choice, §15), `ESP32P4_REV_MIN_100`
  (rev v1.3 — no `REV_MIN_300`/`SELECTS_REV_LESS_V3` in IDF 5.5.1),
  `CONFIG_IDF_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES=y` + `SPIRAM_SPEED_200M` (200 MHz PSRAM —
  gated: without the experimental flag it silently falls back to 20 MHz and the
  DSI underruns), L2 cache 256 KB / 128 B line, 10 KB main task stack, 1000 Hz
  tick, `CONFIG_BSP_LCD_TYPE_720_720_4_INCH=y`. (No esp_hosted / SDIO-pins
  block yet — that lands with the P4 Wi-Fi milestone.)

The `BOARD` choice itself (`BOARD_S3` default / `BOARD_P4`) lives in
`components/board/Kconfig.projbuild` — a root `Kconfig.projbuild` is **not**
processed by ESP-IDF 5.5 (only per-component `Kconfig`/`Kconfig.projbuild`
files are globbed), so the choice sits in the always-built board-shim
component. The root `CMakeLists.txt` `FATAL_ERROR`s if `IDF_TARGET` and the
`BOARD` choice disagree.

### 14.2 UI component (`components/ui/Kconfig`)

| Option                                                                        | Default         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_ENABLE`                                                  | y               | the boot synodic sweep (336 frames); `#ifndef` fallback in `moon_ui.c` re-enables it if the symbol is undefined — disable by _setting 0_                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_FRAMES`                                                  | 336             | sweep length                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_BAKE_PX`                                                 | 240             | sweep bake resolution (the reduced-res fast path)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_ON_WAKE`                                                 | n               | (obsolete test hook — the sweep is boot-only)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_DUSK_ENABLE`                                                  | y               | the light-sleep pole spin (constant projection)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_SPIN_ENABLE`                                                  | y               | the free spin (direct panel write via the wrapped `esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap`; paused while the orbit re-bake, the boot sweep, or the dusk owns the buffer — the screen-switch fade also holds the spin's panel writes (`s_fade_busy`, the angle keeps integrating) so the 0x51 ramp is the only panel-io traffic in flight, §10.4) |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_SPIN_PERIOD_S`                                                | 300             | active spin: seconds per full turn while in use (range 30-7200)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_SPIN_SETTLED_PERIOD_S`                                        | 600             | settled spin: seconds per full turn at rest (range 60-7200) — the constant slow burn-in spin (the phase-true coast it read as a freeze)                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_SPIN_FPS`                                                     | 8               | spin frame rate: gathered + panel-written frames per second (range 2-30)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_SPIN_SETTLE_S`                                                | 10              | activity→settled-spin window                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ORBIT_ENABLE`                                                 | n               | tilt-driven viewport orbit (off on the S3 — the relief re-bake cadence doesn't fit; retry on the P4). Kconfig-`n` leaves the macro UNDEFINED — the `#ifndef` fallback in `moon_ui.c` is `#define 0`                                                                                                                                 |
| `CONFIG_UI_MOON_ORBIT_MAX_DEG` / `_STEP_DEG` / `_DEADZONE_DEG` / `_LPF_ALPHA` | 30 / 1 / 2 / 30 | orbit viewport bounds, step, dead zone, low-pass %                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `CONFIG_UI_DEEP_SLEEP_COUNTDOWN_SEC`                                          | 60              | deep-sleep countdown (runtime-overridable)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `CONFIG_UI_LIGHT_SLEEP_DIM_PCT`                                               | 25              | the panel's hardware brightness in light sleep (%): the entry ramps DOWN to it and the wake / an alarm ring ramp back to 100, paced like the fade (§7.3, `moon_ui_panel_dim_ramp`)                                                                                                                                                  |
| `CONFIG_UI_CLOCK_ALPHA_PCT`                                                   | 100             | the shared clock widget's opacity in light sleep (%): the entry sets the clock container to this (the panel dim above carries the readability; lower it to dim the clock further relative to the moon), the wake restores 100 (§7.3; Kconfig-`n` leaves the macro UNDEFINED — the `#ifndef` fallback in `actions.c` is 100)         |
| `CONFIG_UI_LIGHT_SLEEP_TICK_MS`                                               | 100             | LVGL tick cadence in light sleep                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `CONFIG_UI_IMU_ENABLE`                                                        | y               | QMI8658C tilt (drive the clock roll + activity)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `CONFIG_UI_IMU_ACTIVITY_DEG` / `_WAKE_DEG`                                    | 5 / 20          | activity bar / wake bar (departure-from-settled model)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `CONFIG_UI_IMU_ANGLE_SIGN` / `_ROLL_OFFSET_DEG`                               | 1 / 0           | sign/offset calibration for the mount                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `CONFIG_UI_CLOCK_ROLL_SIGN`                                                   | 1               | flips the tilt→clock-roll sign for a mirrored mount                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CONFIG_UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE`                                                | 240             | the fade-to-black screen switch (ms per leg; 0 = the plain atomic switch)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### 14.3 Clock component (`components/clock/Kconfig`)

| Option                          | Default                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A`           | `y` (n in the P4 defaults)     | the PCF85063A hardware path (S3). `n` (the P4) = the M5.1 software clock: system-clock time base + software minute tick + `esp_timer` countdown/alarm one-shots (§2.3); `n` leaves the macro UNDEFINED — the code gates on `#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A` |
| `CLOCK_TIME_FORMAT`             | 24H                            | display format (the RTC stores 24 h)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`        | `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0/2,M10.5.0/3` | POSIX TZ                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `CLOCK_NTP_SERVER`              | `pool.ntp.org`                 | SNTP server                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CLOCK_NTP_SYNC_INTERVAL_HOURS` | 1                              | the on-demand sync interval                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CLOCK_NTP_TIMEOUT_MS`          | 10000                          | SNTP timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC`        | 60                             | idle → light sleep (runtime-overridable)                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Test hooks (all default off, §12.3): `TEST_SETTINGS_DEMO_SEC`,
`TEST_AUTO_WAKE_SEC`, `TEST_ROLL_TILT_SEC`, `TEST_CPU_STATS_SEC`,
`TEST_BAKE_NO_RELIEF`, `TEST_WIFI_SCAN_SEC`, `TEST_SPIN_BANDS`,
`TEST_ALARM_RING_SEC`.

### 14.4 Runtime settings store (`/spiffs/settings.txt`)

`key = value` lines (the live overrides; absent keys fall back to the
Kconfig-seeded defaults; written by the settings screens, read at boot):

```
idle_timeout_sec = 60
deep_sleep_countdown_sec = 60
boot_anim_enable = 1
dusk_anim_enable = 1
```

`/spiffs/alarm.txt` (the cron rules, one per line, `#` comments): `*/N * * * *`
(interval, N ≤ 1440) and `M H * * <dow>` (dow = comma list / `*` = all days;
bit 0 = Sunday). `/spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt` (two lines, gitignored). A full
`idf.py flash` re-bakes the SPIFFS partition from the tree — runtime edits are
lost on flash (the tree keeps the `spiffs/alarm.txt` default — 7:00 Mon–Fri;
`spiffs/settings.txt` must NOT be in the tree — it is runtime-owned).

## 15. Project structure

```
CMakeLists.txt               IDF project (managed_components, the target-select:
                             partitions.csv vs partitions_p4.csv, EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS
                             + the per-target dependencies lock for the P4)
dependencies.lock            pinned managed components (S3; the P4 build uses the
                             gitignored dependencies.lock.p4 — different BSP + stacks)
partitions.csv               16 MB layout (§3.1)
partitions_p4.csv            32 MB P4 layout (§3.2)
sdkconfig.defaults           the shared build defaults (sdkconfig is gitignored)
sdkconfig.defaults.esp32s3   the S3-only defaults (octal PSRAM 80 M, 240 MHz, WDT,
sdkconfig.defaults.esp32p4     flush queue depth 1) + the P4 defaults (BOARD_P4,
                               rev1_3, 200 MHz PSRAM, 720×720 LCD type)
README.md                    the front page (build/hardware/demo/timings)
CLAUDE.md                    this project's agent instructions (the docs rule)
main/
  main.cpp                   app_main: boot sync -> display -> UI; test hooks
components/
  board/                     the board shim: board_display.{c,h} (the panel handle,
    Kconfig.projbuild          the S3-only IO expander) + the BOARD Kconfig choice
  moon/                      the portable core (§5): astro/bake/fixp/render + ERFA
    include/moon.h           the public API (geometry/bake/reproject/rotate)
    include/moon_consts.h    generated single source of truth (pole, DEM, earthshine, tone LUT)
    include/moon_assets.h    the asset partition access
  clock/                     RTC/minute/idle/sntp/alarm-scheduler/settings-store
  ui/                        the LVGL UI: screens.c (15 screens) + moon_ui.c
    (the pipeline) + actions.c (flow) + styles.c (the theme) + fonts/ (generated)
  imu/                       QMI8658C driver
  wifi/                      scan (settings)
  esp32_s3_touch_amoled_1_75/  the S3 BSP (CO5300 QSPI + CST9217 + TCA9554 +
                               brightness); the P4 uses the registry
                               waveshare/esp32_p4_wifi6_touch_lcd_xc 3.0.1
host_sim/                    moon_sim + check_gate.py + pole_test.c + uisim/ + render_demo.py
assets/                      LROC/LOLA sources, the Python prototype, the 8,760
                             NASA SVS 5415 frames, the generated device assets
spiffs/                      wifi_credentials.example.txt + alarm.txt (the 7:00 Mon-Fri default)
docs/                        this document + the media (§1) + the Sphinx book
                             (book/, a 25-chapter furo build — figures, the
                             uisim screenshots, the device composites, the
                             client-side mermaid diagrams, the Moon Lab sim)
                             + the interactive keyboard lab
                             (keyboard/round-keyboard-lab.html, §7.14)
                             + the NASA figure script (nasa_figs.py, §12.4)
                             + the research notes (research/)
```

Line counts (tracked, 2026-10-31): moon core ~5,400; ui ~10,100 (incl. the
generated font subsets ~4,100); clock ~3,100; host_sim ~3,500; BSP ~1,200;
board shim ~115; main ~450; wifi ~430; imu ~410 — **~26,400 lines** of tracked
code.

````markdown
# Moon Phase Clock — project instructions

Physically correct moon-phase clock, dual-board: the Waveshare ESP32-S3 Touch
AMOLED 1.75 (466x466 RGB565 CO5300 QSPI panel, CST9217 touch, QMI8658C IMU,
PCF85063A RTC behind a TCA9554, 16 MB flash + octal PSRAM) and the Waveshare
ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-XC "4C" (720x720 round IPS, JD9365 MIPI-DSI, GT911
touch, remote C6 Wi-Fi over SDIO, 32 MB flash + PSRAM; board plumbing in,
Wi-Fi/moon-scale/UI-upscale/clock path in progress). ESP-IDF 5.5.1, LVGL 9.6.
The portable moon core (`components/moon/core`) is shared verbatim with the
host simulator (`host_sim/`).

## Standing rule: keep the documentation current

**After every change to the project** (code, Kconfig, screens, timings,
hardware facts, test system, build steps) **update the project documentation**
— do not let `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` drift:

1. The prose lives in `docs/doc_template.md`. Fix any statement the change
   invalidated (timings, sizes, options, flow, limits) there.
2. The complete source code is embedded in the generated
   `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` by `docs/gen_doc.py` — **regenerate it**:
   `python3 docs/gen_doc.py` (embeds every tracked source file verbatim, plus
   the docs/ inventory and this CLAUDE.md). Commit template, generator output,
   and the code change together.
3. If the change adds/reworks a screen, regenerate the screenshots:
   `host_sim/uisim/build.sh run` and copy `host_sim/uisim/out/*.png` into
   `docs/img/screens/`. New animations: `python3 docs/gen_media.py` (needs
   `host_sim/.venv`, PIL, ffmpeg).
4. If the change touches the moon bake path, the host image gate must pass
   before the doc's numbers are trustworthy:
   `host_sim/.venv/bin/python host_sim/check_gate.py`.

## Hard invariants (violations ship visible bugs)

- Every moon-pipeline frame hits the panel as ONE atomic whole-panel
  `lv_refr_now` under `s_rgb_mtx` (`moon_ui_screen_switched`). Two sanctioned
  exceptions: the fade-to-black screen switch (`UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE`, a
  hardware panel-brightness ramp that writes no pixels — the new screen's one
  atomic flush runs while the panel is still black) and the burn-in spin's
  direct panel write (wrapped `esp_lcd_panel_draw_bitmap`, the render task owns
  the panel for that frame under `s_panel_mtx`).
- `spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt` and `sdkconfig` are gitignored — never commit
  either; `spiffs/` edits are separate `spiffs:` commits.
- The 16 MB board's PSRAM is NOT SPI-DMA-capable: display flush strips are
  staged through internal RAM; keep the BSP `buffer_height` at 25 and the flush
  queue depth at 1 (32 KiB S3 SPI DMA cap).
- Flash budget: S3 `factory` partition 2,097,152 B (2048 K — widened from the
  old 1392 K / 1,425,408 B ceiling when the app outgrew it); P4 `factory` 9216
  K (`partitions_p4.csv`, 32 MB chip — the binary header stays 16 MB, so
  esptool's size-mismatch warning is expected); check the binary size after
  every build.
- Kconfig `n` leaves the macro UNDEFINED — all runtime values go through
  `#ifndef`-seeded getters, never `#define` redefinitions of the Kconfig
  macros.
- `managed_components/` is gitignored — depend on its public API only, never on
  modified vendor files.

## Commands

```bash
source ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
# S3 (466) — the default target; the S3 board is /dev/ttyACM0
idf.py build && idf.py flash -p /dev/ttyACM0
# P4 4C (720) — the Kconfig BOARD choice comes from
# sdkconfig.defaults.esp32p4 (CONFIG_BOARD_P4=y); own build dir + own
# dependencies.lock.p4 (gitignored); the P4 board is /dev/ttyACM1
idf.py -D IDF_TARGET=esp32p4 -B build/p4 build
idf.py -D IDF_TARGET=esp32p4 -B build/p4 flash -p /dev/ttyACM1
python3 docs/gen_doc.py                        # regenerate docs/DOCUMENTATION.md
host_sim/.venv/bin/python host_sim/check_gate.py   # moon image gate (NASA refs)
host_sim/uisim/build.sh run                    # real screens -> PNG snapshots
python3 docs/gen_media.py                      # docs videos (moon_sim frames)
```

Defaults are the 3-file split (`sdkconfig.defaults` shared +
`sdkconfig.defaults.esp32s3` / `sdkconfig.defaults.esp32p4` per-target — the
per-target file is auto-appended when it exists, later file wins).
`idf.py save-defconfig` writes the _shared_ file only — with this split it
would clobber the board-specific lines, so keep the three files hand-curated (a
stray board line in the wrong file is caught by the root CMakeLists'
target/board `FATAL_ERROR`).

zsh: quote globs (`--include='*.c'`). Pre-commit runs clang-format on C/H only
— **never run clang-format on Kconfig/other extensionless files** (it mangles
them; the hook's own filter keeps it safe).
````

### `CMakeLists.txt`

```ini
# The following five lines of boilerplate have to be in your project's
# CMakeLists in this exact order for cmake to work correctly
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)

include($ENV{IDF_PATH}/tools/cmake/project.cmake)

# P4 target block. (The partition table is NOT set here: the partition_table
# component's project hook re-derives PARTITION_CSV_PATH from the Kconfig
# values, so a plain set() before project() is clobbered. The selection
# lives in the per-target defaults files instead — the shared
# sdkconfig.defaults sets CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM=y, and
# sdkconfig.defaults.esp32p4 sets
# CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM_FILENAME="partitions_p4.csv" (32 MB layout,
# 9216K factory); the S3 keeps the default "partitions.csv".)
if(IDF_TARGET STREQUAL "esp32p4")
    # The vendored S3 BSP is S3-only (its manifest declares
    # targets: [esp32s3]); EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS keeps it out of the P4
    # build AND of the component manager's local-manifest list (which
    # would otherwise FATAL_ERROR on the target mismatch).
    set(EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS "esp32_s3_touch_amoled_1_75")
    # The component manager rewrites its dependencies lock on every
    # configure and the two targets resolve DIFFERENT dependency sets
    # (different BSPs + driver stacks), so the P4 build uses its own
    # lock file (dependencies.lock.p4, gitignored) and never touches the
    # tracked S3 dependencies.lock. The property must be set before
    # project(), which runs the component manager.
    idf_build_set_property(DEPENDENCIES_LOCK
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/dependencies.lock.p4")
endif()

project(moon-phase)

# Target/board mismatch guard (risk: a stray CONFIG_BOARD_P4=y in an S3
# build, or vice versa, would resolve two BSPs / the wrong partition
# table and fail obscurely deep in the build).
if((IDF_TARGET STREQUAL "esp32p4" AND NOT CONFIG_BOARD_P4) OR
        (IDF_TARGET STREQUAL "esp32s3" AND NOT CONFIG_BOARD_S3))
    message(FATAL_ERROR "Board mismatch: IDF_TARGET=${IDF_TARGET} (CONFIG_BOARD_S3='${CONFIG_BOARD_S3}', "
        "CONFIG_BOARD_P4='${CONFIG_BOARD_P4}'). Pass the matching -D IDF_TARGET / "
        "sdkconfig.defaults.<target> so the build target and the Kconfig BOARD choice agree.")
endif()

# Automatically include SPIFFS data from spiffs/ folder
spiffs_create_partition_image(storage spiffs FLASH_IN_PROJECT)

# Moon phase assets: flash the combined equirect albedo + relief DEM blob
# into the moon_assets data partition (subtype "undefined" = plain raw
# binary region; read at boot via esp_partition_read). The blob is
# generated by the asset pipeline (local-only, gitignored):
#   cd assets/images/moon && python -m moon.assets
# It emits moon_assets.bin (albedo MOON_ALB_W x MOON_ALB_H u8 at 0, then
# relief DEM MOON_DEM_W x MOON_DEM_H int8).
set(MOON_ASSETS_BIN ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/images/moon/moon_assets.bin)
if(EXISTS ${MOON_ASSETS_BIN})
    esptool_py_flash_to_partition(flash "moon_assets" ${MOON_ASSETS_BIN})
else()
    message(WARNING "moon assets not found at ${MOON_ASSETS_BIN} -- "
        "run 'cd assets/images/moon && python -m moon.assets' to generate them "
        "(the build succeeds, but the moon_assets partition is not flashed).")
endif()
```

### `README.md`

````markdown
# ESP32 Moon Phase Clock

A physically correct moon-phase clock. A 466 px disk of the moon -- the current
phase, from the last new moon to now -- is rendered in real time on an AMOLED
panel from LROC Wide-Angle Camera albedo and LOLA relief, lit with
displaced-normal Lambert shading at the exact Sun/Moon/Earth geometry of the
cheap ephemeris (JPL Moon98 + ERFA EPV). The disk is baked on-chip every day,
the free spin is a fixed-point in-plane re-gather (~8 ms/frame) written
straight to the panel, and sleep is signalled by a pole-axis spin that carries
the terminator across the disk to the fully unilluminated side. Time comes from
NTP (brief hourly WiFi activation, then back to airplane mode); the PCF85063A
RTC holds the clock between syncs.

## Build

```bash
source ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py build
idf.py flash
```

- **WiFi credentials** (before the first `idf.py flash`): two lines, SSID then
  password, in `spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt` (the template
  `spiffs/wifi_credentials.example.txt` is the format). The SPIFFS partition is
  re-baked from `spiffs/` on every build.
- **Timezone:** `idf.py menuconfig` -> Component config -> Clock Component
  Configuration -> Default timezone. Default: `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0/2,M10.5.0/3`.
- **Albedo/relief assets** (already in the tree, pre-generated): the
  `moon_assets` partition holds the 864x432 equirect albedo + 2048x1024 int8
  relief DEM. Regenerate with
  `assets/images/moon/.venv/bin/python -m moon.assets` (LROC + LOLA sources).

## Hardware

Waveshare **ESP32-S3 Touch AMOLED 1.75**, with the 16 MB flash variant:

| Block      | Part                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Display    | 466x466 AMOLED, RGB565               |
| Display IF | CO5300, QSPI (GPIO4-7, 38)           |
| Touch      | CST9217 (I2C, GPIO14/15/11)          |
| IMU        | QMI8658C (I2C)                       |
| RTC        | PCF85063A behind TCA9554 IO expander |
| Flash      | 16 MB                                |

Flash layout (`partitions.csv`): fixed 80 K (bootloader + table + NVS + PHY),
`factory` 1392 K (measured app 1.42 MB, ~1.3 KB margin), `storage` 64 K SPIFFS,
`moon_assets` 2560 K (albedo + DEM).

## Moon rendering

Per pixel of the disk the bake does: equirect gather of the 864x432 albedo
through the per-frame view basis, displaced-normal (normal from the int8 DEM
gradient) Lambert against the body-frame Sun direction, earthshine ramp for the
night side, and the 8-bit -> RGB565 tone LUT. One full-disk bake at the 2048 px
DEM takes ~1.3 s on the S3; the daily re-bake is the only lighting pass --
everything else (spin, tilt, the dusk) re-projects the baked result with a
fixed-point gather.

`host_sim/moon_sim` builds the **exact device core** on the host and writes
PNGs at the real panel size (`--size 466`); `host_sim/check_gate.py`
image-diffs it against NASA reference images.

## Animations

Rendered by `host_sim/render_demo.py` (PIL + `moon_sim` are the only deps):
`cmake --build host_sim/build && python3 host_sim/render_demo.py --phi-star <deg>`.
Each cell is a downscaled exact panel frame; the `--pole` flag of `moon_sim` is
a 1:1 copy of the device's pole spin (`moon_ui.c moon_pole_geometry`).

**Boot sweep** -- the synodic sweep from the last new moon to now (336 frames
on the device, 12 shown here):

![Boot sweep](docs/img/boot_sweep.png)

**Free spin** -- the settled animation: the disk rotates in-plane at the
current phase (8 rotations at 45 deg shown):

![Free spin](docs/img/free_spin.png)

**Dusk** -- light-sleep entry: a pole-axis spin, 1 deg/frame, until the fully
unilluminated side faces the viewer (phi\* = 139 deg for the demo epoch; the
final frame keeps its earthshine + crater-rim detail, not a flat black disk):

![Dusk](docs/img/dusk.png)

## Measured timings (device)

| Stage      | Value                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Boot sweep | 336 frames @ 240 px reduced-res bake, ~190 s (display-paced)                                                       |
| Free spin  | ~8 ms gather + direct panel write per frame (8 fps, settled 600 s/turn), 0 WDT resets                              |
| Dusk       | shade-map build 1598 ms once + 156 re-projected frames in 90.7 s + final full-res bake + 30 s deep-sleep countdown |
| Wake       | static current phase (no animation); hourly NTP re-sync on demand                                                  |

## Development

Before pushing, please manually run

```
idf.py save-defconfig
idf.py clang-check --exit-code --run-clang-tidy-options="-header-filter=''" main/main.cpp
```

### Test hooks

Kconfig switches for headless verification (all default off):
`TEST_SETTINGS_DEMO_SEC` (scripted settings run after boot),
`TEST_AUTO_WAKE_SEC`, `TEST_BAKE_NO_RELIEF`, `TEST_FORCE_NTP_SYNC`.

## Hardware Differences Affecting RTC-Driven Clocks

This clock component was tested on multiple Waveshare Touch-AMOLED boards.
However, **RTC interrupt and wake capabilities differ by board revision** due
to hardware wiring.

### ESP32-S3 Touch AMOLED 1.75

The external RTC (**PCF85063A**) is **not connected to any ESP32 GPIO**. RTC
interrupt (`RTC_INT`) is routed to the **AXP PMIC (EXIO3)** only, and AXP
interrupt (`AXP_IRQ`) is **not wired to the ESP32**.

**Consequences:** ❌ RTC alarms and timers **cannot generate interrupts**, ❌
RTC cannot wake the ESP32 from sleep, ❌ Minute-tick updates cannot be
interrupt-driven.

**Recommended usage:** Use the RTC **only as a time source**. Perform
**minute-aligned software updates** (e.g. via `esp_timer`). Do not rely on RTC
wake or alarm interrupts.

This board is designed for **continuous operation with display power
management**, not RTC-driven wake.

### RP2350 Touch AMOLED 2.41

The RTC interrupt is **directly wired to the MCU**. `RTC_INT` is connected to
**GPIO8**.

**Consequences:** ✅ RTC alarms and timers **can generate interrupts**, ✅
Minute-tick updates can be interrupt-driven, ✅ MCU wake from RTC events is
possible.

**Recommended usage:** Use RTC interrupts for **minute-aligned UI updates**.
Optional low-power sleep strategies using RTC wake.

This board supports a **traditional alarm-clock style architecture**.

---

[Data Sheet](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/RP2350-Touch-AMOLED-2.41/RP2350-Touch-AMOLED-2.41.pdf):

### Component Behavior

This clock component adapts its behavior based on the target board:

**On boards without RTC interrupts:** Time display updates are scheduled in
software.

**On boards with RTC interrupts:** Time display updates may be
interrupt-driven.

The API remains the same; only the internal scheduling strategy changes.

### Summary

| Board         | RTC → GPIO | RTC Interrupt | RTC Wake | Strategy                 |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| ESP32-S3 1.75 | ❌         | ❌            | ❌       | Software-timed updates   |
| RP2350 2.41   | ✅ (GPIO8) | ✅            | ✅       | Interrupt-driven updates |
````

### `components/board/CMakeLists.txt`

```ini
# Board shim: one stable include surface (include/board_display.h) over the
# two BSPs. The active BSP is selected by the build target — the P4 BSP is a
# registry dep gated to esp32p4 (main/idf_component.yml) and the vendored S3
# BSP registers only on esp32s3 (its own CMakeLists). CONFIG_BOARD_* is not
# in scope during component registration (kconfig runs later), so the target
# keys the choice; the root CMakeLists FATAL_ERRORs on a target/board
# mismatch anyway.
if(IDF_TARGET STREQUAL "esp32p4")
    set(BSP_COMPONENT waveshare__esp32_p4_wifi6_touch_lcd_xc)
else()
    set(BSP_COMPONENT esp32_s3_touch_amoled_1_75)
endif()

# esp_lcd / esp_driver_i2c / esp_io_expander: board_display.h includes
# their headers directly. (The P4 BSP keeps esp_lcd private, so the
# shim must take it publicly; on the S3 the vendored BSP already
# exports it — requiring it again is a no-op there.)
idf_component_register(
    SRCS "board_display.c"
    INCLUDE_DIRS "include"
    REQUIRES ${BSP_COMPONENT} esp_lcd esp_driver_i2c esp_io_expander
)
```

### `components/board/include/board_display.h`

```c
/* Board shim: the stable app-side surface over the two BSPs (the vendored
 * Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75 BSP and the registry Waveshare
 * ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD-XC BSP).
 *
 * Both BSPs ship a `bsp/esp-bsp.h` that resolves to the ACTIVE board
 * header, and they export an identical API except for two names:
 *   - bsp_display_get_panel() (S3) vs bsp_display_get_panel_handle() (P4)
 *   - the IO expander: bsp_io_expander_init() exists only on the S3
 *     (TCA9554; the P4 board has no expander).
 *
 * This header re-exports the active board header and normalizes those two
 * via board_panel() / board_io_expander_init(). Everything else —
 * bsp_display_start(), bsp_display_lock/unlock(), bsp_display_backlight_
 * on/off(), bsp_display_brightness_set(), bsp_i2c_get_handle(),
 * BSP_LCD_H_RES/V_RES — is identical on both BSPs and the app calls it
 * through each board's own BSP headers unchanged. */
#pragma once

#include "driver/i2c_master.h"
#include "esp_err.h"
#include "esp_io_expander.h"
#include "esp_lcd_types.h"

#include "bsp/esp-bsp.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Panel geometry (both BSPs define BSP_LCD_H_RES/V_RES). */
#define BOARD_LCD_W (BSP_LCD_H_RES)
#define BOARD_LCD_H (BSP_LCD_V_RES)

/* The active BSP's panel handle (S3 bsp_display_get_panel, P4
 * bsp_display_get_panel_handle). Valid after bsp_display_start. */
esp_lcd_panel_handle_t board_panel(void);

/* The S3 IO expander handle (TCA9554; the PCF85063A interrupt line).
 * The P4 board has no expander: returns NULL. */
esp_io_expander_handle_t board_io_expander_init(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/clock.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/time.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "driver/i2c_master.h"
#include "esp_io_expander.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"

#include "board_display.h"
#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_alarm.h"
#include "clock_interrupt.h"
#include "clock_sntp.h"
#include "clock_timer.h"
#include "pcf85063a.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_component";

// EXIO 3 pin definition (IO expander pin for RTC interrupt)
#define EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN IO_EXPANDER_PIN_NUM_3

// Global state accessible to other modules
pcf85063a_dev_t s_rtc_dev;
i2c_master_bus_handle_t s_bus_handle = NULL;
esp_io_expander_handle_t s_io_expander = NULL;
bool s_initialized = false;

// Validation functions
static bool validate_time(const clock_time_t *time) {
    if (!time)
        return false;
    if (time->year < 2000 || time->year > 2099)
        return false;
    if (time->month < 1 || time->month > 12)
        return false;
    if (time->day < 1 || time->day > 31)
        return false;
    if (time->hour < 0 || time->hour > 23)
        return false;
    if (time->minute < 0 || time->minute > 59)
        return false;
    if (time->second < 0 || time->second > 59)
        return false;
    return true;
}

// Helper functions to convert between our API and PCF85063A types
static void clock_to_pcf_time(const clock_time_t *clock_time, pcf85063a_datetime_t *pcf_time) {
    pcf_time->year = clock_time->year;
    pcf_time->month = clock_time->month;
    pcf_time->day = clock_time->day;
    pcf_time->hour = clock_time->hour;
    pcf_time->min = clock_time->minute;
    pcf_time->sec = clock_time->second;
    pcf_time->dotw = 0; // We don't use day of week
}

static void pcf_to_clock_time(const pcf85063a_datetime_t *pcf_time, clock_time_t *clock_time) {
    clock_time->year = pcf_time->year;
    clock_time->month = pcf_time->month;
    clock_time->day = pcf_time->day;
    clock_time->hour = pcf_time->hour;
    clock_time->minute = pcf_time->min;
    clock_time->second = pcf_time->sec;
}

esp_err_t clock_sync_time_from_ntp(uint32_t timeout_ms) {
    esp_err_t ret = clock_sntp_sync(timeout_ms);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "NTP synchronization failed: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
    clock_time_t time_to_set;
    ret = clock_sntp_get_system_time(&time_to_set);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to obtain NTP-synchronized time: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Successfully obtained time via NTP: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d", time_to_set.year,
             time_to_set.month, time_to_set.day, time_to_set.hour, time_to_set.minute, time_to_set.second);
    /* Only valid when the RTC is up (called from clock_init after
     * s_initialized = true, and from the sync task after boot). */
    if (s_initialized) {
        ret = clock_set_time(&time_to_set);
        if (ret != ESP_OK)
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to update RTC time: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }
    return ret;
}

esp_err_t clock_init(const clock_config_t *cfg) {
    if (!cfg) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid configuration");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Initializing clock component");

    esp_err_t ret;

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Get I2C master bus handle from BSP
    s_bus_handle = bsp_i2c_get_handle();
    if (!s_bus_handle) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get I2C bus handle from BSP");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    // Initialize PCF85063A using the library
    ret = pcf85063a_init(&s_rtc_dev, s_bus_handle, PCF85063A_ADDRESS);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to initialize PCF85063A: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Store IO expander handle (shim: the P4 board has no expander, but
    // this path is PCF-only anyway — see the CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A guard).
    s_io_expander = board_io_expander_init();
    if (!s_io_expander) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to initialize IO expander from BSP");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    // Configure EXIO 3 pin as input for RTC interrupt
    ret = esp_io_expander_set_dir(s_io_expander, EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN, IO_EXPANDER_INPUT);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to configure EXIO 3 as input: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
#else
    // No PCF85063A / IO expander on this build: the time base is the
    // crystal-backed internal RTC timer (RTC_CLK_SRC_EXT_CRYS) + SNTP; the
    // minute tick and the countdown/alarm arming run in software
    // (esp_timer, see clock_interrupt.c / clock_alarm_scheduler.c).
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "No external RTC IC (internal crystal RTC timer + SNTP)");
#endif

    // Mark as initialized before attempting time operations
    s_initialized = true;

    // Handle time initialization with NTP integration
    clock_time_t time_to_set;
    bool time_obtained = false;

    // Initialize SNTP component first
    ret = clock_sntp_init();
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to initialize SNTP: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }

    // Try NTP synchronization if enabled and WiFi is available
    if (cfg->enable_ntp_sync) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Attempting NTP time synchronization...");
        if (clock_sync_time_from_ntp(CONFIG_CLOCK_NTP_TIMEOUT_MS) == ESP_OK) {
            // clock_sync_time_from_ntp already wrote the (its own, valid)
            // value to the RTC; fill time_to_set from the now-synced system
            // clock so the redundant clock_set_time below does not write an
            // uninitialized stack variable (it was left unfilled on the
            // NTP-success path and logged "Invalid time values").
            if (clock_sntp_get_system_time(&time_to_set) == ESP_OK)
                time_obtained = true;
        }
    }

    // If NTP failed or not enabled, try to get system time
    if (!time_obtained) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Using system time for RTC initialization");
        ret = clock_sntp_get_system_time(&time_to_set);
        if (ret == ESP_OK) {
            time_obtained = true;
        }
    }

    // Check current RTC time
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Reading current time from RTC.");
    clock_time_t current_time;
    ret = clock_get_time(&current_time);

    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Current RTC time: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d", current_time.year, current_time.month,
                 current_time.day, current_time.hour, current_time.minute, current_time.second);
    } else {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to read RTC time: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }

    // Update RTC with synchronized time if available
    if (time_obtained) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Setting RTC to synchronized time: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d", time_to_set.year,
                 time_to_set.month, time_to_set.day, time_to_set.hour, time_to_set.minute, time_to_set.second);

        ret = clock_set_time(&time_to_set);
        if (ret == ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "RTC time updated successfully");
        } else {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to update RTC time: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        }
    }

    // Initialize alarm scheduler from SPIFFS
    ret = clock_alarm_scheduler_init();
    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm scheduler initialized, %d rules loaded", clock_alarm_get_rule_count());

        // Get current time and schedule next alarm
        clock_time_t alarm_current_time;
        ret = clock_get_time(&alarm_current_time);
        if (ret == ESP_OK) {
            ret = clock_alarm_schedule_next(&alarm_current_time);
            if (ret == ESP_OK) {
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Next alarm scheduled successfully");
            } else {
                ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to schedule next alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
            }
        }
    } else {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to initialize alarm scheduler: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Clock component initialized successfully");
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t clock_get_time(clock_time_t *out) {
    if (!out || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // No external RTC IC: the time base is the system clock (SNTP-synced;
    // the NVS epoch backup + unsynced UI flag land in M5.2).
    time_t now;
    struct tm timeinfo;
    time(&now);
    localtime_r(&now, &timeinfo);
    out->year = timeinfo.tm_year + 1900;
    out->month = timeinfo.tm_mon + 1;
    out->day = timeinfo.tm_mday;
    out->hour = timeinfo.tm_hour;
    out->minute = timeinfo.tm_min;
    out->second = timeinfo.tm_sec;
    return ESP_OK;
#else
    pcf85063a_datetime_t pcf_time;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_get_time_date(&s_rtc_dev, &pcf_time);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    pcf_to_clock_time(&pcf_time, out);
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_get_utc_epoch(int64_t *out) {
    if (!out)
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    if (!s_initialized)
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;

    clock_time_t t;
    esp_err_t ret = clock_get_time(&t);
    if (ret != ESP_OK)
        return ret;

    // Reject implausible dates so callers (moon phase) show nothing rather
    // than a wrong phase. validate_time covers the same ranges the RTC write
    // path uses.
    if (!validate_time(&t))
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;

    // The RTC holds local (TZ/DST-adjusted) time; mktime interprets it as
    // local and returns the UTC epoch. The TZ env var is set by
    // clock_sntp_init() during clock_init, before any moon use.
    struct tm tm;
    memset(&tm, 0, sizeof(tm));
    tm.tm_year = t.year - 1900;
    tm.tm_mon = t.month - 1;
    tm.tm_mday = t.day;
    tm.tm_hour = t.hour;
    tm.tm_min = t.minute;
    tm.tm_sec = t.second;
    tm.tm_isdst = -1;
    time_t epoch = mktime(&tm);
    if (epoch == (time_t)-1)
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;

    *out = (int64_t)epoch;
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t clock_set_time(const clock_time_t *time) {
    if (!time || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    if (!validate_time(time)) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid time values");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // No external RTC IC: the "RTC" is the system clock. mktime interprets
    // the value as local time (TZ/DST-adjusted), which is what settimeofday
    // wants.
    struct tm tm;
    memset(&tm, 0, sizeof(tm));
    tm.tm_year = time->year - 1900;
    tm.tm_mon = time->month - 1;
    tm.tm_mday = time->day;
    tm.tm_hour = time->hour;
    tm.tm_min = time->minute;
    tm.tm_sec = time->second;
    tm.tm_isdst = -1;
    time_t epoch = mktime(&tm);
    if (epoch == (time_t)-1) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    struct timeval tv = {.tv_sec = epoch, .tv_usec = 0};
    if (settimeofday(&tv, NULL) != 0) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }
    // The epoch of the scheduled alarm shifted with the wall clock: re-arm
    // the software one-shot (re-parses the rules, recomputes the next fire
    // from the new time, disarms on 0 rules). This is the re-arm after
    // every SNTP sync and manual time SET (DST itself needs no re-arm --
    // time(NULL) is the UTC epoch, which DST shifts do not move).
    clock_alarm_scheduler_reload();
    return ESP_OK;
#else
    pcf85063a_datetime_t pcf_time;
    clock_to_pcf_time(time, &pcf_time);

    return pcf85063a_set_time_date(&s_rtc_dev, pcf_time);
#endif
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_alarm.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_alarm.h"
#include "pcf85063a.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_alarm";

// External references from clock.c
extern pcf85063a_dev_t s_rtc_dev;
extern bool s_initialized;

// Helper functions to convert between our API and PCF85063A types
#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
static void clock_to_pcf_time(const clock_time_t *clock_time, pcf85063a_datetime_t *pcf_time) {
    pcf_time->year = clock_time->year;
    pcf_time->month = clock_time->month;
    pcf_time->day = clock_time->day;
    pcf_time->hour = clock_time->hour;
    pcf_time->min = clock_time->minute;
    pcf_time->sec = clock_time->second;
    pcf_time->dotw = 0; // We don't use day of week
}
#endif

esp_err_t clock_set_alarm(const clock_time_t *time) {
    if (!time || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    if (time->hour < 0 || time->hour > 23 || time->minute < 0 || time->minute > 59) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid alarm time");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    pcf85063a_datetime_t pcf_alarm_time;
    clock_to_pcf_time(time, &pcf_alarm_time);

    return pcf85063a_set_alarm(&s_rtc_dev, pcf_alarm_time);
#else
    // No PCF ALM registers: the scheduler's s_next_alarm cache is the
    // source of truth (it calls this before arming the software esp_timer
    // one-shot in clock_alarm_scheduler.c).
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Alarm time set (software, no PCF ALM registers)");
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_get_alarm(clock_time_t *time) {
    if (!time || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    pcf85063a_datetime_t pcf_alarm_time;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_get_alarm(&s_rtc_dev, &pcf_alarm_time);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    // Convert PCF format to clock format (only hour and minute are relevant for alarm)
    time->hour = pcf_alarm_time.hour;
    time->minute = pcf_alarm_time.min;
    time->second = pcf_alarm_time.sec;
    time->year = 0;
    time->month = 0;
    time->day = 0;

    return ESP_OK;
#else
    // No PCF ALM registers to read back; the scheduled alarm lives in the
    // scheduler (clock_alarm_scheduler.c).
    return ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_enable_alarm(bool enable) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Read current CTRL2 to preserve MI/HMI bits
    uint8_t ctrl2;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &ctrl2, 1);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    if (enable) {
        // Enable alarm interrupt by setting AIE bit, clear AF flag
        ctrl2 |= PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AIE;
        ctrl2 &= ~PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AF;
    } else {
        // Disable alarm interrupt by clearing AIE bit
        ctrl2 &= ~PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AIE;
    }

    uint8_t write_buf[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, ctrl2};
    return pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_buf, 2);
#else
    // No PCF AIE bit: the alarm's armed state is the scheduler's esp_timer
    // one-shot (armed together with the s_next_alarm cache in
    // clock_alarm_scheduler.c).
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Alarm %s (software, no PCF AIE bit)", enable ? "enabled" : "disabled");
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_clear_alarm(void) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Disable alarm interrupt
    esp_err_t ret = clock_enable_alarm(false);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    // Clear alarm registers by writing 0 (disable alarm enable bits)
    uint8_t disabled_alarm = 0;
    uint8_t write_buf1[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_MINUTE_ALARM, disabled_alarm};
    ret = pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_buf1, 2);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    uint8_t write_buf2[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_HOUR_ALARM, disabled_alarm};
    return pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_buf2, 2);
#else
    // No PCF ALM registers to clear; the 0-rule phantom guard on the P4 is
    // "no esp_timer one-shot armed" (the scheduler owns that, see
    // clock_alarm_scheduler.c).
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Alarm cleared (software, no PCF ALM registers)");
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}
```
