### `components/clock/clock_alarm_scheduler.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_alarm.h"
#include "clock_alarm_scheduler.h"
#include "clock_cb.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_alarm_sched";
static const char *ALARM_FILE_PATH = "/spiffs/alarm.txt";

static alarm_rule_t s_alarm_rules[MAX_ALARM_RULES];
static int s_alarm_count = 0;
static clock_time_t s_next_alarm = {0}; // Cache of next scheduled alarm
static bool s_alarm_scheduled = false;  // Whether an alarm is currently scheduled

// Day of week calculation (Zeller's congruence for Gregorian calendar)
static int get_day_of_week(int year, int month, int day) {
    if (month < 3) {
        month += 12;
        year--;
    }
    int q = day;
    int m = month;
    int k = year % 100;
    int j = year / 100;
    int h = (q + ((13 * (m + 1)) / 5) + k + (k / 4) + (j / 4) - (2 * j)) % 7;
    // Convert to 0=Sunday, 1=Monday, ..., 6=Saturday
    return (h + 6) % 7;
}

// Parse day of week pattern (e.g., "1-5", "0,6", "*")
static bool parse_day_pattern(const char *pattern, uint8_t *day_mask, bool *all_days) {
    *day_mask = 0;
    *all_days = false;

    if (strcmp(pattern, "*") == 0) {
        *all_days = true;
        return true;
    }

    // Check for range (e.g., "1-5")
    if (strchr(pattern, '-')) {
        int start, end;
        if (sscanf(pattern, "%d-%d", &start, &end) == 2) {
            if (start < 0 || start > 6 || end < 0 || end > 6 || start > end) {
                return false;
            }
            for (int i = start; i <= end; i++) {
                *day_mask |= (1 << i);
            }
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Check for comma-separated list (e.g., "0,6")
    if (strchr(pattern, ',')) {
        char *pattern_copy = strdup(pattern);
        if (!pattern_copy) {
            return false;
        }
        char *token = strtok(pattern_copy, ",");
        while (token) {
            int day = atoi(token);
            if (day < 0 || day > 6) {
                free(pattern_copy);
                return false;
            }
            *day_mask |= (1 << day);
            token = strtok(NULL, ",");
        }
        free(pattern_copy);
        return true;
    }

    // Single day
    int day = atoi(pattern);
    if (day < 0 || day > 6) {
        return false;
    }
    *day_mask = (1 << day);
    return true;
}

// Parse minute or hour field (supports *, */N, or number).
// For the minute field the */N interval may span the whole day (N up to
// 1440, the pomodoro "repeat every N minutes" setting); the hour field
// is capped at its own range.
static bool parse_time_field(const char *field, int *value, int *interval, int max_value) {
    *value = -1;   // -1 means wildcard
    *interval = 0; // 0 means no interval

    if (strcmp(field, "*") == 0) {
        *value = -1; // wildcard
        return true;
    }

    // Check for */N pattern
    if (strncmp(field, "*/", 2) == 0) {
        int n = atoi(field + 2);
        int interval_max = (max_value == 59) ? 1440 : max_value; /* minutes may span the day */
        if (n <= 0 || n > interval_max) {
            return false;
        }
        *interval = n;
        *value = -1; // wildcard with interval
        return true;
    }

    // Regular number
    int n = atoi(field);
    if (n < 0 || n > max_value) {
        return false;
    }
    *value = n;
    return true;
}

// Parse a single alarm rule line (cron format: minute hour day_of_month month day_of_week)
static bool parse_alarm_line(const char *line, alarm_rule_t *rule) {
    char minute_str[16], hour_str[16], dom_str[16], month_str[16], dow_str[32];

    // Skip empty lines and comments
    if (line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '\0' || line[0] == '\n') {
        return false;
    }

    // Parse format: "minute hour day_of_month month day_of_week"
    int parsed = sscanf(line, "%15s %15s %15s %15s %31s", minute_str, hour_str, dom_str, month_str, dow_str);

    // Support both 5-field and 3-field formats for backward compatibility
    if (parsed == 3) {
        // Old 3-field format: minute hour day_of_week
        strcpy(dow_str, dom_str);
        strcpy(dom_str, "*");
        strcpy(month_str, "*");
    } else if (parsed != 5) {
        return false;
    }

    // Parse minute field
    if (!parse_time_field(minute_str, &rule->minute, &rule->minute_interval, 59)) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid minute field: %s", minute_str);
        return false;
    }

    // Parse hour field
    if (!parse_time_field(hour_str, &rule->hour, &rule->hour_interval, 23)) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid hour field: %s", hour_str);
        return false;
    }

    // Validate: can't have both minute and hour intervals
    if (rule->minute_interval > 0 && rule->hour_interval > 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Cannot specify both minute and hour intervals");
        return false;
    }

    // Parse day of week pattern
    if (!parse_day_pattern(dow_str, &rule->day_mask, &rule->all_days)) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid day pattern: %s", dow_str);
        return false;
    }

    // Log the parsed rule
    if (rule->minute_interval > 0) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Parsed alarm rule: every %d minutes at hour %s, days=0x%02x", rule->minute_interval, hour_str,
                 rule->day_mask);
    } else if (rule->hour_interval > 0) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Parsed alarm rule: minute %d, every %d hours, days=0x%02x", rule->minute, rule->hour_interval,
                 rule->day_mask);
    } else {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Parsed alarm rule: %02d:%02d, days=0x%02x, all_days=%d", rule->hour, rule->minute,
                 rule->day_mask, rule->all_days);
    }

    return true;
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_init(void) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Initializing alarm scheduler from SPIFFS");

    // SPIFFS is already initialized by the system
    // Just try to open the alarm file
    FILE *f = fopen(ALARM_FILE_PATH, "r");
    if (!f) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to open alarm file: %s (file may not exist yet)", ALARM_FILE_PATH);
        return ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND;
    }

    // Read and parse alarm rules
    s_alarm_count = 0;
    char line[128];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) && s_alarm_count < MAX_ALARM_RULES) {
        // Remove newline
        line[strcspn(line, "\r\n")] = 0;

        alarm_rule_t rule;
        if (parse_alarm_line(line, &rule)) {
            s_alarm_rules[s_alarm_count++] = rule;
        }
    }

    fclose(f);

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Loaded %d alarm rules from SPIFFS", s_alarm_count);
    return ESP_OK;
}

// Calculate next alarm time based on a single rule
static bool calculate_next_alarm_time(const alarm_rule_t *rule, const clock_time_t *current, clock_time_t *next) {
    // Handle interval-based alarms (*/N syntax)
    if (rule->minute_interval > 0) {
        if (rule->minute_interval > 59) {
            // Interval spans the whole day (pomodoro "every N minutes", N up
            // to 1440): the grid is anchored at midnight, so the next ring is
            // the first total-minutes-of-day multiple of N strictly after
            // now, or 00:00 of the next day once today's grid is exhausted.
            int total = current->hour * 60 + current->minute + 1;
            int next_total = ((total + rule->minute_interval - 1) / rule->minute_interval) * rule->minute_interval;

            if (next_total >= 1440) {
                // Today's grid is exhausted: 00:00 of the next day.
                struct tm time_info = {0};
                time_info.tm_year = current->year - 1900;
                time_info.tm_mon = current->month - 1;
                time_info.tm_mday = current->day + 1;
                time_info.tm_hour = 0;
                time_info.tm_min = 0;
                mktime(&time_info);
                next->year = time_info.tm_year + 1900;
                next->month = time_info.tm_mon + 1;
                next->day = time_info.tm_mday;
                next->hour = 0;
                next->minute = 0;
            } else {
                next->year = current->year;
                next->month = current->month;
                next->day = current->day;
                next->hour = next_total / 60;
                next->minute = next_total % 60;
            }
            next->second = 0;

            // Check if this day matches the rule's day mask (pomodoro writes
            // "*", so it is all days).
            int day_of_week = get_day_of_week(next->year, next->month, next->day);
            if (!rule->all_days && !(rule->day_mask & (1 << day_of_week))) {
                // This day doesn't match, find the next matching day (the
                // grid restarts at 00:00, a multiple of any interval).
                for (int day_offset = 1; day_offset < 8; day_offset++) {
                    struct tm time_info = {0};
                    time_info.tm_year = next->year - 1900;
                    time_info.tm_mon = next->month - 1;
                    time_info.tm_mday = next->day + day_offset;
                    time_info.tm_hour = 0;
                    time_info.tm_min = 0;
                    mktime(&time_info);

                    int dow = get_day_of_week(time_info.tm_year + 1900, time_info.tm_mon + 1, time_info.tm_mday);
                    if (rule->day_mask & (1 << dow)) {
                        next->year = time_info.tm_year + 1900;
                        next->month = time_info.tm_mon + 1;
                        next->day = time_info.tm_mday;
                        next->hour = 0;
                        next->minute = 0;
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }
            return true;
        }

        // Every N minutes (N <= 59: at most one ring per hour)
        next->year = current->year;
        next->month = current->month;
        next->day = current->day;
        next->hour = current->hour;
        next->second = 0;

        // Calculate next minute that's a multiple of the interval
        int current_minute = current->minute + 1; // Next minute
        int next_minute =
            ((current_minute + rule->minute_interval - 1) / rule->minute_interval) * rule->minute_interval;

        if (next_minute >= 60) {
            // Move to next hour
            next->hour++;
            next_minute = 0;

            if (next->hour >= 24) {
                // Move to next day
                next->hour = 0;
                struct tm time_info = {0};
                time_info.tm_year = current->year - 1900;
                time_info.tm_mon = current->month - 1;
                time_info.tm_mday = current->day + 1;
                mktime(&time_info);
                next->year = time_info.tm_year + 1900;
                next->month = time_info.tm_mon + 1;
                next->day = time_info.tm_mday;
            }
        }
        next->minute = next_minute;

        // Check if this day matches the rule's day mask
        int day_of_week = get_day_of_week(next->year, next->month, next->day);
        if (!rule->all_days && !(rule->day_mask & (1 << day_of_week))) {
            // This day doesn't match, find the next matching day
            for (int day_offset = 1; day_offset < 8; day_offset++) {
                struct tm time_info = {0};
                time_info.tm_year = current->year - 1900;
                time_info.tm_mon = current->month - 1;
                time_info.tm_mday = current->day + day_offset;
                time_info.tm_hour = 0;
                time_info.tm_min = 0;
                mktime(&time_info);

                int dow = get_day_of_week(time_info.tm_year + 1900, time_info.tm_mon + 1, time_info.tm_mday);
                if (rule->day_mask & (1 << dow)) {
                    next->year = time_info.tm_year + 1900;
                    next->month = time_info.tm_mon + 1;
                    next->day = time_info.tm_mday;
                    next->hour = 0;
                    next->minute = 0;
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Handle regular time-based alarms
    next->year = current->year;
    next->month = current->month;
    next->day = current->day;
    next->hour = rule->hour;
    next->minute = rule->minute;
    next->second = 0;

    // Check if alarm time today has already passed
    bool alarm_passed_today = false;
    if (current->hour > rule->hour || (current->hour == rule->hour && current->minute >= rule->minute)) {
        alarm_passed_today = true;
    }

    // Try up to 7 days to find the next matching day
    for (int day_offset = (alarm_passed_today ? 1 : 0); day_offset < 8; day_offset++) {
        // Calculate the date
        struct tm time_info = {0};
        time_info.tm_year = current->year - 1900;
        time_info.tm_mon = current->month - 1;
        time_info.tm_mday = current->day + day_offset;
        time_info.tm_hour = rule->hour;
        time_info.tm_min = rule->minute;
        time_info.tm_sec = 0;

        // Normalize the date (handles month/year rollover)
        mktime(&time_info);

        int day_of_week = get_day_of_week(time_info.tm_year + 1900, time_info.tm_mon + 1, time_info.tm_mday);

        // Check if this day matches the rule
        if (rule->all_days || (rule->day_mask & (1 << day_of_week))) {
            next->year = time_info.tm_year + 1900;
            next->month = time_info.tm_mon + 1;
            next->day = time_info.tm_mday;
            return true;
        }
    }

    return false;
}

// Compare two times and return true if time1 < time2
static bool time_is_before(const clock_time_t *time1, const clock_time_t *time2) {
    if (time1->year != time2->year)
        return time1->year < time2->year;
    if (time1->month != time2->month)
        return time1->month < time2->month;
    if (time1->day != time2->day)
        return time1->day < time2->day;
    if (time1->hour != time2->hour)
        return time1->hour < time2->hour;
    return time1->minute < time2->minute;
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_schedule_next(const clock_time_t *current_time) {
    if (!current_time || s_alarm_count == 0) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "No alarm rules loaded or invalid current time");
        if (s_alarm_count == 0) {
            /* Disarm the hardware alarm: the PCF85063A's ALM register
             * persists on the RTC, so a stale armed time (e.g. from a
             * previous boot's rules) would otherwise fire a phantom
             * alarm screen when the clock next matches it -- with no
             * rules loaded there is nothing left to reschedule. On a
             * no-PCF build the phantom guard is "no software one-shot
             * armed" (the disarm below, esp_timer is not persistent). */
            esp_err_t ret = clock_clear_alarm();
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
            clock_alarm_disarm_esp_timer();
#endif
            if (ret != ESP_OK) {
                ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to clear stale RTC alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
            } else {
                s_alarm_scheduled = false;
            }
        }
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Calculating next alarm from current time: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d", current_time->year,
             current_time->month, current_time->day, current_time->hour, current_time->minute, current_time->second);

    clock_time_t next_alarm = {0};
    bool found_alarm = false;

    // Check all rules and find the nearest alarm
    for (int i = 0; i < s_alarm_count; i++) {
        clock_time_t candidate = {0};
        if (calculate_next_alarm_time(&s_alarm_rules[i], current_time, &candidate)) {
            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Rule %d candidate: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d", i, candidate.year, candidate.month,
                     candidate.day, candidate.hour, candidate.minute);

            if (!found_alarm || time_is_before(&candidate, &next_alarm)) {
                next_alarm = candidate;
                found_alarm = true;
            }
        }
    }

    if (!found_alarm) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to calculate next alarm time");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Next alarm scheduled for: %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d", next_alarm.year, next_alarm.month,
             next_alarm.day, next_alarm.hour, next_alarm.minute);

    // Cache the next alarm time before setting it
    s_next_alarm = next_alarm;
    s_alarm_scheduled = true;

    // Set the alarm in the RTC (a validated no-op on no-PCF builds)
    esp_err_t ret = clock_set_alarm(&next_alarm);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to set alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Enable the alarm (AIE bit; a no-op on no-PCF builds)
    ret = clock_enable_alarm(true);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to enable alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Arm the software one-shot for the epoch of the scheduled time.
    // Reaching this from clock_alarm_scheduler_reload also covers an
    // SNTP/manual time SET that shifted the epoch (the poll's backup
    // check is the backstop). The fire itself is gated on
    // clock_sntp_time_trusted() in the poll.
    ret = clock_alarm_arm_esp_timer(&next_alarm);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to arm software alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
#endif

    // Trigger alarm display update via callback
    clock_trigger_alarm_update();

    return ESP_OK;
}

int clock_alarm_get_rule_count(void) { return s_alarm_count; }

esp_err_t clock_alarm_get_next_scheduled(clock_time_t *time) {
    if (!time) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    if (!s_alarm_scheduled) {
        return ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND;
    }

    *time = s_next_alarm;
    return ESP_OK;
}

// Write the alarm file (full replace). The content is cron rules, one per
// line, or comments only for "no alarms".
esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_write(const char *content) {
    if (!content) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    FILE *f = fopen(ALARM_FILE_PATH, "w");
    if (!f) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to open alarm file for writing: %s", ALARM_FILE_PATH);
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    int n = fputs(content, f);
    fclose(f);
    if (n < 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Alarm file write failed");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm file written (%d bytes)", (int)strlen(content));
    return ESP_OK;
}

// Re-parse the alarm file and reschedule from the current RTC time. 0
// valid rules (missing file or comments only) disarms the hardware
// alarm -- the PCF85063A's ALM register persists on the RTC, so a stale
// armed time would otherwise fire a phantom alarm.
esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_reload(void) {
    esp_err_t ret = clock_alarm_scheduler_init();
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        s_alarm_count = 0;
        s_alarm_scheduled = false;
    }

    if (s_alarm_count == 0) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm reload: 0 rules -- disarming the RTC alarm");
        esp_err_t clear = clock_clear_alarm();
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
        // The software one-shot is not persistent, but the scheduler cache
        // IS: drop it too, or the poll's backup check would see a stale
        // scheduled alarm after the last rule was deleted. (The S3 keeps
        // its historical stale-cache behavior -- the UI refreshes on the
        // rule-write path.)
        s_alarm_scheduled = false;
        clock_alarm_disarm_esp_timer();
#endif
        if (clear != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to clear stale RTC alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(clear));
        }
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    clock_time_t now;
    ret = clock_get_time(&now);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Alarm reload: failed to read RTC time: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
    return clock_alarm_schedule_next(&now);
}

uint8_t clock_alarm_rule_types(void) {
    uint8_t types = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < s_alarm_count; i++) {
        if (s_alarm_rules[i].minute_interval > 0) {
            types |= 1u << 0; /* interval rule (pomodoro) */
        } else if (s_alarm_rules[i].minute >= 0 && s_alarm_rules[i].hour >= 0) {
            types |= 1u << 1; /* fixed-time rule */
        }
    }
    return types;
}

int clock_alarm_get_interval_rule(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < s_alarm_count; i++) {
        if (s_alarm_rules[i].minute_interval > 0) {
            return s_alarm_rules[i].minute_interval;
        }
    }
    return -1;
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_get_fixed_rule(int *hour, int *minute, uint8_t *dow_mask) {
    for (int i = 0; i < s_alarm_count; i++) {
        if (s_alarm_rules[i].minute >= 0 && s_alarm_rules[i].hour >= 0) {
            if (hour)
                *hour = s_alarm_rules[i].hour;
            if (minute)
                *minute = s_alarm_rules[i].minute;
            if (dow_mask)
                *dow_mask = s_alarm_rules[i].all_days ? 0x7F : s_alarm_rules[i].day_mask;
            return ESP_OK;
        }
    }
    return ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND;
}

// Render a day-of-week mask as the cron dow field: "*" for all 7 days,
// otherwise a comma list (0=Sunday .. 6=Saturday).
static bool alarm_dow_mask_to_str(uint8_t mask, char *out, size_t out_len) {
    if (mask == 0) {
        return false;
    }
    if (mask == 0x7F) {
        snprintf(out, out_len, "*");
        return true;
    }
    size_t pos = 0;
    for (int d = 0; d < 7; d++) {
        if (!(mask & (1u << d))) {
            continue;
        }
        int n = snprintf(out + pos, out_len - pos, "%s%d", pos > 0 ? "," : "", d);
        if (n < 0 || (size_t)n >= out_len - pos) {
            return false;
        }
        pos += (size_t)n;
    }
    return true;
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_set_pomodoro_interval(int minutes_total) {
    if (minutes_total < 1 || minutes_total > 1440) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid pomodoro interval: %d minutes", minutes_total);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    char content[96];
    snprintf(content, sizeof(content), "# pomodoro: ring every %d minutes\n*/%d * * * *\n", minutes_total,
             minutes_total);
    esp_err_t ret = clock_alarm_scheduler_write(content);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }
    return clock_alarm_scheduler_reload();
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_set_clock_alarm(int hour, int minute, uint8_t dow_mask) {
    if (hour < 0 || hour > 23 || minute < 0 || minute > 59) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid alarm time: %02d:%02d", hour, minute);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    char dow[32];
    if (!alarm_dow_mask_to_str(dow_mask, dow, sizeof(dow))) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid day mask: 0x%02x (no day selected)", dow_mask);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    char content[96];
    snprintf(content, sizeof(content), "# alarm: %02d:%02d on %s\n%d %d * * %s\n", minute, hour, dow, minute, hour,
             dow);
    esp_err_t ret = clock_alarm_scheduler_write(content);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }
    return clock_alarm_scheduler_reload();
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_deactivate_all(void) {
    esp_err_t ret = clock_alarm_scheduler_write("# no alarms\n");
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }
    return clock_alarm_scheduler_reload();
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_idle.c`

```c
#include "clock_idle.h"
#include "clock_cb.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_timer.h"
#include "lvgl.h"
#include "sdkconfig.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_idle";

// Idle state
static uint64_t s_last_activity_time_ms = 0;
static uint64_t s_idle_entered_ms = 0; /* when the current idle episode started (0 = not idle) */
static bool s_is_in_idle_mode = false;
static bool s_idle_monitoring_enabled = true;

// Configuration from Kconfig (the default; the runtime settings store
// can override it via clock_idle_set_timeout_ms before/at boot and from
// the light-sleep settings screen).
#ifndef CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC
#define CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC 10
#endif
static uint64_t s_idle_timeout_ms = (uint64_t)CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC * 1000ULL;

void clock_idle_set_timeout_ms(uint64_t timeout_ms) {
    if (timeout_ms < 10ULL * 1000ULL)
        timeout_ms = 10ULL * 1000ULL; /* match the Kconfig range floor */
    if (timeout_ms > 300ULL * 1000ULL)
        timeout_ms = 300ULL * 1000ULL;
    s_idle_timeout_ms = timeout_ms;
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Idle timeout set to %llu ms", (unsigned long long)timeout_ms);
}

/**
 * @brief Input device read callback to detect user activity
 */
static void indev_read_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
    lv_indev_t *indev = lv_event_get_target(e);

    // Check if input device is currently pressed/active
    if (lv_indev_get_state(indev) == LV_INDEV_STATE_PRESSED) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "User activity detected (touch)");

        // Update last activity time
        s_last_activity_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;

        // Only trigger wake callback if we were in idle mode
        // (This prevents triggering on every touch when already on main screen)
        if (s_is_in_idle_mode) {
            uint64_t in_idle_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000 - s_idle_entered_ms;
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Waking from idle mode after %llu ms in sleep", (unsigned long long)in_idle_ms);
            s_is_in_idle_mode = false;
            s_idle_entered_ms = 0;
            clock_trigger_idle_wake();
        } else {
            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "touch while active (no wake)");
        }
    }
}

esp_err_t clock_idle_init(void) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Initializing idle timer (timeout: %llu ms)", (unsigned long long)s_idle_timeout_ms);

    // Initialize last activity time to now
    s_last_activity_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;
    s_is_in_idle_mode = false;

    // Register callback on input device to detect touch activity
    lv_indev_t *indev = lv_indev_get_next(NULL);
    if (indev) {
        lv_indev_add_event_cb(indev, indev_read_cb, LV_EVENT_PRESSED, NULL);
        lv_indev_add_event_cb(indev, indev_read_cb, LV_EVENT_PRESSING, NULL);
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Input device event callbacks registered");
    } else {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get input device");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    return ESP_OK;
}

void clock_idle_reset_timer(void) {
    s_last_activity_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Idle timer reset");
}

/* Tilt (IMU) is the moon's input, so sustained device motion counts as
 * user activity: it holds the idle timer while the user is manipulating
 * the ball, and it is the wake path from sleep for a device operated by
 * tilt rather than touch (touch was the only wake input before; the RTC
 * alarm was the only thing that could recover a tilt-only device from
 * sleep). Called at most once per second by the moon UI's tilt monitor. */
void clock_idle_notify_tilt_activity(void) {
    s_last_activity_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;
    if (s_is_in_idle_mode) {
        uint64_t in_idle_ms = s_last_activity_time_ms - s_idle_entered_ms;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Waking from idle mode via tilt after %llu ms in sleep", (unsigned long long)in_idle_ms);
        s_is_in_idle_mode = false;
        s_idle_entered_ms = 0;
        clock_trigger_idle_wake();
    } else {
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "tilt activity while active (no wake)");
    }
}

void clock_idle_check_cb(lv_timer_t *timer) {
    // Don't check if idle monitoring is disabled (e.g., on alarm screen)
    if (!s_idle_monitoring_enabled) {
        return;
    }

    // Don't check if already in idle mode
    if (s_is_in_idle_mode) {
        return;
    }

    uint64_t current_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;
    uint64_t idle_duration_ms = current_time_ms - s_last_activity_time_ms;

    // Check if idle timeout has been reached
    if (idle_duration_ms >= s_idle_timeout_ms) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Idle timeout reached after %llu ms", (unsigned long long)idle_duration_ms);

        s_is_in_idle_mode = true;
        s_idle_entered_ms = current_time_ms;

        // Trigger idle timeout callback
        clock_trigger_idle_timeout();
    }
}

bool clock_is_idle(void) { return s_is_in_idle_mode; }

uint64_t clock_idle_last_activity_ms(void) { return (uint64_t)(esp_timer_get_time() / 1000) - s_last_activity_time_ms; }

void clock_idle_set_enabled(bool enabled) {
    s_idle_monitoring_enabled = enabled;
    if (enabled) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Idle monitoring enabled");
        // Reset timer when re-enabling
        s_last_activity_time_ms = esp_timer_get_time() / 1000;
    } else {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Idle monitoring disabled");
    }
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_interrupt.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "esp_io_expander.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_timer.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_alarm_scheduler.h"
#include "clock_cb.h"
#include "clock_interrupt.h"
#include "clock_minute.h"
#include "clock_sntp.h"
#include "clock_timer.h"
#include "pcf85063a.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_interrupt";

// EXIO 3 pin definition (IO expander pin for RTC interrupt)
#define EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN IO_EXPANDER_PIN_NUM_3

// Polling interval for interrupt detection (in milliseconds)
// Expiration detection is time-based (see clock_handle_interrupts); the
// interval only affects how late the first poll past expiry can be.
static uint32_t s_rtc_poll_interval_ms = 1300; // Default value

// External references from clock.c
extern pcf85063a_dev_t s_rtc_dev;
extern esp_io_expander_handle_t s_io_expander;
extern bool s_initialized;

// P4 (no PCF85063A): the one-shot esp_timer that arms the next alarm fire
// (the analog of the PCF's ALM register + AF flag). Its callback only sets
// the flag -- firing the UI callback happens here, in the LVGL task, under
// the same context discipline as the S3's TF/AF poll.
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
static esp_timer_handle_t s_alarm_esp_timer = NULL;
static volatile bool s_alarm_fired_flag = false;

static void alarm_esp_timer_cb(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    s_alarm_fired_flag = true;
}

static int64_t alarm_local_time_to_epoch(const clock_time_t *t) {
    struct tm tm = {0};
    tm.tm_year = t->year - 1900;
    tm.tm_mon = t->month - 1;
    tm.tm_mday = t->day;
    tm.tm_hour = t->hour;
    tm.tm_min = t->minute;
    tm.tm_sec = 0;
    tm.tm_isdst = -1; // mktime applies the configured TZ/DST rules
    time_t epoch = mktime(&tm);
    return (epoch == (time_t)-1) ? -1 : (int64_t)epoch;
}

esp_err_t clock_alarm_arm_esp_timer(const clock_time_t *next) {
    if (!next) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    int64_t next_epoch = alarm_local_time_to_epoch(next);
    int64_t now_epoch = (int64_t)time(NULL);
    if (next_epoch < 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Alarm arm: mktime failed for the scheduled time");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    int64_t delta_us = (next_epoch - now_epoch) * 1000000;
    if (delta_us < 0) {
        // Already past (an SNTP/manual SET moved the wall clock): the poll
        // fires it on its next pass (the backup check), no one-shot.
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm arm: %lld s in the past -- the poll will fire it", (long long)(-delta_us / 1000000));
        return ESP_OK;
    }
    if (!s_alarm_esp_timer) {
        const esp_timer_create_args_t args = {
            .callback = alarm_esp_timer_cb,
            .name = "clock_alarm",
        };
        esp_err_t ret = esp_timer_create(&args, &s_alarm_esp_timer);
        if (ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create alarm esp_timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
            return ret;
        }
    }
    // Re-arm: stop any previous one-shot, reset the flag, start fresh. (A
    // time SET that shifts the epoch reaches this via schedule_next.)
    esp_timer_stop(s_alarm_esp_timer);
    s_alarm_fired_flag = false;
    esp_err_t ret = esp_timer_start_once(s_alarm_esp_timer, delta_us);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to start alarm esp_timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm one-shot armed for %lld s", (long long)(delta_us / 1000000));
    return ESP_OK;
}

void clock_alarm_disarm_esp_timer(void) {
    if (s_alarm_esp_timer) {
        esp_timer_stop(s_alarm_esp_timer);
    }
    s_alarm_fired_flag = false;
}
#endif

/**
 * @brief Handle all RTC interrupts in one function
 *
 * This function checks for pending RTC interrupts and processes them appropriately.
 * It handles both timer and alarm interrupts, managing synchronization and clearing flags.
 * Callbacks are invoked directly for both timer and alarm interrupts.
 * On no-PCF builds (the P4) the three conditions are synthesized from
 * wall-clock state instead of PCF flag registers.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_handle_interrupts(void) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Software clock path (the P4 has no PCF85063A, no INT line): synthesize
    // the three PCF interrupt conditions from wall-clock state, in the S3's
    // priority order (countdown, then minute, then alarm). All state is
    // consumed here, in the LVGL task, the same as the PCF-flag processing.
    {
        struct tm now_tm;
        time_t now = time(NULL);
        localtime_r(&now, &now_tm);
        clock_time_t now_local;
        now_local.year = now_tm.tm_year + 1900;
        now_local.month = now_tm.tm_mon + 1;
        now_local.day = now_tm.tm_mday;
        now_local.hour = now_tm.tm_hour;
        now_local.minute = now_tm.tm_min;
        now_local.second = now_tm.tm_sec;

        // 1) Countdown expiration (the deep-sleep transition). The one-shot
        // set the flag when it fired; the host start timestamp is the
        // oracle, exactly as on the S3 (clock_timer.c owns the one-shot).
        if (clock_timer_is_active()) {
            uint8_t initial_value = clock_timer_get_value();
            int64_t elapsed_s = (esp_timer_get_time() - clock_timer_get_enabled_at_us()) / 1000000;
            int64_t expiry_s = (initial_value > 1) ? (initial_value - 1) : 0;
            bool expired = clock_timer_take_expired() || elapsed_s >= expiry_s;
            if (expired) {
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Countdown timer expired (software, elapsed=%llds) - triggering deep sleep transition",
                         (long long)elapsed_s);
                esp_err_t disable_ret = clock_timer_disable();
                if (disable_ret != ESP_OK) {
                    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to disable countdown timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(disable_ret));
                }
                clock_trigger_countdown_timer();
                return ESP_OK;
            }
        }

        // 2) Minute tick: a wall-clock minute rollover since the last poll
        // (exact -- the 1.3 s poll cannot straddle one rollover twice; see
        // clock_minute.c).
        bool is_minute_tick = false;
        clock_minute_process_interrupt(&is_minute_tick);
        if (is_minute_tick) {
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Minute interrupt processed (software rollover) - updating display");
            clock_trigger_time_update();
            // The 15-min NVS epoch snapshot (the P4's cross-power-loss
            // time memory; no-op most polls).
            clock_nvs_maybe_save_epoch();
        }

        // 3) Alarm fire: the one-shot reached the next alarm epoch, or the
        // wall clock is already past it (the backup check -- catches a
        // one-shot that a time SET left stale). Gated on time_trusted so a
        // default/unsynced clock (2026-01-24 12:00) can never fire a
        // phantom. Mirrors the S3's fire-then-reschedule sequence.
        clock_time_t next = {0};
        esp_err_t next_ret = clock_alarm_get_next_scheduled(&next);
        bool fired = s_alarm_fired_flag;
        s_alarm_fired_flag = false;
        if (next_ret == ESP_OK && clock_sntp_time_trusted()) {
            int64_t next_epoch = alarm_local_time_to_epoch(&next);
            if (next_epoch > 0 && (fired || now >= (time_t)next_epoch)) {
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm interrupt triggered (software, %02d:%02d)", next.hour, next.minute);
                if (s_alarm_esp_timer) {
                    esp_timer_stop(s_alarm_esp_timer);
                }
                s_alarm_fired_flag = false;
                clock_trigger_alarm_triggered();
                // Reschedule from the current time (the S3's AF handling
                // does the same; the one-shot is re-armed there).
                clock_alarm_schedule_next(&now_local);
            }
        }

        return ESP_OK;
    }
#else
    // Check if there's a pending interrupt on EXIO 3
    bool interrupt_pending = clock_is_interrupt_pending();
    if (!interrupt_pending) {
        return ESP_OK; // No interrupt to process
    }

    // Get interrupt flags
    clock_interrupt_t ints;
    esp_err_t ret = clock_get_interrupts(&ints);
    if (ret != ESP_OK || ints == CLOCK_INT_NONE) {
        return ret; // No valid interrupts
    }

    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "RTC interrupt detected, ints=0x%x", ints);

    // IMPORTANT: Check countdown timer BEFORE processing minute interrupt
    // Both share the TF flag, but minute interrupt processing clears it
    // We need to read timer value while TF is still set
    if (ints & CLOCK_INT_COUNTDOWN) {
        // Read timer value to determine if countdown expired (value will be 0)
        uint8_t timer_val = 0;
        esp_err_t timer_read_ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_VAL, &timer_val, 1);

        if (timer_read_ret == ESP_OK && clock_timer_is_active()) {
            uint8_t initial_value = clock_timer_get_value();

            // Expiration is judged against the host-side start timestamp
            // (esp_timer_get_time at enable), not the RTC register value: the
            // timer auto-reloads at 0 (re-setting TF every period) and the 1 Hz
            // source ticks once per second, so the register value alone cannot
            // distinguish "just expired" from "just started a while ago". The
            // old value-based heuristic (value >= initial - missed_ticks)
            // matched the *starting* value within the first poll and fired the
            // light->deep transition ~2 s after the countdown began.
            //
            // At 1 Hz the counter runs initial_value -> 1 -> 0(reload) per
            // period, so it has expired once at least (initial_value - 1)
            // seconds have elapsed; the -1 tolerates the 1 Hz tick quantization
            // and up to ~1.3 s of poll latency after expiry.
            int64_t elapsed_s = (esp_timer_get_time() - clock_timer_get_enabled_at_us()) / 1000000;
            int64_t expiry_s = (initial_value > 1) ? (initial_value - 1) : 0;

            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Countdown timer check: value=%d, elapsed=%llds, expiry>=%llds", timer_val,
                     (long long)elapsed_s, (long long)expiry_s);

            bool expired = (elapsed_s >= expiry_s);
            if (expired || timer_val == 0 || timer_val == 1) {
                // Countdown timer has expired (time-based, or caught at 0/1)
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Countdown timer expired (value=%d, elapsed=%llds) - triggering deep sleep transition",
                         timer_val, (long long)elapsed_s);

                // CRITICAL: Disable the timer first to prevent further restarts
                // The timer auto-restarts when TF is cleared if TE is still set
                esp_err_t disable_ret = clock_timer_disable();
                if (disable_ret != ESP_OK) {
                    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to disable countdown timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(disable_ret));
                }

                // Trigger countdown timer callback (e.g., transition to deep sleep)
                clock_trigger_countdown_timer();

                // Clear the TF flag
                clock_clear_interrupts(CLOCK_INT_COUNTDOWN);

                // Skip minute interrupt processing since we already cleared TF
                return ESP_OK;
            } else {
                // Countdown still running (elapsed < expiry), this TF is from the
                // minute interrupt
                ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Countdown timer still running (value=%d), will process MI", timer_val);
            }
        } else if (timer_read_ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to read timer value: %s", esp_err_to_name(timer_read_ret));
        }
    }

    // Handle minute interrupts (MI/HMI)
    if (ints & CLOCK_INT_MINUTE) {
        bool is_minute_tick = false;
        esp_err_t process_ret = clock_minute_process_interrupt(&is_minute_tick);

        if (process_ret == ESP_OK && is_minute_tick) {
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Minute interrupt processed - updating display");
            clock_trigger_time_update();
        } else if (process_ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to process minute interrupt: %s", esp_err_to_name(process_ret));
        }
        // Note: clock_minute_process_interrupt() clears TF flag internally
    }

    // Handle alarm interrupts separately
    if (ints & CLOCK_INT_ALARM) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Alarm interrupt triggered!");

        // Trigger alarm trigger callback (e.g. show alarm screen)
        clock_trigger_alarm_triggered();

        // Clear alarm flag
        esp_err_t clear_ret = clock_clear_interrupts(CLOCK_INT_ALARM);
        if (clear_ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear alarm flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(clear_ret));
        }

        // Schedule next alarm based on current time
        clock_time_t current_time;
        esp_err_t time_ret = clock_get_time(&current_time);
        if (time_ret == ESP_OK) {
            esp_err_t sched_ret = clock_alarm_schedule_next(&current_time);
            if (sched_ret == ESP_OK) {
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Next alarm scheduled successfully");
            } else {
                ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Failed to schedule next alarm: %s", esp_err_to_name(sched_ret));
            }
        } else {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get current time for alarm rescheduling: %s", esp_err_to_name(time_ret));
        }
    }

    return ESP_OK;
#endif // !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
}

esp_err_t clock_get_interrupts(clock_interrupt_t *out) {
    if (!out || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    uint8_t ctrl2;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &ctrl2, 1);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }

    *out = CLOCK_INT_NONE;

    // Check for TF (Timer Flag, bit 3) - set by MI, HMI, or countdown timer
    if (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_TF) {
        // Read Timer Mode register to check if countdown timer is enabled
        uint8_t timer_mode = 0;
        esp_err_t timer_ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE, &timer_mode, 1);

        // Check which interrupt sources are enabled
        bool mi_enabled = (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_MI) != 0;
        bool hmi_enabled = (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_HMI) != 0;
        // Countdown timer must have both TE (Timer Enable) AND TIE (Timer Interrupt Enable) set
        bool countdown_enabled = (timer_ret == ESP_OK) && (timer_mode & PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE_TE) != 0 &&
                                 (timer_mode & PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE_TIE) != 0;

        // Set appropriate interrupt flags based on what's enabled
        // Note: TF can be set by MI, HMI, or countdown timer
        if (mi_enabled || hmi_enabled) {
            *out |= CLOCK_INT_MINUTE;
        }
        if (countdown_enabled) {
            *out |= CLOCK_INT_COUNTDOWN;
        }

        // If TF is set but nothing is enabled, log a warning with details
        if (!mi_enabled && !hmi_enabled && !countdown_enabled) {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG,
                     "TF flag set but no interrupt source enabled (CTRL2=0x%02x, TIMER_MODE=0x%02x, MI=%d, HMI=%d, "
                     "TE=%d, TIE=%d)",
                     ctrl2, timer_mode, mi_enabled, hmi_enabled, (timer_mode & PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE_TE) != 0,
                     (timer_mode & PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE_TIE) != 0);
        }
    }

    // Check for alarm interrupt flag (AF)
    if (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AF) {
        *out |= CLOCK_INT_ALARM;
    }

    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t clock_clear_interrupts(clock_interrupt_t flags) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Clearing interrupt flags: 0x%x", flags);
    esp_err_t ret = ESP_OK;

    // Clear minute interrupt or countdown timer (both use TF flag)
    if ((flags & CLOCK_INT_MINUTE) || (flags & CLOCK_INT_COUNTDOWN)) {
        const char *int_type = (flags & CLOCK_INT_MINUTE) ? "MINUTE" : "COUNTDOWN";
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Clearing %s flag (TF)", int_type);
        esp_err_t timer_ret = pcf85063a_clear_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev);
        if (timer_ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear timer flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(timer_ret));
            ret = timer_ret;
        }
    }

    // Clear alarm interrupt
    if (flags & CLOCK_INT_ALARM) {
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Clearing ALARM flag (AF)");
        uint8_t ctrl2;
        esp_err_t alarm_ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &ctrl2, 1);
        if (alarm_ret == ESP_OK) {
            uint8_t ctrl2_before = ctrl2;
            ctrl2 &= ~PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AF;
            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Clearing AF: CTRL2 before=0x%02x, after=0x%02x (MI=%d->%d, HMI=%d->%d)", ctrl2_before, ctrl2,
                     (ctrl2_before & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_MI) != 0, (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_MI) != 0,
                     (ctrl2_before & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_HMI) != 0, (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_HMI) != 0);
            uint8_t write_buf[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, ctrl2};
            alarm_ret = pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_buf, 2);
        }
        if (alarm_ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear alarm flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(alarm_ret));
            ret = alarm_ret;
        }
    }

    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        // Check EXIO 3 pin status after clearing flags
        bool exio_int_active = false;
        if (s_io_expander) {
            uint32_t level_mask = 0;
            esp_err_t exio_ret = esp_io_expander_get_level(s_io_expander, EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN, &level_mask);
            if (exio_ret == ESP_OK) {
                // RTC interrupt is active low
                exio_int_active = (level_mask & EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN) == 0;
            }
        }
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Cleared interrupt flags - EXIO_INT=%d", exio_int_active);
    }

    return ret;
}

/**
 * @brief Check if RTC has pending interrupt flags
 *
 * This function checks the RTC's internal interrupt flags (TF and AF) to determine
 * if there are pending interrupts to process.
 *
 * Note on interrupt detection:
 * - MI/HMI pulses are only ~15ms wide (1/64 second)
 * - Countdown timer pulses depend on TI_TP setting
 * - With polling at 1.3s intervals, we'll miss the pulse but TF/AF flags stay set
 * - We check flags directly since they persist until software clears them
 * - Optional: Can check EXIO pin state, but not reliable for MI/HMI due to short pulse
 *
 * @return true if RTC has pending timer/alarm interrupt flags, false otherwise
 */
bool clock_is_interrupt_pending(void) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return false;
    }

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // No PCF85063A: there is no RTC flag register to poll. This is not
    // called on such builds (clock_handle_interrupts synthesizes the
    // software path directly), kept only so a stray call cannot log an I2C
    // error against a dead device.
    return false;
#endif

    // Check EXIO 3 pin level (useful for wake-up from deep sleep detection)
    bool exio_int_active = false;
    if (s_io_expander) {
        uint32_t level_mask = 0;
        esp_err_t exio_ret = esp_io_expander_get_level(s_io_expander, EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN, &level_mask);
        if (exio_ret == ESP_OK) {
            // RTC interrupt is active low
            exio_int_active = (level_mask & EXIO_RTC_INT_PIN) == 0;
        }
    }

    // Read RTC interrupt flags (TF and AF)
    // These flags are sticky - stay set until explicitly cleared by software
    uint8_t ctrl2;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &ctrl2, 1);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to read RTC CTRL2 for interrupt check: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return false;
    }

    // Check if RTC has any interrupt flags set
    // TF (bit 3): Timer Flag - set by MI, HMI, or countdown timer
    // AF (bit 6): Alarm Flag
    bool tf_flag = (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_TF) != 0;
    bool af_flag = (ctrl2 & PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_AF) != 0;

    if (tf_flag || af_flag) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "RTC interrupt flags detected - CTRL2=0x%02x, TF=%d, AF=%d, EXIO_INT=%d", ctrl2, tf_flag, af_flag,
                 exio_int_active);
        return true;
    }

    return false;
}

void clock_set_poll_interval_ms(uint32_t interval_ms) {
    s_rtc_poll_interval_ms = interval_ms;
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "RTC polling interval set to %lu ms", interval_ms);
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_minute.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_minute.h"
#include "pcf85063a.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_minute";

// External references from clock.c
extern pcf85063a_dev_t s_rtc_dev;
extern bool s_initialized;

// Track which minute interrupt is currently enabled
static clock_minute_int_type_t s_minute_int_type = CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE;

// P4 (no PCF85063A): the last wall-clock minute (UTC minutes since epoch)
// the poller observed. Rollover detection is exact: the poll interval
// (1.3 s) is far shorter than a minute, so at most one rollover can occur
// between two polls -- never missed, never doubled (an SNTP step changes
// the value by !=1 and is re-based, not fired, same as the S3's TF
// semantics for a written time).
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
static uint32_t s_last_seen_minute = 0;
static bool s_minute_base_initialized = false;
#endif

esp_err_t clock_minute_enable_interrupt(clock_minute_int_type_t type) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // Per datasheet: MI/HMI must only be used when MODE = 0 (normal mode)
    // Read Offset register to check/ensure MODE = 0
    uint8_t offset_reg = 0;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_OFFSET_ADDR, &offset_reg, 1);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to read Offset register: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Check if MODE bit is set (bit 7)
    if (offset_reg & PCF85063A_RTC_OFFSET_MODE) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Offset register in coarse mode (MODE=1), switching to normal mode (MODE=0) for MI/HMI");
        // Clear MODE bit to set normal mode
        offset_reg &= ~PCF85063A_RTC_OFFSET_MODE;
        uint8_t write_data[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_OFFSET_ADDR, offset_reg};
        ret = pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_data, sizeof(write_data));
        if (ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to set normal mode: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
            return ret;
        }
    }

    // Note: For consistent MI/HMI periods, OFFSET[6:0] should be 00h
    // Log warning if offset is non-zero
    uint8_t offset_value = offset_reg & 0x7F;
    if (offset_value != 0) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Offset value is 0x%02x (non-zero) - MI/HMI periods may be affected", offset_value);
    }

    // Read current Control_2 register
    uint8_t ctrl2_value = 0;
    ret = pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &ctrl2_value, 1);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to read Control_2 register: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Clear MI and HMI bits first
    ctrl2_value &= ~(PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_MI | PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_HMI);

    // Set appropriate bits based on type
    switch (type) {
    case CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE:
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Disabling minute interrupts");
        break;

    case CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_HALF:
        ctrl2_value |= PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_HMI;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Enabling half-minute interrupt (every 30 seconds)");
        break;

    case CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_FULL:
        ctrl2_value |= PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_MI;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Enabling minute interrupt (every 60 seconds)");
        break;

    default:
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid minute interrupt type: %d", type);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    // Write the updated Control_2 register
    uint8_t write_data[2] = {PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, ctrl2_value};
    ret = pcf85063a_write_register(&s_rtc_dev, write_data, sizeof(write_data));
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to write Control_2 register: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Update tracking variable
    s_minute_int_type = type;

    // Verify the register was set correctly
    uint8_t verify_value = 0;
    pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_CTRL_2_ADDR, &verify_value, 1);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Control_2 register verification: 0x%02x", verify_value);

    return ESP_OK;
#else
    // No PCF85063A MI/HMI bits: the minute tick is detected in software
    // by the interrupt poller (a wall-clock minute rollover since the last
    // poll; the 1.3 s poll interval can never straddle the same rollover
    // twice). Track the requested type so clock_minute_process_interrupt
    // can tell "minute interrupts enabled" from "disabled".
    if (type != CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE && type != CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_FULL && type != CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_HALF) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid minute interrupt type: %d", type);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    s_minute_int_type = type;
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Minute tick: software mode (no PCF85063A), type=%d", type);
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_minute_disable_interrupt(void) { return clock_minute_enable_interrupt(CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE); }

esp_err_t clock_minute_process_interrupt(bool *is_minute_tick) {
    if (!is_minute_tick || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    *is_minute_tick = false;

    // Check if minute interrupt is enabled
    if (s_minute_int_type == CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE) {
        return ESP_OK; // Not using minute interrupts
    }

    // Check for timer flag (TF)
    uint8_t timer_flag = 0;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_get_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev, &timer_flag);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to read timer flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // If timer flag is not set, this is not our interrupt
    if (!timer_flag) {
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    // Clear the timer flag (TF) by reading Control_2 and clearing the bit
    ret = pcf85063a_clear_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear timer flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Valid minute tick occurred
    *is_minute_tick = true;

    const char *int_type = (s_minute_int_type == CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_FULL) ? "minute" : "half-minute";
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Cleared TF flag for %s interrupt", int_type);

    return ESP_OK;
#else
    // Software minute tick: a wall-clock minute rollover since the last
    // poll. The system clock is the time base (SNTP-synced; the S3's PCF
    // TF flag is its analog), so the detection is exact -- the PCF and the
    // system clock are the same 32 kHz domain's seconds on each board.
    *is_minute_tick = false;

    if (s_minute_int_type == CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE) {
        return ESP_OK; // Not using minute interrupts
    }
    if (s_minute_int_type != CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_FULL) {
        // HMI (30 s) has no software analog: the display's seconds come
        // from the UI's 1 s lv_timer anyway. Re-base silently so a later
        // FULL enable starts clean.
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    uint32_t current_minute = (uint32_t)(time(NULL) / 60);
    if (!s_minute_base_initialized) {
        s_minute_base_initialized = true;
        s_last_seen_minute = current_minute;
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    int32_t delta = (int32_t)current_minute - (int32_t)s_last_seen_minute;
    if (delta == 1) {
        // The one real minute rollover since the last poll.
        s_last_seen_minute = current_minute;
        *is_minute_tick = true;
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Software minute rollover detected");
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    // Any other change is an SNTP/manual time SET (a small correction or a
    // resync), not a rollover: re-base without firing (the UI refreshes on
    // the sync path, matching the S3's TF semantics for a written time).
    if (delta != 0) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wall clock stepped by %d minute(s); re-basing minute tick without a tick", delta);
    }
    s_last_seen_minute = current_minute;

    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

clock_minute_int_type_t clock_minute_get_enabled_type(void) { return s_minute_int_type; }
```

### `components/clock/clock_sntp.c`

```c
/**
 * @file clock_sntp.c
 * @brief SNTP/NTP time synchronization for clock component
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/time.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "esp_err.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_sntp.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/event_groups.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"

#include "clock_sntp.h"
#include "clock_tz.h"
#include "settings_store.h"
#include "wifi.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_sntp";

#define SNTP_SYNC_BIT BIT0
static EventGroupHandle_t s_sntp_event_group = NULL;
static bool s_sntp_initialized = false;
static time_t s_last_sync_time = 0;

// Trust flag: the wall clock holds SNTP-verified (or manually entered)
// time. The S3's time base is the PCF85063A, which is self-trusting
// (the flag is unused there); on the P4 it gates the software alarm fire
// so the default/unsynced clock (2026-01-24 12:00) can never ring a
// phantom alarm, and it drives the UI's "unsynced" state.
static bool s_time_trusted = false;

// P4 (no PCF85063A): NVS epoch backup. A FULL POWER LOSS kills the crystal
// RTC domain (VBAT coverage is unverified on the 4C), and the crystal only
// keeps counting through the app-level sleep states (no esp_deep_sleep) --
// so the NVS snapshot is the only cross-power-loss memory of the wall
// clock. Saved on every SNTP success and every ~15 min (the minute tick);
// restored at boot in place of the 2026-01-24 default (and only then --
// the time is still NOT trusted: the flag stays down until the next SNTP
// sync or a manual entry, so the clock shows dim and no alarm can fire).
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
#include "nvs.h"

#define CLOCK_NVS_NAMESPACE "clock"
#define CLOCK_NVS_KEY_EPOCH "epoch"
// 15 min: tight enough that a power loss loses little, sparse enough
// that the NVS wear is negligible (one commit per quarter hour).
#define CLOCK_NVS_SAVE_INTERVAL_SEC 900

static time_t s_last_nvs_save = 0;

esp_err_t clock_nvs_save_epoch(void) {
    nvs_handle_t h;
    if (nvs_open(CLOCK_NVS_NAMESPACE, NVS_READWRITE, &h) != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "NVS open failed for the epoch backup");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    esp_err_t ret = nvs_set_i64(h, CLOCK_NVS_KEY_EPOCH, (int64_t)time(NULL));
    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        ret = nvs_commit(h);
    }
    nvs_close(h);
    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        s_last_nvs_save = time(NULL);
    }
    return ret;
}

// The minute tick's periodic save: only write when the interval has
// elapsed (a no-op ESP_OK otherwise, so the caller needs no bookkeeping).
esp_err_t clock_nvs_maybe_save_epoch(void) {
    if (s_last_nvs_save && (time(NULL) - s_last_nvs_save) < CLOCK_NVS_SAVE_INTERVAL_SEC) {
        return ESP_OK;
    }
    esp_err_t ret = clock_nvs_save_epoch();
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Periodic NVS epoch save failed: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }
    return ret;
}

// Restore the last snapshot into the system clock. Returns true (and the
// restored time is live) when a plausible snapshot was applied.
bool clock_nvs_restore_epoch(void) {
    nvs_handle_t h;
    if (nvs_open(CLOCK_NVS_NAMESPACE, NVS_READONLY, &h) != ESP_OK) {
        return false;
    }
    int64_t saved = 0;
    bool found = (nvs_get_i64(h, CLOCK_NVS_KEY_EPOCH, &saved) == ESP_OK);
    nvs_close(h);
    if (!found || saved < 1609459200) { // pre-2021-01-01 snapshots are junk
        return false;
    }
    struct timeval tv = {.tv_sec = (time_t)saved, .tv_usec = 0};
    if (settimeofday(&tv, NULL) != 0) {
        return false;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Restored wall clock from NVS backup (unsynced until NTP): %lld", (long long)saved);
    return true;
}
#endif

// Callback function called when SNTP sync is complete
static void sntp_sync_time_cb(struct timeval *tv) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "SNTP time synchronized");
    s_last_sync_time = tv->tv_sec;
    s_time_trusted = true;
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // The just-synced epoch is the most trusted value we hold: snapshot
    // it (force, ignoring the 15 min interval).
    if (clock_nvs_save_epoch() != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "NVS epoch save after SNTP sync failed");
    }
#endif
    if (s_sntp_event_group) {
        xEventGroupSetBits(s_sntp_event_group, SNTP_SYNC_BIT);
    }
}

esp_err_t clock_sntp_init(void) {
    if (s_sntp_initialized) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "SNTP already initialized");
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    // Set the timezone from the runtime selection (settings store; loaded
    // before clock_init in main). The default (no settings file yet) is the
    // Europe/Berlin entry = the Kconfig value, so a fresh boot is unchanged.
    const char *tz = clock_tz_string_for_index(settings_timezone_idx());
    setenv("TZ", tz ? tz : CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, 1);
    tzset();
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Timezone set to: %s (idx %d)", tz ? tz : CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, settings_timezone_idx());

    // Create event group for synchronization
    s_sntp_event_group = xEventGroupCreate();
    if (!s_sntp_event_group) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create SNTP event group");
        return ESP_ERR_NO_MEM;
    }

    s_sntp_initialized = true;
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "SNTP component initialized");
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t clock_sntp_sync(uint32_t timeout_ms) {
    if (!s_sntp_initialized) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "SNTP not initialized");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    // Check if WiFi is connected
    if (!wifi_manager_is_connected()) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "WiFi not connected, cannot sync time via NTP");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Starting SNTP time synchronization...");

    // Clear any previous sync bit
    if (s_sntp_event_group) {
        xEventGroupClearBits(s_sntp_event_group, SNTP_SYNC_BIT);
    }

    // Configure SNTP
    esp_sntp_setoperatingmode(SNTP_OPMODE_POLL);
    esp_sntp_setservername(0, CONFIG_CLOCK_NTP_SERVER);
    esp_sntp_set_time_sync_notification_cb(sntp_sync_time_cb);
    esp_sntp_init();

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Waiting for SNTP synchronization (timeout: %lu ms)...", timeout_ms);

    // Wait for synchronization with timeout
    EventBits_t bits =
        xEventGroupWaitBits(s_sntp_event_group, SNTP_SYNC_BIT, pdTRUE, pdFALSE, pdMS_TO_TICKS(timeout_ms));

    esp_sntp_stop();

    if (bits & SNTP_SYNC_BIT) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "SNTP synchronization successful");

        // Log the synchronized time
        time_t now;
        struct tm timeinfo;
        char strftime_buf[64];

        time(&now);
        localtime_r(&now, &timeinfo);
        strftime(strftime_buf, sizeof(strftime_buf), "%c", &timeinfo);
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Current local time: %s", strftime_buf);

        return ESP_OK;
    } else {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "SNTP synchronization timeout");
        return ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT;
    }
}

esp_err_t clock_sntp_get_system_time(clock_time_t *time_out) {
    if (!time_out) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    time_t now;
    struct tm timeinfo;

    time(&now);

    // P4: before falling back to the 2026-01-24 default, try the NVS
    // snapshot (a full power loss reset the crystal domain to its boot
    // default; the snapshot keeps the last known time). Still unsynced:
    // the trust flag is untouched either way.
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    if (now < 1609459200) { // Jan 1, 2021 timestamp
        if (clock_nvs_restore_epoch()) {
            time(&now);
        }
    }
#endif

    // If system time is invalid (epoch time), set a reasonable default
    if (now < 1609459200) { // Jan 1, 2021 timestamp
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "System time appears invalid, setting default time");

        // Set to January 24, 2026 12:00:00 CET
        timeinfo.tm_year = 2026 - 1900;
        timeinfo.tm_mon = 0; // January (0-based)
        timeinfo.tm_mday = 24;
        timeinfo.tm_hour = 12;
        timeinfo.tm_min = 0;
        timeinfo.tm_sec = 0;
        timeinfo.tm_isdst = -1;

        now = mktime(&timeinfo);
        struct timeval tv = {.tv_sec = now, .tv_usec = 0};
        settimeofday(&tv, NULL);

        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Set default system time to 2026-01-24 12:00:00");
    }

    localtime_r(&now, &timeinfo);

    // Convert to our clock format
    time_out->year = timeinfo.tm_year + 1900;
    time_out->month = timeinfo.tm_mon + 1;
    time_out->day = timeinfo.tm_mday;
    time_out->hour = timeinfo.tm_hour;
    time_out->minute = timeinfo.tm_min;
    time_out->second = timeinfo.tm_sec;

    return ESP_OK;
}

bool clock_sntp_needs_sync(void) {
    if (!s_sntp_initialized || s_last_sync_time == 0) {
        return true;
    }

    time_t now;
    time(&now);

    // Check if sync interval has elapsed
    uint32_t sync_interval_sec = CONFIG_CLOCK_NTP_SYNC_INTERVAL_HOURS * 3600;
    return (now - s_last_sync_time) > sync_interval_sec;
}

time_t clock_sntp_get_last_sync_time(void) { return s_last_sync_time; }

bool clock_sntp_time_trusted(void) { return s_time_trusted; }

// Set by the manual time-entry screen (P4) when the user commits a time
// with no network available.
void clock_sntp_set_time_trusted(bool trusted) { s_time_trusted = trusted; }

esp_err_t clock_sntp_deinit(void) {
    if (!s_sntp_initialized) {
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    if (esp_sntp_enabled()) {
        esp_sntp_stop();
    }

    if (s_sntp_event_group) {
        vEventGroupDelete(s_sntp_event_group);
        s_sntp_event_group = NULL;
    }

    s_sntp_initialized = false;
    s_last_sync_time = 0;
    s_time_trusted = false;

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "SNTP component deinitialized");
    return ESP_OK;
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_timer.c`

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_timer.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_timer.h"
#include "pcf85063a.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_timer";

// External references from clock.c
extern pcf85063a_dev_t s_rtc_dev;
extern bool s_initialized;

// Track current countdown timer configuration
static uint8_t s_countdown_timer_value = 0;
static bool s_countdown_timer_active = false;
static int64_t s_countdown_enabled_at_us = 0; /* host time the active countdown started */

// P4 (no PCF85063A): the countdown is an esp_timer one-shot. The one-shot
// fires in the esp_timer task context, where it may NOT run the UI callback
// (the S3 runs it from the LVGL task via the interrupt poll); it only sets
// this flag, which clock_interrupt.c's poll picks up and acts on -- the
// same context split as the S3's TF flag.
#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
static esp_timer_handle_t s_countdown_esp_timer = NULL;
static volatile bool s_countdown_expired_flag = false;

static void countdown_esp_timer_cb(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    s_countdown_expired_flag = true;
}
#endif

esp_err_t clock_timer_enable(uint8_t timer_seconds, uint8_t timer_mode) {
    if (!s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    if (timer_seconds == 0) {
        // Disable timer
        esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_disable_timer(&s_rtc_dev);
        if (ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to disable timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        } else {
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Timer disabled");
            s_countdown_timer_active = false;
            s_countdown_timer_value = 0;
            s_countdown_enabled_at_us = 0;
        }
        return ret;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Enabling timer (%d seconds, mode 0x%02x)", timer_seconds, timer_mode);

    // Reset the RTC timer state
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_disable_timer(&s_rtc_dev);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to disable timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    ret = pcf85063a_clear_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear timer flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Configure timer with specified settings
    ret = pcf85063a_set_timer_safe(&s_rtc_dev, timer_seconds, timer_mode);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to enable timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Timer enabled: %d seconds", timer_seconds);

    // Track timer configuration for expiration detection. The host-side
    // start timestamp is the expiration oracle: the PCF85063A's TF flag is
    // SHARED with the minute interrupt and the hardware timer auto-reloads
    // (re-setting TF every period), so the register value alone cannot tell
    // "just expired" from "just started a while ago" (see
    // clock_interrupt.c -- the old value-based heuristic misfired on the
    // first poll after a start).
    s_countdown_timer_value = timer_seconds;
    s_countdown_timer_active = true;
    s_countdown_enabled_at_us = esp_timer_get_time();

    // Verify timer was set correctly
    uint8_t verify_val, verify_mode;
    pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_VAL, &verify_val, 1);
    pcf85063a_read_register(&s_rtc_dev, PCF85063A_RTC_TIMER_MODE, &verify_mode, 1);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Timer verification - Value: %d, Mode: 0x%02x", verify_val, verify_mode);

    return ESP_OK;
#else
    (void)timer_mode;

    if (timer_seconds == 0) {
        // Disable the one-shot. esp_timer_stop() is idempotent; clearing
        // the flag here also cancels a one-shot that already fired but the
        // poller has not consumed yet (wake during the countdown).
        if (s_countdown_esp_timer) {
            esp_timer_stop(s_countdown_esp_timer);
        }
        s_countdown_expired_flag = false;
        s_countdown_timer_active = false;
        s_countdown_timer_value = 0;
        s_countdown_enabled_at_us = 0;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Countdown disabled (software)");
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    if (!s_countdown_esp_timer) {
        const esp_timer_create_args_t args = {
            .callback = countdown_esp_timer_cb,
            .name = "clock_countdown",
        };
        esp_err_t ret = esp_timer_create(&args, &s_countdown_esp_timer);
        if (ret != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create countdown esp_timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
            return ret;
        }
    }

    // (Re)arm: stop any previous one-shot, reset the flag, start fresh.
    esp_timer_stop(s_countdown_esp_timer);
    s_countdown_expired_flag = false;
    esp_err_t ret = esp_timer_start_once(s_countdown_esp_timer, (int64_t)timer_seconds * 1000000);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to start countdown esp_timer: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Countdown armed (software): %d seconds", timer_seconds);
    s_countdown_timer_value = timer_seconds;
    s_countdown_timer_active = true;
    s_countdown_enabled_at_us = esp_timer_get_time();

    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

esp_err_t clock_timer_disable(void) { return clock_timer_enable(0, 0); }

bool clock_timer_is_active(void) { return s_countdown_timer_active; }

uint8_t clock_timer_get_value(void) { return s_countdown_timer_value; }

int64_t clock_timer_get_enabled_at_us(void) { return s_countdown_enabled_at_us; }

esp_err_t clock_timer_process_interrupt(bool *is_timer_tick) {
    if (!is_timer_tick || !s_initialized) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    *is_timer_tick = false;

    // Check for timer flag
    uint8_t timer_flag = 0;
    esp_err_t ret = pcf85063a_get_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev, &timer_flag);
    if (ret != ESP_OK || !timer_flag) {
        // Not a timer interrupt or error reading flag
        return ret;
    }

    // Clear the timer flag
    ret = pcf85063a_clear_timer_flag(&s_rtc_dev);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to clear timer flag: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Valid timer tick
    *is_timer_tick = true;

    return ESP_OK;
#else
    // No PCF TF flag: the software countdown's expiration is the flag set
    // by the one-shot (see clock_timer_take_expired).
    *is_timer_tick = false;
    return ESP_OK;
#endif
}

bool clock_timer_take_expired(void) {
#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // The S3's poller judges expiration from the TF flag + the host-side
    // start timestamp; this flag is unused there.
    return false;
#else
    // Consume the one-shot's expiration flag (set from the esp_timer task).
    bool expired = s_countdown_expired_flag;
    s_countdown_expired_flag = false;
    return expired;
#endif
}
```

### `components/clock/clock_tz.c`

```c
/**
 * @file clock_tz.c
 * @brief Runtime timezone selection (see clock_tz.h).
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "clock.h"
#include "clock_alarm_scheduler.h"
#include "clock_tz.h"

static const char *TAG = "clock_tz";

int clock_tz_offset_minutes(int idx) {
    if (idx < 0 || idx >= CLOCK_TZ_FIXED_STEPS) {
        return -1;
    }
    /* idx 0 = -12:00, 30-minute steps. */
    return -720 + idx * 30;
}

const char *clock_tz_option_name(int idx) {
    static char buf[16];
    if (idx < 0 || idx >= CLOCK_TZ_COUNT) {
        return NULL;
    }
    if (idx == CLOCK_TZ_BERLIN_IDX) {
        return "Europe/Berlin";
    }
    int off = clock_tz_offset_minutes(idx); /* -720 .. +840 */
    int am = (off < 0) ? -off : off;
    snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "UTC%c%02d:%02d", off < 0 ? '-' : '+', am / 60, am % 60);
    return buf;
}

const char *clock_tz_string_for_index(int idx) {
    if (idx < 0 || idx >= CLOCK_TZ_COUNT) {
        return NULL;
    }
    if (idx == CLOCK_TZ_BERLIN_IDX) {
        return CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE;
    }
    static char buf[24];
    int off = clock_tz_offset_minutes(idx); /* -720 .. +840 */
    int am = (off < 0) ? -off : off;
    /* The POSIX TZ sign is the WEST offset (what to add to local to get
     * UTC) -- flipped relative to the east-of-UTC `off` here: the Kconfig
     * default proves it (CET is UTC+1, spelled "CET-1"). So UTC+02:00 is
     * "UTC-2" and UTC-05:30 is "UTC+5:30". */
    if (am % 60) {
        snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "UTC%c%d:%d", off > 0 ? '-' : '+', am / 60, am % 60);
    } else {
        snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "UTC%c%d", off > 0 ? '-' : '+', am / 60);
    }
    return buf;
}

esp_err_t clock_tz_apply(int idx) {
    const char *tz = clock_tz_string_for_index(idx);
    if (!tz) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "invalid timezone index %d", idx);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

#if CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
    // The PCF holds LOCAL digits: read them, convert to the UTC epoch under
    // the CURRENT (old) zone, switch the zone, re-derive the local digits
    // for the same moment and write them back. mktime must run before the
    // env var changes.
    clock_time_t t;
    esp_err_t ret = clock_get_time(&t);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        return ret;
    }
    struct tm tm;
    memset(&tm, 0, sizeof(tm));
    tm.tm_year = t.year - 1900;
    tm.tm_mon = t.month - 1;
    tm.tm_mday = t.day;
    tm.tm_hour = t.hour;
    tm.tm_min = t.minute;
    tm.tm_sec = t.second;
    tm.tm_isdst = -1;
    time_t epoch = mktime(&tm);
    if (epoch == (time_t)-1) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "epoch conversion failed for the current RTC time");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }
    setenv("TZ", tz, 1);
    tzset();
    struct tm nt;
    localtime_r(&epoch, &nt);
    clock_time_t nt2 = {nt.tm_year + 1900, nt.tm_mon + 1, nt.tm_mday, nt.tm_hour, nt.tm_min, nt.tm_sec};
    ret = clock_set_time(&nt2);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "rewriting the RTC digits for the new zone failed: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }
#else
    // The P4's time base is the system clock: the epoch is untouched, the
    // local digits re-derive from it through the new zone.
    setenv("TZ", tz, 1);
    tzset();
#endif

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "timezone applied: %s (%s)", clock_tz_option_name(idx), tz);

    // The next fire time (local time-of-day + weekday) depends on the zone:
    // re-arm from the new local time (S3: the PCF ALM; P4: the software
    // one-shot + cache).
    return clock_alarm_scheduler_reload();
}
```
