### `components/clock/include/clock.h`

```c
#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "bsp/esp-bsp.h"
#include "driver/gpio.h"
#include "driver/i2c_master.h"
#include "esp_err.h"
#include "esp_io_expander.h"
#include <time.h>

#include "clock_types.h"

// Include all specialized clock headers
#include "clock_alarm.h"
#include "clock_alarm_scheduler.h"
#include "clock_cb.h"
#include "clock_idle.h"
#include "clock_interrupt.h"
#include "clock_minute.h"
#include "clock_sntp.h"
#include "clock_timer.h"

/**
 * @brief Clock configuration structure
 */
typedef struct {
    // Configuration is minimal since BSP handles I2C
    bool enable_ntp_sync; // Enable automatic NTP time synchronization
} clock_config_t;

/**
 * @brief Initialize the clock component
 *
 * This function initializes the RTC and optionally synchronizes time via NTP.
 * If enable_ntp_sync is true and WiFi is available, it will attempt NTP synchronization.
 * Otherwise, it uses current system time. If RTC time appears invalid (before 2020),
 * it will be corrected automatically.
 *
 * @param cfg Clock configuration including NTP sync option
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_init(const clock_config_t *cfg);

/**
 * @brief One-shot NTP sync: sync the system clock, then update the RTC
 *
 * Used at boot (from clock_init) and by the on-demand sync flow (the
 * WiFi screen's background task). Requires a connected WiFi.
 *
 * @param timeout_ms SNTP wait timeout (ms)
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_sync_time_from_ntp(uint32_t timeout_ms);

/**
 * @brief Get current time from RTC
 *
 * @param out Pointer to store time
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_get_time(clock_time_t *out);

/**
 * @brief Get the current UTC epoch (seconds since 1970) from the RTC
 *
 * The RTC stores local (timezone/DST-adjusted) time; this converts it back
 * to a UTC epoch using the configured timezone so consumers (e.g. the moon
 * phase) can work in UTC. Returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE when the RTC time is
 * not a plausible calendar date, so the caller can show nothing rather than
 * a wrong value.
 *
 * @param out Pointer to store the epoch seconds
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_get_utc_epoch(int64_t *out);

/**
 * @brief Set RTC time
 *
 * @param time Time to set
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_set_time(const clock_time_t *time);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/include/clock_alarm_scheduler.h`

```c
#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "clock_types.h"
#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define MAX_ALARM_RULES 10

/**
 * @brief Alarm rule structure (cron-like)
 */
typedef struct {
    int minute;          // 0-59, or -1 for wildcard
    int hour;            // 0-23, or -1 for wildcard
    int minute_interval; // For */N syntax: trigger every N minutes (0 = disabled)
    int hour_interval;   // For */N syntax: trigger every N hours (0 = disabled)
    uint8_t day_mask;    // Bit mask for days: bit 0 = Sunday, bit 1 = Monday, etc.
    bool all_days;       // True if alarm should trigger every day
} alarm_rule_t;

/**
 * @brief Initialize alarm scheduler from SPIFFS
 *
 * Reads alarm.txt from SPIFFS and loads alarm rules.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Calculate and set the next alarm based on loaded rules
 *
 * Finds the next alarm time from current time based on all loaded rules,
 * and programs it into the RTC.
 *
 * @param current_time Current time to calculate next alarm from
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_schedule_next(const clock_time_t *current_time);

/**
 * @brief Get the number of loaded alarm rules
 *
 * @return int Number of alarm rules
 */
int clock_alarm_get_rule_count(void);

/**
 * @brief Get the next scheduled alarm time
 *
 * Returns the cached next alarm time that was scheduled.
 *
 * @param time Pointer to store the next alarm time
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success, ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if no alarm scheduled
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_get_next_scheduled(clock_time_t *time);

/**
 * @brief Write the alarm file (/spiffs/alarm.txt) with the given content
 *
 * The file is re-parsed by clock_alarm_scheduler_reload() after writing;
 * the writers below (set_pomodoro_interval / set_clock_alarm /
 * deactivate_all) do both in one call. All on the LVGL task, like the
 * RTC alarm poll -- no lock needed.
 *
 * @param content NUL-terminated cron rules (5 fields: minute hour dom month dow)
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_write(const char *content);

/**
 * @brief Re-parse the alarm file and reschedule the next alarm
 *
 * A file with no valid rules disarms the RTC alarm (the PCF85063A's
 * ALM register persists on the RTC, so a stale armed time would
 * otherwise fire a phantom alarm).
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success (incl. 0 rules -> disarmed)
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_scheduler_reload(void);

/**
 * @brief Bitmask of the kinds of loaded alarm rules
 *
 * Bit 0: an interval rule (star-slash-N minutes -- the pomodoro timer).
 * Bit 1: a fixed-time rule (HH:MM on selected days).
 *
 * @return uint8_t 0 when no rules are loaded
 */
```

### `components/clock/include/clock_interrupt.h`

```c
#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>

/**
 * @brief Clock interrupt types
 */
typedef enum {
    CLOCK_INT_NONE = 0,
    CLOCK_INT_MINUTE = 1 << 0,    // Minute interrupt (MI/HMI)
    CLOCK_INT_COUNTDOWN = 1 << 1, // Countdown timer interrupt
    CLOCK_INT_ALARM = 1 << 2,     // Alarm interrupt
} clock_interrupt_t;

/**
 * @brief Handle all RTC interrupts comprehensively
 *
 * This function checks for pending RTC interrupts and processes them appropriately.
 * It handles both timer and alarm interrupts, managing synchronization and clearing flags.
 * Callbacks are invoked directly for both timer and alarm interrupts.
 * Should be called from a polling timer or interrupt handler.
 *
 * @return ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_handle_interrupts(void);

/**
 * @brief Get pending interrupts
 *
 * @param out Pointer to store interrupt flags
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_get_interrupts(clock_interrupt_t *out);

/**
 * @brief Clear specific interrupt flags
 *
 * @param flags Interrupt flags to clear
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_clear_interrupts(clock_interrupt_t flags);

/**
 * @brief Check if RTC interrupt is active on EXIO 3
 *
 * @return true if interrupt line is low (active), false otherwise
 */
bool clock_is_interrupt_pending(void);

/**
 * @brief Set the polling interval for RTC interrupt detection
 *
 * This is used to calculate the countdown timer expiration threshold.
 * Should be called before starting countdown timers.
 *
 * @param interval_ms Polling interval in milliseconds
 */
void clock_set_poll_interval_ms(uint32_t interval_ms);

/**
 * @brief Arm the software alarm one-shot (no-PCF builds only)
 *
 * Arms an esp_timer one-shot for the epoch of the given local alarm time
 * (the analog of the PCF's ALM register + AIE). The one-shot only sets a
 * flag; the interrupt poll (LVGL task) consumes it and fires the alarm
 * callback. Called from clock_alarm_scheduler.c after each schedule, so
 * an SNTP/manual time SET that shifts the epoch re-arms it there.
 * A no-op returning ESP_OK on PCF builds (the hardware register is armed
 * by clock_set_alarm / clock_enable_alarm instead).
 *
 * @param next The scheduled alarm time (full date, local)
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_alarm_arm_esp_timer(const clock_time_t *next);

/**
 * @brief Disarm the software alarm one-shot (no-PCF builds only)
 *
 * Stops the one-shot and clears its fire flag (the 0-rules phantom
 * guard's P4 half). A no-op on PCF builds.
 */
void clock_alarm_disarm_esp_timer(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/include/clock_minute.h`

```c
#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/**
 * @brief Minute interrupt type
 */
typedef enum {
    CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_NONE = 0, ///< No minute interrupt
    CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_HALF = 1, ///< Half minute interrupt (every 30 seconds)
    CLOCK_MINUTE_INT_FULL = 2, ///< Full minute interrupt (every 60 seconds)
} clock_minute_int_type_t;

/**
 * @brief Enable minute or half-minute interrupt
 *
 * This function enables the RTC's built-in minute (MI) or half-minute (HMI) interrupt.
 * These interrupts run in sync with the seconds counter:
 * - MI generates an interrupt every 60 seconds (at seconds = 0)
 * - HMI generates an interrupt every 30 seconds (at seconds = 0 and 30)
 *
 * When starting MI, the first interrupt will be generated after 1-59 seconds.
 * When starting HMI, the first interrupt will be generated after 1-29 seconds.
 * Subsequent periods do not have such a delay.
 *
 * The interrupt pulse on INT pin is 1/64 seconds wide in normal mode.
 *
 * Note: Enabling both MI and HMI will result in interrupts every 30 seconds.
 * A minute interrupt on top of a half-minute interrupt is not distinguishable.
 *
 * @param type Type of minute interrupt to enable (NONE to disable both)
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_minute_enable_interrupt(clock_minute_int_type_t type);

/**
 * @brief Disable all minute interrupts
 *
 * Disables both MI and HMI interrupts.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_minute_disable_interrupt(void);

/**
 * @brief Process minute interrupt
 *
 * This function should be called from the interrupt handler when a timer flag
 * is detected. It verifies the flag is from MI/HMI and clears it.
 *
 * @param[out] is_minute_tick Set to true if this was a valid minute interrupt
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_minute_process_interrupt(bool *is_minute_tick);

/**
 * @brief Check which minute interrupt is currently enabled
 *
 * @return clock_minute_int_type_t Current minute interrupt type
 */
clock_minute_int_type_t clock_minute_get_enabled_type(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

```c
/**
 * @file clock_sntp.h
 * @brief SNTP/NTP time synchronization for clock component
 */

#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "clock_types.h"
#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <time.h>

/**
 * @brief Initialize SNTP component
 *
 * Sets up timezone from Kconfig and prepares SNTP for synchronization.
 * Must be called before other SNTP functions.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_sntp_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Synchronize time via SNTP/NTP
 *
 * Attempts to synchronize system time with configured NTP server.
 * Requires WiFi connection to be active.
 *
 * @param timeout_ms Maximum time to wait for synchronization
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success, ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT on timeout, ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE if WiFi not connected
 */
esp_err_t clock_sntp_sync(uint32_t timeout_ms);

/**
 * @brief Get current system time (timezone-adjusted)
 *
 * Returns current system time adjusted for the configured timezone.
 *
 * @param time_out Pointer to store the current time
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_sntp_get_system_time(clock_time_t *time_out);

/**
 * @brief Check if NTP synchronization is needed
 *
 * Returns true if no sync has been performed or if the sync interval has elapsed.
 *
 * @return bool true if sync is needed
 */
bool clock_sntp_needs_sync(void);

/**
 * @brief Get timestamp of last successful NTP sync
 *
 * @return time_t Unix timestamp of last sync, or 0 if never synced
 */
time_t clock_sntp_get_last_sync_time(void);

/**
 * @brief Check whether the wall clock holds trusted time
 *
 * Trusted = the last time written to the system clock came from a
 * successful SNTP sync or from the user's manual time entry. The S3's
 * time base is the PCF85063A (self-trusting; the flag is not consulted
 * there); on the P4 it gates the software alarm fire (a default/unsynced
 * clock must not ring a phantom alarm) and drives the UI's "unsynced"
 * display state.
 *
 * @return bool true once a trusted time source has been applied
 */
bool clock_sntp_time_trusted(void);

/**
 * @brief Mark the wall clock time as trusted (manual time entry)
 *
 * Called by the P4 manual time-entry screen when the user commits a time
 * with no network available.
 *
 * @param trusted true to mark the current wall clock as trusted
 */
void clock_sntp_set_time_trusted(bool trusted);

/**
 * @brief Deinitialize SNTP component
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_sntp_deinit(void);

#if !CONFIG_CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A
/**
 * @brief Snapshot the wall clock to NVS (P4, no external RTC IC)
 *
 * A full power loss kills the crystal RTC domain, so the NVS epoch is the
 * P4's only cross-power-loss memory of the time. Forced save; the 15 min
 * interval is handled by clock_nvs_maybe_save_epoch().
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_nvs_save_epoch(void);

/**
 * @brief Periodically snapshot the wall clock to NVS (P4)
 *
 * No-op (ESP_OK) when the 15 min interval has not elapsed. Called from
 * the software minute tick.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success (or when no save was due)
 */
esp_err_t clock_nvs_maybe_save_epoch(void);

/**
 * @brief Restore the last NVS snapshot into the system clock (P4)
 *
 * Applied only when the system clock is still at its pre-first-sync
 * default. The restored time is NOT trusted: the trust flag stays down
 * until the next SNTP sync or a manual entry.
 *
 * @return bool true when a plausible snapshot was applied
 */
bool clock_nvs_restore_epoch(void);
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/include/clock_timer.h`

```c
#pragma once

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

// Timer frequency constants (maps to TCF[1:0] bits in Timer Mode register)
#define CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_4096HZ (0x00) // 4.096 kHz timer source
#define CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_64HZ (0x08)   // 64 Hz timer source
#define CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_1HZ (0x10)    // 1 Hz timer source (most common)
#define CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_1_60HZ (0x18) // 1/60 Hz timer source

// Timer mode flags
#define CLOCK_TIMER_MODE_ENABLE_INT (0x02) // Enable timer interrupt (TIE bit)
#define CLOCK_TIMER_MODE_PULSE (0x01)      // Pulse mode vs level mode (TI_TP bit)

/**
 * @brief Enable/disable countdown timer with specified configuration
 *
 * On the PCF85063A build this enables the hardware countdown timer with
 * custom settings. On builds without the PCF85063A (CLOCK_USE_PCF85063A=n,
 * the P4) the countdown is an esp_timer one-shot of timer_seconds; the
 * timer_mode bits are accepted but ignored.
 * Pass 0 for timer_seconds to disable the timer.
 *
 * Common timer_mode configurations:
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_4096HZ: 4.096 kHz timer source
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_64HZ: 64 Hz timer source
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_1HZ: 1 Hz timer source (most common)
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_1_60HZ: 1/60 Hz timer source
 * Combine with:
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_MODE_ENABLE_INT: Enable timer interrupt
 * - CLOCK_TIMER_MODE_PULSE: Pulse mode (vs level mode)
 *
 * Example: timer_mode = CLOCK_TIMER_FREQ_1HZ | CLOCK_TIMER_MODE_ENABLE_INT
 *
 * @param timer_seconds Timer duration in seconds (0 to disable, 1-255 to enable)
 * @param timer_mode Timer configuration (clock frequency + interrupt settings)
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_timer_enable(uint8_t timer_seconds, uint8_t timer_mode);

/**
 * @brief Disable countdown timer
 *
 * Convenience function to disable the timer.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_timer_disable(void);

/**
 * @brief Check if countdown timer is currently active
 *
 * @return true if timer is enabled and running
 */
bool clock_timer_is_active(void);

/**
 * @brief Get the initial countdown timer value
 *
 * @return Initial timer value that was set, or 0 if timer is not active
 */
uint8_t clock_timer_get_value(void);

/**
 * @brief Get the host-side start time of the active countdown
 *
 * @return esp_timer_get_time() (µs) at the moment the countdown was enabled,
 *         or 0 if no countdown is active. This is the expiration oracle:
 *         the PCF85063A timer auto-reloads and the TF flag is shared with the
 *         minute interrupt, so the timer register value alone cannot
 *         distinguish "just expired" from "just started a while ago".
 */
int64_t clock_timer_get_enabled_at_us(void);

/**
 * @brief Process timer interrupt
 *
 * This function should be called from the interrupt handler when a timer flag
 * is detected. It verifies the flag, clears it, and indicates if this was a
 * valid timer interrupt.
 *
 * @param[out] is_timer_tick Set to true if this is a valid timer interrupt
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success
 */
esp_err_t clock_timer_process_interrupt(bool *is_timer_tick);

/**
 * @brief Consume the software countdown's expiration flag (P4 path)
 *
 * On builds without the PCF85063A the countdown's esp_timer one-shot sets
 * a flag when it fires (from the esp_timer task); the interrupt poller
 * (LVGL task) consumes it here before invoking the countdown callback.
 * Returns false immediately on the PCF build (its poller judges the TF
 * flag + host start timestamp instead).
 *
 * @return true if the countdown just expired (flag was set and is now cleared)
 */
bool clock_timer_take_expired(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/include/clock_tz.h`

```c
#pragma once

/**
 * @file clock_tz.h
 * @brief Runtime timezone selection (UTC offset + the Europe/Berlin default)
 *
 * The UI timezone screen offers one roller over every 30-minute UTC offset
 * (UTC-12:00 .. UTC+14:00) plus Europe/Berlin (the Kconfig default, with
 * DST) as the final entry. Applying an option rewrites the POSIX TZ env var
 * (+tzset), which is all the P4's system clock needs (the UTC epoch is
 * untouched, the local digits re-derive). The S3's PCF85063A stores LOCAL
 * digits, so the same moment is re-derived into the new zone's digits and
 * written back before the switch (epoch-consistent). The software/hardware
 * alarm arming is re-armed afterwards (the next fire time depends on the
 * zone). The selection persists via the settings store (timezone_idx); the
 * stored index is applied at SNTP init instead of the Kconfig default.
 */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "esp_err.h"

/* The option list: indices 0..52 = the fixed UTC offsets in 30-minute
 * steps from -12:00 (idx 0) to +14:00 (idx 52), index 53 = Europe/Berlin
 * (the Kconfig default, DST-aware). */
#define CLOCK_TZ_FIXED_STEPS 53
#define CLOCK_TZ_BERLIN_IDX (CLOCK_TZ_FIXED_STEPS)
#define CLOCK_TZ_COUNT (CLOCK_TZ_FIXED_STEPS + 1)

/* The fixed offset of option idx (0..52), in minutes EAST of UTC. */
int clock_tz_offset_minutes(int idx);

/* The human name of option idx ("UTC-12:00" .. "UTC+14:00",
 * "Europe/Berlin" for the default). Returns NULL for a bad idx. The
 * string is static storage (valid until the next call). */
const char *clock_tz_option_name(int idx);

/* The POSIX TZ string for option idx (fixed offsets use the sign-flipped
 * "UTC-2" / "UTC+5:30" form; Berlin uses CONFIG_CLOCK_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE).
 * Returns NULL for a bad idx. Static storage. */
const char *clock_tz_string_for_index(int idx);

/**
 * @brief Apply option idx as the active timezone.
 *
 * Epoch-consistent on both boards (see the file comment), then re-arms the
 * alarm arming from the new local time. The caller persists the selection
 * (settings store).
 */
esp_err_t clock_tz_apply(int idx);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/clock/include/settings_store.h`

```c
#pragma once

/**
 * @file settings_store.h
 * @brief Runtime settings persistence (/spiffs/settings.txt)
 *
 * The Kconfig values are the defaults; the settings screens (light-sleep,
 * deep-sleep) can change them at runtime and persist them across boots.
 * The file is RUNTIME-OWNED: it must not exist in spiffs/ (it would be
 * baked into storage.bin and clobbered on every full flash; a flash
 * resets the settings to the Kconfig defaults, which is the accepted
 * flow).
 *
 * File format: one "key = value" per line, '#' comments, blank lines and
 * unknown keys ignored (the same tolerance as the alarm.txt parsing).
 */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "esp_err.h"

/**
 * @brief Load the settings from /spiffs/settings.txt
 *
 * Missing file / parse failure: the Kconfig-seeded defaults are kept and
 * ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND / ESP_ERR_INVALID_DATA is returned. Call once at
 * boot, after the SPIFFS mount (wifi_manager_init) and before the
 * runtime consumers (clock_idle_set_timeout_ms, the countdown sites).
 */
esp_err_t settings_store_load(void);

/**
 * @brief Persist the current settings to /spiffs/settings.txt
 */
esp_err_t settings_store_save(void);

/* Idle timeout (main operation -> light sleep), seconds. Kconfig
 * CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC, range 10-300. */
uint32_t settings_idle_timeout_sec(void);
void settings_set_idle_timeout_sec(uint32_t sec);

/* Deep-sleep countdown (light sleep -> deep sleep), seconds. Kconfig
 * UI_DEEP_SLEEP_COUNTDOWN_SEC, range 10-300. */
uint32_t settings_deep_sleep_countdown_sec(void);
void settings_set_deep_sleep_countdown_sec(uint32_t sec);

/* Boot sweep animation on/off. Kconfig UI_MOON_ANIM_ENABLE. */
bool settings_boot_anim_enable(void);
void settings_set_boot_anim_enable(bool on);

/* Light-sleep "dusk" animation on/off. Kconfig UI_MOON_DUSK_ENABLE. */
bool settings_dusk_anim_enable(void);
void settings_set_dusk_anim_enable(bool on);

/* Timezone selection, the index into the clock_tz option list (clock_tz.h:
 * 0..52 = the fixed UTC offsets, 53 = Europe/Berlin = the default). */
int settings_timezone_idx(void);
void settings_set_timezone_idx(int idx);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

```c
/**
 * @file settings_store.c
 * @brief Runtime settings persistence (/spiffs/settings.txt)
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "clock_tz.h"
#include "settings_store.h"

static const char *TAG = "settings_store";
#define SETTINGS_PATH "/spiffs/settings.txt"

/* The two transition timeouts are user-facing in MINUTES (the settings
 * screens show a 1..30 minute picker). Stored internally in seconds:
 * 1 min .. 30 min = 60 .. 1800 s, default 1 min (60 s). */
#define SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC 60
#define SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC 1800

/* Kconfig-seeded defaults (#ifndef fallbacks for the Kconfig-`n`-leaves-
 * the-macro-undefined gotcha). */
#ifndef CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC
#define CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC 60
#endif
#ifndef CONFIG_UI_DEEP_SLEEP_COUNTDOWN_SEC
#define CONFIG_UI_DEEP_SLEEP_COUNTDOWN_SEC 60
#endif
#ifndef CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_ENABLE
#define CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_ENABLE 1
#endif
#ifndef CONFIG_UI_MOON_DUSK_ENABLE
#define CONFIG_UI_MOON_DUSK_ENABLE 1
#endif

static uint32_t s_idle_timeout_sec = CONFIG_CLOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC;
static uint32_t s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec = CONFIG_UI_DEEP_SLEEP_COUNTDOWN_SEC;
static bool s_boot_anim_enable = (CONFIG_UI_MOON_ANIM_ENABLE != 0);
static bool s_dusk_anim_enable = (CONFIG_UI_MOON_DUSK_ENABLE != 0);
static int s_timezone_idx = CLOCK_TZ_BERLIN_IDX; /* the Kconfig default zone */

/* Parse one "key = value" line into a numeric field; returns true when
 * the line is recognized (the value is validated by the caller). */
static bool parse_kv(const char *line, const char *key, long *out) {
    char k[32];
    const char *eq = strchr(line, '=');
    if (!eq || (size_t)(eq - line) >= sizeof(k))
        return false;
    memcpy(k, line, (size_t)(eq - line));
    k[eq - line] = 0;
    /* Trim trailing spaces in the key, leading spaces in the value. */
    size_t len = strlen(k);
    while (len > 0 && k[len - 1] == ' ')
        k[--len] = 0;
    if (strcmp(k, key) != 0)
        return false;
    char *end;
    long v = strtol(eq + 1, &end, 10);
    *out = v;
    return true;
}

esp_err_t settings_store_load(void) {
    FILE *f = fopen(SETTINGS_PATH, "r");
    if (!f) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG,
                 "no %s (or missing SPIFFS entry); using Kconfig defaults "
                 "(idle=%u s, countdown=%u s, boot_anim=%d, dusk_anim=%d, timezone_idx=%d)",
                 SETTINGS_PATH, (unsigned)s_idle_timeout_sec, (unsigned)s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec, s_boot_anim_enable,
                 s_dusk_anim_enable, s_timezone_idx);
        return ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND;
    }
    char line[128];
    long v;
    int lines = 0;
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
        lines++;
        if (line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '\n')
            continue;
        if (parse_kv(line, "idle_timeout_sec", &v) && v >= SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC && v <= SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC)
            s_idle_timeout_sec = (uint32_t)v;
        else if (parse_kv(line, "deep_sleep_countdown_sec", &v) && v >= SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC &&
                 v <= SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC)
            s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec = (uint32_t)v;
        else if (parse_kv(line, "boot_anim_enable", &v))
            s_boot_anim_enable = (v != 0);
        else if (parse_kv(line, "dusk_anim_enable", &v))
            s_dusk_anim_enable = (v != 0);
        else if (parse_kv(line, "timezone_idx", &v) && v >= 0 && v < CLOCK_TZ_COUNT)
            s_timezone_idx = (int)v;
        else if (lines < 9)
            ESP_LOGD(TAG, "unrecognized settings line: %s", line);
    }
    fclose(f);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "settings loaded (idle=%u s, countdown=%u s, boot_anim=%d, dusk_anim=%d, timezone_idx=%d)",
             (unsigned)s_idle_timeout_sec, (unsigned)s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec, s_boot_anim_enable, s_dusk_anim_enable,
             s_timezone_idx);
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t settings_store_save(void) {
    FILE *f = fopen(SETTINGS_PATH, "w");
    if (!f) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "cannot open %s for writing", SETTINGS_PATH);
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    int n = fprintf(f,
                    "# Runtime settings (owned by the settings screens; do not\n"
                    "# edit by hand -- a full flash resets this file).\n"
                    "idle_timeout_sec = %u\n"
                    "deep_sleep_countdown_sec = %u\n"
                    "boot_anim_enable = %d\n"
                    "dusk_anim_enable = %d\n"
                    "timezone_idx = %d\n",
                    (unsigned)s_idle_timeout_sec, (unsigned)s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec, s_boot_anim_enable,
                    s_dusk_anim_enable, s_timezone_idx);
    fclose(f);
    if (n < 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "settings write failed");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "settings saved (idle=%u s, countdown=%u s, boot_anim=%d, dusk_anim=%d, timezone_idx=%d)",
             (unsigned)s_idle_timeout_sec, (unsigned)s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec, s_boot_anim_enable, s_dusk_anim_enable,
             s_timezone_idx);
    return ESP_OK;
}

uint32_t settings_idle_timeout_sec(void) { return s_idle_timeout_sec; }

void settings_set_idle_timeout_sec(uint32_t sec) {
    if (sec < SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC)
        sec = SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC;
    if (sec > SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC)
        sec = SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC;
    s_idle_timeout_sec = sec;
}

uint32_t settings_deep_sleep_countdown_sec(void) { return s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec; }

void settings_set_deep_sleep_countdown_sec(uint32_t sec) {
    if (sec < SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC)
        sec = SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MIN_SEC;
    if (sec > SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC)
        sec = SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MAX_SEC;
    s_deep_sleep_countdown_sec = sec;
}

bool settings_boot_anim_enable(void) { return s_boot_anim_enable; }

void settings_set_boot_anim_enable(bool on) { s_boot_anim_enable = on; }

bool settings_dusk_anim_enable(void) { return s_dusk_anim_enable; }

void settings_set_dusk_anim_enable(bool on) { s_dusk_anim_enable = on; }

int settings_timezone_idx(void) { return s_timezone_idx; }

void settings_set_timezone_idx(int idx) {
    if (idx < 0 || idx >= CLOCK_TZ_COUNT)
        return;
    s_timezone_idx = idx;
}
```

```ini
# S3-only component: unregistered on other targets (the P4 build uses the
# registry waveshare/esp32_p4_wifi6_touch_lcd_xc instead; an unregistered
# component is harmlessly skipped — its Kconfig is not processed and no
# component REQUIRES it there).

idf_component_register(
    SRCS "esp32_s3_touch_amoled_1_75.c" ${SRC_VER}
    INCLUDE_DIRS "include" "include/bsp"
    PRIV_INCLUDE_DIRS "priv_include"
    REQUIRES driver esp_driver_i2c esp_driver_gpio esp_lcd
    PRIV_REQUIRES esp_timer spiffs esp_psram fatfs usb
)
endif()
```

```c
/**************************************************************************************************
 *

 **************************************************************************************************/
esp_err_t bsp_i2c_init(void) {
    /* I2C was initialized before */
    if (i2c_initialized) {
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    i2c_master_bus_config_t i2c_bus_conf = {
        .clk_source = I2C_CLK_SRC_DEFAULT,
        .sda_io_num = BSP_I2C_SDA,
        .scl_io_num = BSP_I2C_SCL,
        .i2c_port = BSP_I2C_NUM,
    };
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(i2c_new_master_bus(&i2c_bus_conf, &i2c_handle));

    i2c_initialized = true;

    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t bsp_i2c_deinit(void) {
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(i2c_del_master_bus(i2c_handle));
    i2c_initialized = false;
    return ESP_OK;
}

i2c_master_bus_handle_t bsp_i2c_get_handle(void) {
    bsp_i2c_init();
    return i2c_handle;
}

esp_err_t bsp_spiffs_mount(void) {
    esp_vfs_spiffs_conf_t conf = {
        .base_path = CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_MOUNT_POINT,
        .partition_label = CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_PARTITION_LABEL,
        .max_files = CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_MAX_FILES,
#ifdef CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_FORMAT_ON_MOUNT_FAIL
        .format_if_mount_failed = true,
#else
        .format_if_mount_failed = false,
#endif
    };

    esp_err_t ret_val = esp_vfs_spiffs_register(&conf);

    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(ret_val);

    size_t total = 0, used = 0;
    ret_val = esp_spiffs_info(conf.partition_label, &total, &used);
    if (ret_val != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to get SPIFFS partition information (%s)", esp_err_to_name(ret_val));
    } else {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Partition size: total: %d, used: %d", total, used);
    }

    return ret_val;
}

esp_err_t bsp_spiffs_unmount(void) { return esp_vfs_spiffs_unregister(CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_PARTITION_LABEL); }

esp_err_t bsp_sdcard_mount(void) {

#ifdef CONFIG_BSP_SD_FORMAT_ON_MOUNT_FAIL
        .format_if_mount_failed = true,
#else

#endif

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * I2S Audio Function
 *
 **************************************************************************************************/
esp_err_t bsp_audio_init(const i2s_std_config_t *i2s_config) {
    esp_err_t ret = ESP_FAIL;
    if (i2s_tx_chan && i2s_rx_chan) {
        /* Audio was initialized before */
        return ESP_OK;
    }

    /* Setup I2S peripheral */
    i2s_chan_config_t chan_cfg = I2S_CHANNEL_DEFAULT_CONFIG(CONFIG_BSP_I2S_NUM, I2S_ROLE_MASTER);
    chan_cfg.auto_clear = true; // Auto clear the legacy data in the DMA buffer
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(i2s_new_channel(&chan_cfg, &i2s_tx_chan, &i2s_rx_chan));

    /* Setup I2S channels */
    const i2s_std_config_t std_cfg_default = BSP_I2S_DUPLEX_MONO_CFG(22050);
    const i2s_std_config_t *p_i2s_cfg = &std_cfg_default;
    if (i2s_config != NULL) {
        p_i2s_cfg = i2s_config;
    }

    if (i2s_tx_chan != NULL) {
        ESP_GOTO_ON_ERROR(i2s_channel_init_std_mode(i2s_tx_chan, p_i2s_cfg), err, TAG,
                          "I2S channel initialization failed");
        ESP_GOTO_ON_ERROR(i2s_channel_enable(i2s_tx_chan), err, TAG, "I2S enabling failed");
    }
    if (i2s_rx_chan != NULL) {
        ESP_GOTO_ON_ERROR(i2s_channel_init_std_mode(i2s_rx_chan, p_i2s_cfg), err, TAG,
                          "I2S channel initialization failed");
        ESP_GOTO_ON_ERROR(i2s_channel_enable(i2s_rx_chan), err, TAG, "I2S enabling failed");
    }

    audio_codec_i2s_cfg_t i2s_cfg = {
        .port = CONFIG_BSP_I2S_NUM,
        .rx_handle = i2s_rx_chan,
        .tx_handle = i2s_tx_chan,
    };
    i2s_data_if = audio_codec_new_i2s_data(&i2s_cfg);
    BSP_NULL_CHECK_GOTO(i2s_data_if, err);

    return ESP_OK;

err:
    if (i2s_tx_chan) {
        i2s_del_channel(i2s_tx_chan);
    }
    if (i2s_rx_chan) {
        i2s_del_channel(i2s_rx_chan);
    }

    return ret;
}

esp_codec_dev_handle_t bsp_audio_codec_speaker_init(void) {
    if (i2s_data_if == NULL) {
        /* Initilize I2C */
        BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_i2c_init());
        /* Configure I2S peripheral and Power Amplifier */
        BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_audio_init(NULL));
    }
    assert(i2s_data_if);

    const audio_codec_gpio_if_t *gpio_if = audio_codec_new_gpio();

    audio_codec_i2c_cfg_t i2c_cfg = {
        .port = BSP_I2C_NUM,
        .addr = ES8311_CODEC_DEFAULT_ADDR,
        .bus_handle = i2c_handle,
    };
    const audio_codec_ctrl_if_t *i2c_ctrl_if = audio_codec_new_i2c_ctrl(&i2c_cfg);
    BSP_NULL_CHECK(i2c_ctrl_if, NULL);

    esp_codec_dev_hw_gain_t gain = {
        .pa_voltage = 5.0,
        .codec_dac_voltage = 3.3,
    };

    es8311_codec_cfg_t es8311_cfg = {
        .ctrl_if = i2c_ctrl_if,
        .gpio_if = gpio_if,
        .codec_mode = ESP_CODEC_DEV_WORK_MODE_DAC,
        .pa_pin = BSP_POWER_AMP_IO,
        .pa_reverted = false,
        .master_mode = false,
        .use_mclk = true,
        .digital_mic = false,
        .invert_mclk = false,
        .invert_sclk = false,
        .hw_gain = gain,
    };
    const audio_codec_if_t *es8311_dev = es8311_codec_new(&es8311_cfg);
    BSP_NULL_CHECK(es8311_dev, NULL);

    esp_codec_dev_cfg_t codec_dev_cfg = {
        .dev_type = ESP_CODEC_DEV_TYPE_OUT,
        .codec_if = es8311_dev,
        .data_if = i2s_data_if,
    };
    return esp_codec_dev_new(&codec_dev_cfg);
}

esp_codec_dev_handle_t bsp_audio_codec_microphone_init(void) {
    if (i2s_data_if == NULL) {
        /* Initilize I2C */
        BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_i2c_init());
        /* Configure I2S peripheral and Power Amplifier */
        BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_audio_init(NULL));
    }
    assert(i2s_data_if);

    audio_codec_i2c_cfg_t i2c_cfg = {
        .port = BSP_I2C_NUM,
        .addr = BSP_ES7210_CODEC_ADDR,
        .bus_handle = i2c_handle,
    };
    const audio_codec_ctrl_if_t *i2c_ctrl_if = audio_codec_new_i2c_ctrl(&i2c_cfg);
    BSP_NULL_CHECK(i2c_ctrl_if, NULL);

    es7210_codec_cfg_t es7210_cfg = {
        .ctrl_if = i2c_ctrl_if,
    };
    const audio_codec_if_t *es7210_dev = es7210_codec_new(&es7210_cfg);
    BSP_NULL_CHECK(es7210_dev, NULL);

    esp_codec_dev_cfg_t codec_es7210_dev_cfg = {
        .dev_type = ESP_CODEC_DEV_TYPE_IN,
        .codec_if = es7210_dev,
        .data_if = i2s_data_if,
    };
    return esp_codec_dev_new(&codec_es7210_dev_cfg);
}

#define LCD_CMD_BITS (8)
#define LCD_PARAM_BITS (8)
#define LCD_LEDC_CH (CONFIG_BSP_DISPLAY_BRIGHTNESS_LEDC_CH)
#define LVGL_TICK_PERIOD_MS (CONFIG_BSP_DISPLAY_LVGL_TICK)
#define LVGL_MAX_SLEEP_MS (CONFIG_BSP_DISPLAY_LVGL_MAX_SLEEP)

esp_err_t bsp_display_brightness_init(void) {
    bsp_display_brightness_set(100);
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t bsp_display_brightness_set(int brightness_percent) {
    if (panel_handle == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Panel handle is not initialized");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    if (brightness_percent < 0 || brightness_percent > 100) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid brightness percentage. Should be between 0 and 100.");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    brightness = (uint8_t)(brightness_percent * 255 / 100);

    uint32_t lcd_cmd = 0x51;
    lcd_cmd &= 0xff;
    lcd_cmd <<= 8;
    lcd_cmd |= 0x02 << 24;
    uint8_t param = brightness;
    esp_lcd_panel_io_tx_param(io_handle, lcd_cmd, &param, 1);

    return ESP_OK;
}

int bsp_display_brightness_get(void) {
    if (panel_handle == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Panel handle is not initialized");
        return -1;
    }

    return brightness * 100 / 255;
}

esp_err_t bsp_display_backlight_off(void) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Backlight off");
    return bsp_display_brightness_set(0);
}

esp_err_t bsp_display_backlight_on(void) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Backlight on");
    return bsp_display_brightness_set(100);
}
#if LVGL_VERSION_MAJOR >= 9
static void rounder_event_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
    lv_area_t *area = (lv_area_t *)lv_event_get_param(e);
    uint16_t x1 = area->x1;
    uint16_t x2 = area->x2;

    uint16_t y1 = area->y1;
    uint16_t y2 = area->y2;

    // round the start of coordinate down to the nearest 2M number
    area->x1 = (x1 >> 1) << 1;
    area->y1 = (y1 >> 1) << 1;
    // round the end of coordinate up to the nearest 2N+1 number
    area->x2 = ((x2 >> 1) << 1) + 1;
    area->y2 = ((y2 >> 1) << 1) + 1;
}
#else
static void bsp_lvgl_rounder_cb(lv_disp_drv_t *disp_drv, lv_area_t *area) {
    uint16_t x1 = area->x1;
    uint16_t x2 = area->x2;

    uint16_t y1 = area->y1;
    uint16_t y2 = area->y2;

    // round the start of coordinate down to the nearest 2M number
    area->x1 = (x1 >> 1) << 1;
    area->y1 = (y1 >> 1) << 1;
    // round the end of coordinate up to the nearest 2N+1 number
    area->x2 = ((x2 >> 1) << 1) + 1;
    area->y2 = ((y2 >> 1) << 1) + 1;
}
#endif
esp_err_t bsp_display_new(const bsp_display_config_t *config, esp_lcd_panel_handle_t *ret_panel,
                          esp_lcd_panel_io_handle_t *ret_io) {
    esp_err_t ret = ESP_OK;
    assert(config != NULL && config->max_transfer_sz > 0);

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Initialize SPI bus");
    const spi_bus_config_t buscfg = CO5300_PANEL_BUS_QSPI_CONFIG(BSP_LCD_PCLK, BSP_LCD_DATA0, BSP_LCD_DATA1,
                                                                 BSP_LCD_DATA2, BSP_LCD_DATA3, config->max_transfer_sz);
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(spi_bus_initialize(BSP_LCD_SPI_NUM, &buscfg, SPI_DMA_CH_AUTO));

    esp_lcd_panel_io_spi_config_t io_config = CO5300_PANEL_IO_QSPI_CONFIG(BSP_LCD_CS, NULL, NULL);
    io_config.trans_queue_depth = CONFIG_BSP_LCD_TRANS_QUEUE_DEPTH;
    co5300_vendor_config_t vendor_config = {
        .init_cmds = lcd_init_cmds,
        .init_cmds_size = sizeof(lcd_init_cmds) / sizeof(lcd_init_cmds[0]),
        .flags =
            {
                .use_qspi_interface = 1,
            },
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_lcd_new_panel_io_spi((esp_lcd_spi_bus_handle_t)BSP_LCD_SPI_NUM, &io_config, &io_handle));
    const esp_lcd_panel_dev_config_t panel_config = {
        .reset_gpio_num = BSP_LCD_RST,
        .rgb_ele_order = LCD_RGB_ELEMENT_ORDER_RGB,
        .bits_per_pixel = BSP_LCD_BITS_PER_PIXEL,
        .vendor_config = &vendor_config,
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_lcd_new_panel_co5300(io_handle, &panel_config, &panel_handle));
    esp_lcd_panel_set_gap(panel_handle, 0x06, 0);
    esp_lcd_panel_reset(panel_handle);
    esp_lcd_panel_init(panel_handle);
    esp_lcd_panel_disp_on_off(panel_handle, true);

    if (ret_panel) {
        *ret_panel = panel_handle;
    }
    if (ret_io) {
        *ret_io = io_handle;
    }
    return ret;
}

esp_err_t bsp_touch_new(const bsp_display_cfg_t *cfg, esp_lcd_touch_handle_t *ret_touch) {
    assert(cfg != NULL);
    /* Initilize I2C */
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(bsp_i2c_init());

    /* Initialize touch */
    const esp_lcd_touch_config_t tp_cfg = {
        .x_max = BSP_LCD_H_RES,
        .y_max = BSP_LCD_V_RES,
        .rst_gpio_num = BSP_LCD_TOUCH_RST, // Shared with LCD reset
        .int_gpio_num = BSP_LCD_TOUCH_INT,
        .levels =
            {
                .reset = 0,
                .interrupt = 0,
            },
        .flags =
            {
                .swap_xy = cfg->touch_flags.swap_xy,
                .mirror_x = cfg->touch_flags.mirror_x,
                .mirror_y = cfg->touch_flags.mirror_y,
            },
    };
    esp_lcd_panel_io_handle_t tp_io_handle = NULL;
    esp_lcd_panel_io_i2c_config_t tp_io_config = ESP_LCD_TOUCH_IO_I2C_CST9217_CONFIG();
    tp_io_config.scl_speed_hz = CONFIG_BSP_I2C_CLK_SPEED_HZ;
    ESP_RETURN_ON_ERROR(esp_lcd_new_panel_io_i2c(i2c_handle, &tp_io_config, &tp_io_handle), TAG, "");
    return esp_lcd_touch_new_i2c_cst9217(tp_io_handle, &tp_cfg, ret_touch);
}

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * IO Expander Function
 *
 **************************************************************************************************/
esp_io_expander_handle_t bsp_io_expander_init(void) {
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(bsp_i2c_init());
    if (!io_expander) {
        BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(
            esp_io_expander_new_i2c_tca9554(i2c_handle, BSP_IO_EXPANDER_I2C_ADDRESS, &io_expander));
    }
    return io_expander;
}

static lv_display_t *bsp_display_lcd_init(const bsp_display_cfg_t *cfg) {
    assert(cfg != NULL);
    const bsp_display_config_t disp_config = {
        /* 466 x 25 x 2 -- the LVGL flush strip, NOT the full panel. The S3's
         * PSRAM is not SPI-DMA-capable, so every QSPI chunk is staged through
         * internal RAM, and the largest DMA-capable free block is ~31 KiB
         * (see the buffer_height 50 -> 25 fix below): at the full-panel size
         * the io driver's 32 KiB chunking would stage one 32 KiB internal
         * alloc that does not fit -> ESP_ERR_NO_MEM. At 23,300 B every chunk
         * stages like the proven LVGL strips (and the 23,300 B flush strips
         * stay single-transaction, byte-identical), and the spin's single
         * 400x400 window write -- one CASET+RASET, CS held between chunks;
         * the 16-strip variant left a visible seam line at every 25-row
         * strip boundary (2026-11-01) -- streams as 14 such chunks. */
        .max_transfer_sz = BSP_LCD_H_RES * 25 * BSP_LCD_BITS_PER_PIXEL / 8,
    };

    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_display_new(&disp_config, &panel_handle, &io_handle));

    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Add LCD screen");
    esp_lv_adapter_display_config_t disp_cfg = {
        .panel = panel_handle,
        .panel_io = io_handle,
        .profile =
            {
                .interface = ESP_LV_ADAPTER_PANEL_IF_OTHER,
                .rotation = cfg->rotation,
                .hor_res = BSP_LCD_H_RES,
                .ver_res = BSP_LCD_V_RES,
                /* 25 rows instead of the upstream 50: the draw buffer is PSRAM
                 * (use_psram=true), and on this board PSRAM is NOT DMA-capable
                 * for SPI2_HOST (esp_ptr_dma_capable() is false below
                 * SOC_DMA_LOW=0x3FC88000). So esp_driver_spi's setup_priv_desc
                 * stages every flush strip into an internal-RAM DMA copy of the
                 * chunk, and an S3 SPI DMA transaction is capped at 32 KiB
                 * (SPI_LL_DMA_MAX_BIT_LEN=1<<18). A 50-row strip is 466*50*2 =
                 * 46.6 KiB -> 32 KiB first chunk -> a 32 KiB internal malloc
                 * that does not fit the largest DMA-capable free block
                 * (~31 KiB) -> ESP_ERR_NO_MEM on every full-panel flush.
                 * 25 rows -> 23.3 KiB strip -> single 23.3 KiB staging copy,
                 * which fits with margin. Bandwidth cost is negligible: the
                 * QSPI pclk and panel write rate are unchanged, only the
                 * per-transaction command overhead goes up slightly. */
                .buffer_height = 25,
                .use_psram = true,
                .enable_ppa_accel = false,
                .require_double_buffer = true,
            },
        .tear_avoid_mode = cfg->tear_avoid_mode,
    };

    lv_display_t *disp = esp_lv_adapter_register_display(&disp_cfg);
    if (!disp) {
        return NULL;
    }

#if LVGL_VERSION_MAJOR >= 9
    lv_display_add_event_cb(disp, rounder_event_cb, LV_EVENT_INVALIDATE_AREA, NULL);
#else
    lv_disp_t *disp_v8 = (lv_disp_t *)disp;
    if (disp_v8 && disp_v8->driver) {
        disp_v8->driver->rounder_cb = bsp_lvgl_rounder_cb;
    }
#endif

    return disp;
}

static lv_indev_t *bsp_display_indev_init(const bsp_display_cfg_t *cfg, lv_display_t *disp) {
    assert(cfg != NULL);
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_touch_new(cfg, &tp));
    assert(tp);

    const esp_lv_adapter_touch_config_t touch_cfg = ESP_LV_ADAPTER_TOUCH_DEFAULT_CONFIG(disp, tp);

    return esp_lv_adapter_register_touch(&touch_cfg);
}
/**********************************************************************************************************
 *
 * Display Function
 *
 **********************************************************************************************************/
lv_display_t *bsp_display_start(void) {
    bsp_display_cfg_t cfg = {.lv_adapter_cfg = ESP_LV_ADAPTER_DEFAULT_CONFIG(),
                             .rotation = ESP_LV_ADAPTER_ROTATE_0,
                             .tear_avoid_mode = ESP_LV_ADAPTER_TEAR_AVOID_MODE_NONE,
                             .touch_flags = {.swap_xy = 0, .mirror_x = 1, .mirror_y = 1}};
    return bsp_display_start_with_config(&cfg);
}

lv_display_t *bsp_display_start_with_config(bsp_display_cfg_t *cfg) {
    lv_display_t *disp;

    assert(cfg != NULL);
    /* Pin the LVGL task to core 0. The adapter default (core -1, no
     * affinity) lets FreeRTOS park it on core 1, where the moon bake
     * producer (pinned core 1, priority configMAX_PRIORITIES - 3)
     * starves it for the whole ~2 min boot animation: the producer's
     * 1 ms yields only go to idle, never to the lower-priority LVGL
     * task, so the 50 ms moon tick (strip display + the animation's
     * catch-up guard) stops running and the sweep shows nothing. Core
     * 0 keeps the LVGL task responsive on the other core, which is the
     * design the moon pipeline relies on (components/ui/moon_ui.c). */
    cfg->lv_adapter_cfg.task_core_id = 0;
    /* Pace the LVGL task on the 10 ms UI tick, not the 1 ms adapter
     * default. The loop sleeps on lv_timer_handler()'s return clamped to
     * [task_min_delay_ms, task_max_delay_ms] via vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS)
     * -- and this build runs FreeRTOS at 100 Hz ticks
     * (CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=100), so the default 1 ms floor is
     * pdMS_TO_TICKS(1) == 0 ticks: vTaskDelay(0) yields instead of
     * sleeping. Whenever the shortest live LVGL timer's remaining time is
     * < 10 ms (i.e. almost every pass, right after the 10 ms UI tick
     * fires) the loop spins at ~3500 Hz and the lvgl task burns ~95 % of
     * core 0 on static screens (measured: the "30 % CPU at idle" report).
     * A 10 ms floor makes the floor 1 real tick, so the task sleeps on
     * the UI tick's cadence (<= 100 Hz) when nothing is dirty. Touch
     * latency cost is <= 10 ms (the indev read timer is 33 ms anyway);
     * the 50 ms moon tick and the 1 s timers are unaffected. */
    cfg->lv_adapter_cfg.task_min_delay_ms = 10;
    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(esp_lv_adapter_init(&cfg->lv_adapter_cfg));

    BSP_NULL_CHECK(disp = bsp_display_lcd_init(cfg), NULL);

    BSP_NULL_CHECK(disp_indev = bsp_display_indev_init(cfg, disp), NULL);

    BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(bsp_display_brightness_init());

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_lv_adapter_start());

    return disp;
}

lv_indev_t *bsp_display_get_input_dev(void) { return disp_indev; }

esp_lcd_panel_handle_t bsp_display_get_panel(void) { return panel_handle; }

esp_err_t bsp_display_rotation_set(bsp_display_rotation_t rotation) {
    if (panel_handle == NULL || io_handle == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Panel or IO handle is not initialized");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    uint8_t madctl = 0x00;

    switch (rotation) {
    case BSP_DISPLAY_ROTATE_0:
        madctl = 0x00;
        break;
    case BSP_DISPLAY_ROTATE_90:
        madctl = 0x60;
        break;
    case BSP_DISPLAY_ROTATE_180:
        madctl = 0xC0;
        break;
    case BSP_DISPLAY_ROTATE_270:
        madctl = 0xA0;
        break;
    default:
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Invalid rotation value: %d", rotation);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }

    uint32_t lcd_cmd = 0x36;
    lcd_cmd &= 0xff;
    lcd_cmd <<= 8;
    lcd_cmd |= 0x02 << 24;

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Set display rotation: %d (MADCTL=0x%02X)", rotation, madctl);

    return esp_lcd_panel_io_tx_param(io_handle, lcd_cmd, &madctl, 1);
}

esp_err_t bsp_display_lock(uint32_t timeout_ms) { return esp_lv_adapter_lock(timeout_ms); }

void bsp_display_unlock(void) { esp_lv_adapter_unlock(); }
```

```c
#pragma once
```

```c
#include "esp_codec_dev.h"
#include "esp_err.h"
#include "sdkconfig.h"

#include "esp_io_expander_tca9554.h"

#include "esp_lv_adapter.h"
#include "lvgl.h"

/**************************************************************************************************
 *  BSP Capabilities
 **************************************************************************************************/

#define BSP_CAPS_DISPLAY 1
#define BSP_CAPS_TOUCH 1
#define BSP_CAPS_BUTTONS 0
#define BSP_CAPS_AUDIO 1
#define BSP_CAPS_AUDIO_SPEAKER 1
#define BSP_CAPS_AUDIO_MIC 1
#define BSP_CAPS_SDCARD 1
#define BSP_CAPS_IMU 0

/**************************************************************************************************
 * ESP-SparkBot-BSP pinout
 **************************************************************************************************/

/* I2C */
#define BSP_I2C_SCL (GPIO_NUM_14)
#define BSP_I2C_SDA (GPIO_NUM_15)

#define BSP_I2S_SCLK (GPIO_NUM_9)
#define BSP_I2S_MCLK (GPIO_NUM_42)
#define BSP_I2S_LCLK (GPIO_NUM_45)
#define BSP_I2S_DOUT (GPIO_NUM_8)
#define BSP_I2S_DSIN (GPIO_NUM_10)
#define BSP_POWER_AMP_IO (GPIO_NUM_46)

/* Display */
#define BSP_LCD_CS (GPIO_NUM_12)
#define BSP_LCD_PCLK (GPIO_NUM_38)
#define BSP_LCD_DATA0 (GPIO_NUM_4)
#define BSP_LCD_DATA1 (GPIO_NUM_5)
#define BSP_LCD_DATA2 (GPIO_NUM_6)
#define BSP_LCD_DATA3 (GPIO_NUM_7)

#define BSP_LCD_BACKLIGHT (GPIO_NUM_NC)
#define BSP_LCD_RST (GPIO_NUM_39)
#define BSP_LCD_TOUCH_RST (GPIO_NUM_40)
#define BSP_LCD_TOUCH_INT (GPIO_NUM_11)

/* uSD card */
#define BSP_SD_D0 (GPIO_NUM_3)
#define BSP_SD_CMD (GPIO_NUM_1)
#define BSP_SD_CLK (GPIO_NUM_2)

#define BSP_IO_EXPANDER_I2C_ADDRESS (ESP_IO_EXPANDER_I2C_TCA9554_ADDRESS_000)

#define LVGL_BUFFER_HEIGHT (CONFIG_BSP_DISPLAY_LVGL_BUF_HEIGHT)

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * I2C interface
 *
 * There are two devices connected to I2C peripheral:
 *  - QMA7981 Inertial measurement unit
 *  - OV2640 Camera module
 **************************************************************************************************/
#define BSP_I2C_NUM CONFIG_BSP_I2C_NUM

/**
 * @brief Init I2C driver
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK                On success
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG   I2C parameter error
 *      - ESP_FAIL              I2C driver installation error
 *
 */
esp_err_t bsp_i2c_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Deinit I2C driver and free its resources
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK                On success
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG   I2C parameter error
 *
 */
esp_err_t bsp_i2c_deinit(void);

/**
 * @brief Get I2C driver handle
 *
 * @return
 *      - I2C handle
 *
 */
i2c_master_bus_handle_t bsp_i2c_get_handle(void);

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * I2S audio interface
 *
 * There are two devices connected to the I2S peripheral:
 *  - Codec ES8311 for output(playback) and input(recording) path
 *
 * For speaker initialization use bsp_audio_codec_speaker_init() which is inside initialize I2S with bsp_audio_init().
 * For microphone initialization use bsp_audio_codec_microphone_init() which is inside initialize I2S with
 * bsp_audio_init(). After speaker or microphone initialization, use functions from esp_codec_dev for play/record audio.
 * Example audio play:
 * \code{.c}
 * esp_codec_dev_set_out_vol(spk_codec_dev, DEFAULT_VOLUME);
 * esp_codec_dev_open(spk_codec_dev, &fs);
 * esp_codec_dev_write(spk_codec_dev, wav_bytes, bytes_read_from_spiffs);
 * esp_codec_dev_close(spk_codec_dev);
 * \endcode
 **************************************************************************************************/

/**
 * @brief Init audio
 *
 * @note There is no deinit audio function. Users can free audio resources by calling i2s_del_channel()
 * @warning The type of i2s_config param is depending on IDF version.
 * @param[in]  i2s_config I2S configuration. Pass NULL to use default values (Mono, duplex, 16bit, 22050 Hz)
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK                On success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED The communication mode is not supported on the current chip
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG   NULL pointer or invalid configuration
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND     No available I2S channel found
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM        No memory for storing the channel information
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE This channel has not initialized or already started
 */
esp_err_t bsp_audio_init(const i2s_std_config_t *i2s_config);

/**
 * @brief Initialize speaker codec device
 *
 * @return Pointer to codec device handle or NULL when error occurred
 */
esp_codec_dev_handle_t bsp_audio_codec_speaker_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Initialize microphone codec device
 *
 * @return Pointer to codec device handle or NULL when error occurred
 */
esp_codec_dev_handle_t bsp_audio_codec_microphone_init(void);

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * SPIFFS
 *
 * After mounting the SPIFFS, it can be accessed with stdio functions ie.:
 * \code{.c}
 * FILE* f = fopen(BSP_SPIFFS_MOUNT_POINT"/hello.txt", "w");
 * fprintf(f, "Hello World!\n");
 * fclose(f);
 * \endcode
 **************************************************************************************************/
#define BSP_SPIFFS_MOUNT_POINT CONFIG_BSP_SPIFFS_MOUNT_POINT

/**
 * @brief Mount SPIFFS to virtual file system
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE if esp_vfs_spiffs_register was already called
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM if memory can not be allocated
 *      - ESP_FAIL if partition can not be mounted
 *      - other error codes
 */
esp_err_t bsp_spiffs_mount(void);

/**
 * @brief Unmount SPIFFS from virtual file system
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE if already unmounted
 */
esp_err_t bsp_spiffs_unmount(void);

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * uSD card
 *
 * After mounting the uSD card, it can be accessed with stdio functions ie.:
 * \code{.c}
 * FILE* f = fopen(BSP_MOUNT_POINT"/hello.txt", "w");
 * fprintf(f, "Hello %s!\n", bsp_sdcard->cid.name);
 * fclose(f);
 * \endcode
 **************************************************************************************************/
#define BSP_SD_MOUNT_POINT CONFIG_BSP_SD_MOUNT_POINT
extern sdmmc_card_t *bsp_sdcard;

/**
 * @brief Mount microSD card to virtual file system
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE if esp_vfs_fat_sdmmc_mount was already called
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM if memory cannot be allocated
 *      - ESP_FAIL if partition cannot be mounted
 *      - other error codes from SDMMC or SPI drivers, SDMMC protocol, or FATFS drivers
 */
esp_err_t bsp_sdcard_mount(void);

/**
 * @brief Unmount microSD card from virtual file system
 *
 * @return
 *      - ESP_OK on success
 *      - ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND if the partition table does not contain FATFS partition with given label
 *      - ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE if esp_vfs_fat_spiflash_mount was already called
 *      - ESP_ERR_NO_MEM if memory can not be allocated
 *      - ESP_FAIL if partition can not be mounted
 *      - other error codes from wear levelling library, SPI flash driver, or FATFS drivers
 */
esp_err_t bsp_sdcard_unmount(void);

/**
 * @brief Init IO expander chip TCA9554
 *
 * @note If the device was already initialized, users can also use it to get handle.
 * @note This function will be called in `bsp_display_start()` when using LCD sub-board 2 with the resolution of
 * 480x480.
 * @note This function will be called in `bsp_audio_init()`.
 *
 * @return Pointer to device handle or NULL when error occurred
 */
esp_io_expander_handle_t bsp_io_expander_init(void);

/**************************************************************************************************
 *
 * LCD interface
 *
 * LVGL is used as graphics library. LVGL is NOT thread safe, therefore the user must take LVGL mutex
 * by calling bsp_display_lock() before calling any LVGL API (lv_...) and then give the mutex with
 * bsp_display_unlock().
 *
 * If you want to use the display without LVGL, see bsp/display.h API and use BSP version with 'noglib' suffix.
 **************************************************************************************************/
#define BSP_LCD_SPI_NUM (SPI2_HOST)

#if (BSP_CONFIG_NO_GRAPHIC_LIB == 0)

/**
 * @brief BSP display configuration structure
 */
typedef struct {
    esp_lv_adapter_config_t lv_adapter_cfg;
    esp_lv_adapter_rotation_t rotation;
    esp_lv_adapter_tear_avoid_mode_t tear_avoid_mode;
    struct {
        unsigned int swap_xy;  /*!< Swap X and Y after read coordinates */
        unsigned int mirror_x; /*!< Mirror X after read coordinates */
        unsigned int mirror_y; /*!< Mirror Y after read coordinates */
    } touch_flags;
} bsp_display_cfg_t;

/**
 * @brief Initialize display
 *
 * This function initializes SPI, display controller and starts LVGL handling task.
 *
 * @return Pointer to LVGL display or NULL when error occurred
 */
lv_display_t *bsp_display_start(void);

/**
 * @brief Initialize display
 *
 * This function initializes SPI, display controller and starts LVGL handling task.
 * LCD backlight must be enabled separately by calling bsp_display_brightness_set()
 *
 * @param cfg display configuration
 *
 * @return Pointer to LVGL display or NULL when error occurred
 */
lv_display_t *bsp_display_start_with_config(bsp_display_cfg_t *cfg);

/**
 * @brief Get pointer to input device (touch, buttons, ...)
 *
 * @note The LVGL input device is initialized in bsp_display_start() function.
 *
 * @return Pointer to LVGL input device or NULL when not initialized
 */
lv_indev_t *bsp_display_get_input_dev(void);

/**
 * @brief Take LVGL mutex
 *
 * @param timeout_ms Timeout in [ms]. -1 will block indefinitely.
 * @return true  Mutex was taken
 * @return false Mutex was NOT taken
 */
esp_err_t bsp_display_lock(uint32_t timeout_ms);

/**
 * @brief Give LVGL mutex
 *
 */
void bsp_display_unlock(void);
#endif // BSP_CONFIG_NO_GRAPHIC_LIB == 0

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

```c
#pragma once

#include "esp_check.h"
#include "sdkconfig.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Assert on error, if selected in menuconfig. Otherwise return error code. */
#if CONFIG_BSP_ERROR_CHECK
#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(x) ESP_ERROR_CHECK(x)
#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(x) ESP_ERROR_CHECK(x)
#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK(x, ret) ESP_ERROR_CHECK(x)
#define BSP_NULL_CHECK(x, ret) assert(x)
#define BSP_NULL_CHECK_GOTO(x, goto_tag) assert(x)
#else
#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_ERR(x)                                                                                  \
    do {                                                                                                               \
        esp_err_t err_rc_ = (x);                                                                                       \
        if (unlikely(err_rc_ != ESP_OK)) {                                                                             \
            return err_rc_;                                                                                            \
        }                                                                                                              \
    } while (0)

#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK_RETURN_NULL(x)                                                                                 \
    do {                                                                                                               \
        if (unlikely((x) != ESP_OK)) {                                                                                 \
            return NULL;                                                                                               \
        }                                                                                                              \
    } while (0)

#define BSP_NULL_CHECK(x, ret)                                                                                         \
    do {                                                                                                               \
        if ((x) == NULL) {                                                                                             \
            return ret;                                                                                                \
        }                                                                                                              \
    } while (0)

#define BSP_ERROR_CHECK(x, ret)                                                                                        \
    do {                                                                                                               \
        if (unlikely((x) != ESP_OK)) {                                                                                 \
            return ret;                                                                                                \
        }                                                                                                              \
    } while (0)

#define BSP_NULL_CHECK_GOTO(x, goto_tag)                                                                               \
    do {                                                                                                               \
        if ((x) == NULL) {                                                                                             \
            goto goto_tag;                                                                                             \
        }                                                                                                              \
    } while (0)
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

### `components/imu/imu_qmi8658.c`

```c
/* QMI8658 gravity reader (see include/imu.h).
 *
 * Register map (from the Waveshare SensorLib that ships with this board --
 * the exact lib the board vendor's 03_QMI8658 example uses):
 *   WHO_AM_I  0x00 (0x05)
 *   CTRL1     0x02  (bit 6 = EN.ADDR_AI)
 *   CTRL2     0x03  (bits 4-5 accel range, bits 0-3 accel ODR)
 *   CTRL7     0x08  (bit 0 = accel enable)
 *   ACC X/Y/Z 16-bit little-endian, 6-byte burst from 0x35..0x3A
 *
 * Config (mirrors the vendor app for this board): no soft reset on a
 * healthy chip (the reset path has been seen to leave the chip's I2C
 * reads stuck) -> EN.ADDR_AI -> accel +/-8 g @ 1000 Hz (self-test off)
 * -> enable. If the WHO_AM_I read already fails (chip left in a stuck
 * state by an earlier reset), imu_init() runs the vendor's soft-reset
 * sequence (0x60=0xB0, poll RST_RESULT, EN.ADDR_AI) once and retries.
 * The driver is range-agnostic:
 * it averages 16 samples at rest and calibrates "1 g" to that magnitude, so
 * the screen-plane angle atan2(gy, gx) and the runtime |g| sanity band are
 * in calibrated units regardless of the chosen range.
 *
 * Bus: the shared BSP I2C master. The bus handle is probed with
 * i2c_master_probe (both candidate addresses), then a device handle is
 * added (same pattern as the PCF85063A driver on this bus); transactions
 * use the device-level API.
 *
 * Cost: one 6-byte burst read per tick (a few hundred microseconds on the
 * shared 100 kHz bus); init does ~30 short transactions, once at boot.
 */
#include "imu.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#include "board_display.h"
#include "driver/i2c_master.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"

static const char *TAG = "imu";

/* Register map (see file header). */
#define IMU_REG_WHOAMI 0x00
#define IMU_WHOAMI_VAL 0x05
#define IMU_REG_SOFT_RST 0x60
#define IMU_SOFT_RST_VAL 0xB0
#define IMU_REG_RST_RESULT 0x4D
#define IMU_RST_RESULT_VAL 0x80
#define IMU_REG_CTRL1 0x02
#define IMU_CTRL1_ADDR_AI_BIT 6
#define IMU_REG_CTRL2 0x03
#define IMU_REG_CTRL7 0x08
#define IMU_CTRL7_ACC_EN_BIT 0
/* CTRL2: bits 4-5 = accel range (8 g = 0b10), bits 0-3 = ODR (1000 Hz = 3);
 * self-test (bit 7) stays clear. => 0x20 | 0x03 = 0x23. */
#define IMU_CTRL2_ACC_8G_1KHZ 0x23
#define IMU_REG_AX_L 0x35
#define IMU_ACC_LEN 6
#define IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS 100
#define IMU_CAL_SAMPLES 16
#define IMU_CAL_SETTLE_MS 20 /* between samples (1000 Hz ODR settles fast) */
#define IMU_ANG_EMA 0.3f     /* per read, shortest-path */

static i2c_master_bus_handle_t s_bus;
static i2c_master_dev_handle_t s_dev;
static uint8_t s_addr; /* probed IMU address (for logging) */
static float s_inv_g;  /* 1 / magnitude of 1 g, in LSB^-1 (calibrated) */
static float s_angle;  /* EMA-smoothed atan2(gy, gx) */
static bool s_have_angle;
static bool s_ready;
static int s_fail_count; /* consecutive I2C read failures (0 = healthy) */

static esp_err_t imu_write(uint8_t reg, uint8_t val) {
    uint8_t b[2] = {reg, val};
    return i2c_master_transmit(s_dev, b, 2, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS);
}

/* Register reads use a STOP + fresh START (select the register, then a
 * separate receive) rather than i2c_master_transmit_receive's repeated
 * START, matching how the vendor driver reads through Arduino Wire (STOP
 * after the register-select, a new START for the data). */
static uint8_t imu_read_reg(uint8_t reg) {
    uint8_t v = 0;
    if (i2c_master_transmit(s_dev, &reg, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK)
        return 0xFF;
    return i2c_master_receive(s_dev, &v, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) == ESP_OK ? v : 0xFF;
}

static void imu_set_bit(uint8_t reg, uint8_t bit) {
    uint8_t v = imu_read_reg(reg);
    if (v != 0xFF)
        imu_write(reg, (uint8_t)(v | (1u << bit)));
}

/* Software reset (the vendor lib's reset(), for a chip whose I2C reads
 * are stuck): write 0x60=0xB0, poll RST_RESULT 0x4D == 0x80 for up to
 * ~500 ms, then set EN.ADDR_AI (CTRL1 bit 6). */
#define IMU_REG_SOFT_RST 0x60
#define IMU_SOFT_RST_VAL 0xB0
#define IMU_REG_RST_RESULT 0x4D
#define IMU_RST_RESULT_VAL 0x80
static bool imu_soft_reset(void) {
    esp_err_t err = imu_write(IMU_REG_SOFT_RST, IMU_SOFT_RST_VAL);
    if (err != ESP_OK) {
        /* Distinguishes "chip NACKs even the reset write" (I2C core dead or
         * wrong address) from "write ACKed but the chip never came back"
         * (reset ignored -- rail held / chip faulted). */
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "soft reset write 0x60=0xB0 not ACKed (%s)", esp_err_to_name(err));
        return false;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "soft reset write 0x60=0xB0 ACKed; polling RST_RESULT");
    for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) { /* ~500 ms */
        if (imu_read_reg(IMU_REG_RST_RESULT) == IMU_RST_RESULT_VAL)
            break;
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
    }
    imu_set_bit(IMU_REG_CTRL1, IMU_CTRL1_ADDR_AI_BIT);
    return true;
}

/* AXP2101 PMIC status probe (read-only): the board's power state decides
 * whether a "power cycle" ever actually cut the IMU rail. If a battery is
 * connected (STATUS1 bit 3) the PMIC rails survive a USB unplug, so the
 * IMU never sees a true cold power-on and can stay stuck in whatever state
 * it was left in. Registers (vendor XPowersLib AXP2101Constants.h):
 *   STATUS1 0x00 -- bit5 VBUS good, bit4 BATFET, bit3 battery connected
 *   STATUS2 0x01 -- bits6-5 charging=01/discharging=10/standby=00, bit2 chg
 *   PWRON_STATUS 0x20 -- what woke the board (bit4 battery, bit2 VBUS). */
static int imu_axp_read(i2c_master_dev_handle_t d, uint8_t reg) {
    uint8_t v = 0;
    if (i2c_master_transmit(d, &reg, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK)
        return -1;
    return i2c_master_receive(d, &v, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) == ESP_OK ? v : -1;
}

/* AXP2101 PMIC status probe (read-only): tells whether a battery holds
 * the IMU rail alive across a "power cycle". Registers (vendor XPowersLib
 * AXP2101Constants.h): STATUS1 0x00 (bit5 VBUS good, bit3 battery
 * connected), STATUS2 0x01 (bits6-5 charge state), PWRON_STATUS 0x20
 * (what started the board: bit4 battery, bit2 VBUS). */
static void imu_axp_probe(void) {
    i2c_device_config_t cfg = {.dev_addr_length = I2C_ADDR_BIT_LEN_7, .device_address = 0x34, .scl_speed_hz = 100000};
    i2c_master_dev_handle_t axp;
    if (i2c_master_bus_add_device(s_bus, &cfg, &axp) != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "AXP2101 @0x34 not probing; cannot read power state");
        return;
    }
    int s1 = imu_axp_read(axp, 0x00), s2 = imu_axp_read(axp, 0x01), s3 = imu_axp_read(axp, 0x20);
    i2c_master_bus_rm_device(axp);
    if (s1 < 0) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "AXP2101 answers 0x34 but status reads fail");
        return;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "AXP2101: STATUS1=0x%02X (VBUS %s, battery %s) STATUS2=0x%02X PWRON=0x%02X", s1,
             (s1 & 0x20) ? "good" : "absent", (s1 & 0x08) ? "connected" : "absent", s2, s3);
}

/* Diagnostic: probe the whole 7-bit address range and log every responder.
 * A healthy board shows the PCF85063 (0x51) and the TCA9554 (0x20) here;
 * if the IMU does not appear at 0x6A/0x6B the chip has not power-cycled
 * (its rail was held by the battery/caps) or is faulted. */
static void imu_bus_scan(void) {
    char buf[160];
    int n = 0;
    for (uint8_t a = 0x08; a <= 0x77; a++) {
        if (i2c_master_probe(s_bus, a, 20) == ESP_OK)
            n += snprintf(buf + n, sizeof(buf) - (size_t)n, " %02X", a);
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "bus scan:%s", n ? buf + 1 : " (no responders)");
}

static esp_err_t imu_read_raw(int16_t xyz[3]) {
    uint8_t reg = IMU_REG_AX_L;
    uint8_t buf[IMU_ACC_LEN];
    /* STOP + fresh START (see imu_read_reg for the why). */
    if (i2c_master_transmit(s_dev, &reg, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK)
        return ESP_FAIL;
    if (i2c_master_receive(s_dev, buf, IMU_ACC_LEN, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK)
        return ESP_FAIL;
    xyz[0] = (int16_t)(buf[0] | (buf[1] << 8));
    xyz[1] = (int16_t)(buf[2] | (buf[3] << 8));
    xyz[2] = (int16_t)(buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8));
    return ESP_OK;
}

esp_err_t imu_init(void) {
    if (s_ready)
        return ESP_OK;
    s_bus = bsp_i2c_get_handle();
    if (!s_bus) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "no I2C bus handle from BSP");
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }

    /* Probe 0x6A (SAD high), then 0x6B, for a matching WHO_AM_I. A brief
     * retry: right after a cold power-on the chip's I2C peripheral can be
     * a few ms behind its own ready state, and the vendor example polls
     * WHO_AM_I in a loop for exactly this reason. */
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++) {
        if (attempt > 0) {
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(250));
            imu_bus_scan();
        }
        for (uint8_t addr = 0x6A; addr <= 0x6B && !s_dev; addr++) {
            if (i2c_master_probe(s_bus, addr, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS) != ESP_OK)
                continue;
            i2c_device_config_t cfg = {.dev_addr_length = I2C_ADDR_BIT_LEN_7,
                                       .device_address = addr,
                                       .scl_speed_hz = 100000}; /* the vendor QMI8658
                                                                 * example runs this bus at
                                                                 * 100 kHz; the chip's reads
                                                                 * have been seen to fail at
                                                                 * 400 kHz */
            i2c_master_dev_handle_t tmp;
            if (i2c_master_bus_add_device(s_bus, &cfg, &tmp) != ESP_OK)
                continue;
            /* s_dev must be live before any transaction: imu_read_reg and
             * imu_soft_reset use it, and a NULL handle fails every
             * transfer with ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG before touching the wire,
             * which reads back as 0xFF and looks like a dead chip. */
            s_dev = tmp;
            s_addr = addr;
            uint8_t who = 0xFF;
            uint8_t reg = IMU_REG_WHOAMI;
            esp_err_t werr = i2c_master_transmit(s_dev, &reg, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS);
            if (werr == ESP_OK)
                werr = i2c_master_receive(s_dev, &who, 1, IMU_XFER_TIMEOUT_MS);
            if (werr != ESP_OK)
                ESP_LOGW(TAG, "@0x%02X WHO_AM_I read failed: %s", addr, esp_err_to_name(werr));
            if (who != IMU_WHOAMI_VAL) {
                /* Chip present but reads stuck (e.g. after an earlier
                 * software reset): run the vendor's reset sequence once
                 * and re-check. */
                ESP_LOGW(TAG, "@0x%02X answers but WHO_AM_I 0x%02X != 0x%02X; trying soft reset", addr, who,
                         IMU_WHOAMI_VAL);
                imu_soft_reset();
                who = imu_read_reg(IMU_REG_WHOAMI);
                if (who != IMU_WHOAMI_VAL) {
                    i2c_master_bus_rm_device(s_dev);
                    s_dev = NULL;
                    s_addr = 0;
                    continue;
                }
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "@0x%02X recovered after soft reset", addr);
            }
        }
        if (s_dev)
            break;
    }
    if (!s_dev) {
        imu_bus_scan();
        imu_axp_probe(); /* did the PMIC rails survive a "power cycle"? */
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "QMI8658 not found on the I2C bus (0x6A/0x6B); moon tilt disabled");
        return ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND;
    }

    /* No soft reset: the Waveshare reference app for this board configures
     * + enables the accel directly on the power-on sensor (the reset path
     * leaves the accel stuck off). Set EN.ADDR_AI (CTRL1 bit 6), then
     * accel +/-8 g @ 1000 Hz (self-test off), then enable (CTRL7 bit 0).
     * The gyro stays off (unused). */
    imu_set_bit(IMU_REG_CTRL1, IMU_CTRL1_ADDR_AI_BIT);
    {
        uint8_t v = imu_read_reg(IMU_REG_CTRL2);
        if (v != 0xFF)
            imu_write(IMU_REG_CTRL2, (uint8_t)((v & 0x80u) | IMU_CTRL2_ACC_8G_1KHZ));
    }
    imu_set_bit(IMU_REG_CTRL7, IMU_CTRL7_ACC_EN_BIT);
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));

    /* Calibrate: average 16 samples; the device is assumed at rest, so the
     * mean vector magnitude is 1 g. */
    float sx = 0, sy = 0, sz = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < IMU_CAL_SAMPLES; i++) {
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(IMU_CAL_SETTLE_MS));
        int16_t v[3];
        if (imu_read_raw(v) != ESP_OK) {
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "accel read failed during init; moon tilt disabled");
            return ESP_FAIL;
        }
        sx += v[0];
        sy += v[1];
        sz += v[2];
    }
    float ax = sx / IMU_CAL_SAMPLES, ay = sy / IMU_CAL_SAMPLES, az = sz / IMU_CAL_SAMPLES;
    float mag = sqrtf(ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az);
    if (mag < 0.2f) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "init |g| %.3f is implausible (chip moving or stuck); moon tilt disabled", mag);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE;
    }
    s_inv_g = 1.0f / mag;
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "QMI8658 @0x%02X ready: avg (%.3f, %.3f, %.3f) g", s_addr, ax * s_inv_g, ay * s_inv_g, az * s_inv_g);
    s_ready = true;
    return ESP_OK;
}

bool imu_is_ready(void) { return s_ready; }

/* One burst read -> calibrated, sanity-checked gravity vector (units of
 * g, |g| ~ 1 at rest). Shared by imu_read_roll and imu_read_gravity.
 *
 * A chip left stuck on the shared I2C bus NACKs every transfer; log the
 * start and every 20th consecutive failure so the stuck state is visible
 * in the serial log (it also stalls the RTC on the same bus). */
static bool imu_gravity_sample(float g[3]) {
    if (!s_ready)
        return false;
    int16_t v[3];
    if (imu_read_raw(v) != ESP_OK) {
        s_fail_count++;
        if (s_fail_count == 1 || s_fail_count % 20 == 0)
            ESP_LOGW(TAG, "accel read failed (consecutive %d)", s_fail_count);
        return false;
    }
    if (s_fail_count) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "accel reads recovered after %d consecutive failures", s_fail_count);
        s_fail_count = 0;
    }
    g[0] = v[0] * s_inv_g;
    g[1] = v[1] * s_inv_g;
    g[2] = v[2] * s_inv_g;
    float mag = sqrtf(g[0] * g[0] + g[1] * g[1] + g[2] * g[2]);
    if (mag < 0.5f || mag > 1.5f) /* shaking / dropped: skip the sample */
        return false;
    return true;
}

bool imu_read_gravity(float g[3]) { return imu_gravity_sample(g); }

bool imu_read_roll(float *angle_rad) {
    float g[3];
    if (!imu_gravity_sample(g))
        return false;
    float ang = atan2f(g[1], g[0]);
    if (s_have_angle) {
        float diff = ang - s_angle;
        if (diff > M_PI)
            diff -= 2.0f * M_PI;
        else if (diff < -M_PI)
            diff += 2.0f * M_PI;
        s_angle += IMU_ANG_EMA * diff;
        if (s_angle > M_PI)
            s_angle -= 2.0f * M_PI;
        else if (s_angle < -M_PI)
            s_angle += 2.0f * M_PI;
    } else {
        s_angle = ang;
        s_have_angle = true;
    }
    *angle_rad = s_angle;
    return true;
}
```

### `components/imu/include/imu.h`

```c
/* QMI8658 6-axis IMU (on-board, shared BSP I2C bus).
 *
 * Minimal gravity reader for the moon phase UI's tilt-driven
 * "ball-in-hand" rotation (components/ui/moon_ui.c): the screen-plane
 * roll of the device from the accelerometer's gravity vector,
 * EMA-smoothed, plus the raw calibrated 3-axis gravity vector for
 * motion detection (idle timer / wake). No gyro, no FIFO, no
 * interrupts -- one 6-byte burst read per call at the UI tick rate
 * (<= 20 Hz on a 50 ms tick).
 *
 * Bus: the shared BSP I2C master (bsp_i2c_get_handle()). The board also
 * has the PCF85063A RTC @0x51, TCA9554 @0x20 and the CST9217 touch @0x15;
 * the QMI8658 sits at 0x6A (SAD low; 0x6B is probed as a fallback), so
 * there is no address conflict.
 */
#ifndef IMU_H
#define IMU_H

#include <stdbool.h>

#include "esp_err.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Find + verify the QMI8658 (WHO_AM_I @0x00 == 0x05), soft-reset it,
 * enable the accelerometer and calibrate "1 g" to the at-rest sample
 * magnitude, logging the calibrated axis vector. Soft-fails (the moon
 * stays static; no tilt input) when the chip is absent. */
esp_err_t imu_init(void);

/* True once init verified the chip. */
bool imu_is_ready(void);

/* Calibrated 3-axis gravity vector in units of g (|g| ~ 1 at rest),
 * screen coordinates (x right, y down, z toward the viewer). RAW -- no
 * EMA smoothing -- so the angle between two calls reflects actual motion
 * since the last sample (use for tilt activity / wake detection). Reads
 * the 6 accelerometer bytes (0x35..0x3A); returns false on I2C error or
 * an implausible |g| (< 0.5 g / > 1.5 g). */
bool imu_read_gravity(float g[3]);

/* Screen-plane gravity angle in radians (atan2(gy, gx) in screen coords,
 * x right, y down), EMA-smoothed with shortest-path wrap across the
 * +/-pi seam. Reads the 6 accelerometer bytes (0x35..0x3A); returns
 * false on I2C error or an implausible |g| (< 0.5 g / > 1.5 g). The
 * consumer applies its own orientation offset + sign (the board's IMU
 * mounting is not known at driver level). */
bool imu_read_roll(float *angle_rad);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* IMU_H */
```

```ini
# Moon phase display component.

# Portable core (pure C + vendored public-domain ERFA ephemeris): the exact
# same translation units are also built into the host simulator
```
