### `components/ui/screens.h`

```c
#ifndef EEZ_LVGL_UI_SCREENS_H
#define EEZ_LVGL_UI_SCREENS_H

#include <lvgl.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* objects_t layout contract:
 *
 * 1. The screen ROOTS are the first members, in enum ScreensEnum order:
 *    loadScreen(id) indexes this array at `id - 1` (ui.c
 *    getLvglObjectFromIndex), so a mismatch is an out-of-bounds read,
 *    not a visible bug.
 *
 * 2. ONE shared clock widget. create_user_widget_clock(parent, 16) is
 *    called exactly once (the modem-sleep screen) and creates the only
 *    clock: objects[16] (the full-screen flex container), objects[17]
 *    (the HH:MM slot row) and objects[18] (the alarm label). The four
 *    other moon screens ALIAS those same three objects at their own
 *    bases -- objects[21/22/23] (wifi), [26/27/28] (light sleep),
 *    [30/31/32] (deep sleep), [35/36/37] (alarm) point at the SAME
 *    lv_obj_t's -- so every screen ticks and reads one set of labels
 *    that is always current: the vars are updated at the minute tick
 *    (which ticks the shared widget regardless of the active screen)
 *    and ui_clock_attach_to() (the loadScreen choke point) reparents
 *    the widget onto the new moon screen and refreshes the vars from
 *    the RTC, so a switch (the wake in particular) shows the current
 *    minute immediately. The per-screen <screen>_clock containers
 *    ([15], [20], [25], [29], [34]) stay as the widget's parent
 *    targets (plus the unclickable_recursive targets); the deep-sleep
 *    HIDDEN flag and the light-sleep alpha apply to the shared widget
 *    (objects[16]) itself. tick_user_widget_clock(16) is the only
 *    clock tick; the per-screen tick functions no longer tick it.
 *
 *      [0]  modem_sleep              [15]  modem_sleep_clock         (widget parent 1/5)
 *      [1]  wifi                     [16]  modem_sleep_clock__clock  (THE widget container)
 *      [2]  light_sleep              [17]  ..._label_clock_time      (the HH:MM slot row)
 *      [3]  deep_sleep               [18]  ..._label_clock_alarm     (the alarm label)
 *      [4]  alarm                    [19]  arc_clock_seconds_modem
 *      [5]  settings_hub             [20]  wifi_clock                (widget parent 2/5)
 *      [6]  settings_alarm           [21]  wifi_clock__clock         = objects[16] (alias)
 *      [7]  settings_pomodoro        [22]  ..._label_clock_time      = objects[17] (alias)
 *      [8]  settings_alarm_time      [23]  ..._label_clock_alarm     = objects[18] (alias)
 *      [9]  settings_light_sleep     [24]  arc_clock_seconds_wifi
 *      [10] settings_deep_sleep      [25]  light_sleep_clock         (widget parent 3/5)
 *      [11] settings_wifi            [26]  light_sleep_clock__clock  = objects[16] (alias)
 *      [12] settings_wifi_password   [27]  ..._label_clock_time      = objects[17] (alias)
 *      [13] settings_time            [28]  ..._label_clock_alarm     = objects[18] (alias)
 *      [14] settings_tz              [29]  deep_sleep_clock          (widget parent 4/5)
 *                                 [30]  deep_sleep_clock__clock     = objects[16] (alias)
 *                                 [31]  ..._label_clock_time        = objects[17] (alias)
 *                                 [32]  ..._label_clock_alarm       = objects[18] (alias)
 *                                 [33]  screen_indicator_sleep1
 *                                 [34]  alarm_clock                 (widget parent 5/5)
 *                                 [35]  alarm_clock__clock          = objects[16] (alias)
 *                                 [36]  ..._label_clock_time        = objects[17] (alias)
 *                                 [37]  ..._label_clock_alarm       = objects[18] (alias)
 *                                 [38]  screen_indicator_alarm
 *                                 [39]  settings_hub_exit        (the settings hub's central exit)
 *                                 [40]  settings_alarm_master    (deactivate-all toggle)
 *                                 [41]  settings_alarm_pomodoro  (pomodoro entry)
 *                                 [42]  settings_alarm_clock     (real-alarm entry)
 *                                 [43]  settings_pomodoro_roller_h
 *                                 [44]  settings_pomodoro_roller_m
 *                                 [45]  settings_pomodoro_caption
 *                                 [46]  settings_alarm_time_roller_h
 *                                 [47]  settings_alarm_time_roller_m
 *                                 [48]  settings_alarm_time_band        (the day-range arc)
 *                                 [49]  settings_alarm_time_handle_start
 *                                 [50]  settings_alarm_time_handle_end
 *                                 [51]  wifi_indicator_wifi
 *                                 [52]  settings_time_roller_d      (manual time entry: date day)
 *                                 [53]  settings_time_roller_m      (date month)
 *                                 [54]  settings_time_roller_y      (date year, 2000+YY)
 *                                 [55]  settings_time_roller_h      (manual time entry: time hour)
 *                                 [56]  settings_time_roller_mi     (time minute)
 *                                 [57]  settings_tz_roller          (timezone/UTC offset, clock_tz.h)
 *
 * The wheel-keyboard's own widgets (the 26 letters, the group dividers,
 * the sweep highlight, the mode keys, the centre preview) are LOCAL to
 * create_screen_settings_wifi_password (static arrays in screens.c);
 * objects_t only names the screen roots and the clock-widget slots.
 */
typedef struct _objects_t {
    /* Screen roots (loadScreen index = ScreensEnum value - 1). */
    lv_obj_t *modem_sleep;
    lv_obj_t *wifi;
    lv_obj_t *light_sleep;
    lv_obj_t *deep_sleep;
    lv_obj_t *alarm;
    lv_obj_t *settings_hub;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *settings_pomodoro;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time;
    lv_obj_t *settings_light_sleep;
    lv_obj_t *settings_deep_sleep;
    lv_obj_t *settings_wifi;
    lv_obj_t *settings_wifi_password;
    lv_obj_t *settings_time; /* manual time/date entry (P4 entry point; the screen is shared) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_tz;   /* timezone / UTC offset picker (S3 + P4 entry point) */
    /* Per-screen children (see the layout contract above). */
    lv_obj_t *modem_sleep_clock;
    lv_obj_t *modem_sleep_clock__clock;
    lv_obj_t *modem_sleep_clock__label_clock_time;
    lv_obj_t *modem_sleep_clock__label_clock_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *arc_clock_seconds_modem;
    lv_obj_t *wifi_clock;
    lv_obj_t *wifi_clock__clock;
    lv_obj_t *wifi_clock__label_clock_time;
    lv_obj_t *wifi_clock__label_clock_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *arc_clock_seconds_wifi;
    lv_obj_t *light_sleep_clock;
    lv_obj_t *light_sleep_clock__clock;
    lv_obj_t *light_sleep_clock__label_clock_time;
    lv_obj_t *light_sleep_clock__label_clock_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *deep_sleep_clock;
    lv_obj_t *deep_sleep_clock__clock;
    lv_obj_t *deep_sleep_clock__label_clock_time;
    lv_obj_t *deep_sleep_clock__label_clock_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *screen_indicator_sleep1;
    lv_obj_t *alarm_clock;
    lv_obj_t *alarm_clock__clock;
    lv_obj_t *alarm_clock__label_clock_time;
    lv_obj_t *alarm_clock__label_clock_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *screen_indicator_alarm;
    lv_obj_t *settings_hub_exit;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_master;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_pomodoro;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_clock;
    lv_obj_t *settings_pomodoro_roller_h;
    lv_obj_t *settings_pomodoro_roller_m;
    lv_obj_t *settings_pomodoro_caption;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time_roller_h;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time_roller_m;
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time_band;         /* the day-range arc (upper half circle) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time_handle_start; /* the range-start drag handle (a day knob) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_alarm_time_handle_end;   /* the range-end drag handle (a day knob) */
    lv_obj_t *wifi_indicator_wifi; /* WiFi-screen indicator (below the clock): grey = connecting, white = connected */
    lv_obj_t *settings_time_roller_d;  /* manual time entry: the date day (01-31) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_time_roller_m;  /* the date month (01-12) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_time_roller_y;  /* the date year (2000+YY, two-digit 00-99) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_time_roller_h;  /* the time hour (00-23) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_time_roller_mi; /* the time minute (00-59) */
    lv_obj_t *settings_tz_roller;      /* the timezone / UTC offset (clock_tz option list) */
} objects_t;

extern objects_t objects;

enum ScreensEnum {
    SCREEN_ID_MODEM_SLEEP = 1,
    SCREEN_ID_WIFI,
    SCREEN_ID_LIGHT_SLEEP,
    SCREEN_ID_DEEP_SLEEP,
    SCREEN_ID_ALARM,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_HUB,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_ALARM,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_POMODORO,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_ALARM_TIME,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_LIGHT_SLEEP,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_DEEP_SLEEP,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_WIFI,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_WIFI_PASSWORD,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_TIME,
    SCREEN_ID_SETTINGS_TZ,
};

void create_screen_modem_sleep();
void tick_screen_modem_sleep();

void create_screen_wifi();
void tick_screen_wifi();

void create_screen_light_sleep();
void tick_screen_light_sleep();

void create_screen_deep_sleep();
void tick_screen_deep_sleep();

void create_screen_alarm();
void tick_screen_alarm();

/* Settings screens (moon-less by design: the settings hub and its
 * sub-screens show no moon image, so they must NOT call
 * moon_screen_prepare / moon_ui_create_image). */
void create_screen_settings_hub();
void tick_screen_settings_hub();

void create_screen_settings_alarm();
void tick_screen_settings_alarm();

void create_screen_settings_pomodoro();
void tick_screen_settings_pomodoro();

void create_screen_settings_alarm_time();
void tick_screen_settings_alarm_time();

void create_screen_settings_light_sleep();
void tick_screen_settings_light_sleep();

void create_screen_settings_deep_sleep();
void tick_screen_settings_deep_sleep();

void create_screen_settings_wifi();
void tick_screen_settings_wifi();

/* Manual time/date entry (the P4's fallback for a clock it could not
 * sync: reached by the settings hub's clock icon, P4-only -- the S3's
 * time comes from the PCF85063A and the icon is not added there).
 * Six clock-style rollers in two rows (the time HH:MM:SS at the home
 * clock label's position, the date DD.MM.YY below) seed from the wall
 * clock; releasing a roller commits the whole value (clock_set_time +
 * the trusted flag) so the alarm one-shot re-arms and the moon
 * re-bakes. The S3 build carries the screen too (structurally
 * identical) -- it is simply unreachable. */
void create_screen_settings_time();
void tick_screen_settings_time();

/* Timezone / UTC offset (both boards' entry point: the hub's globe icon).
 * One roller over every 30-minute UTC offset (UTC-12:00 .. UTC+14:00) plus
 * Europe/Berlin (the Kconfig default, DST-aware). Releasing the roller
 * applies the zone (clock_tz_apply -- the P4 re-derives its local digits
 * from the same epoch; the S3 rewrites the PCF digits epoch-consistently),
 * re-arms the alarm arming, and persists the selection. The S3 and the P4
 * both reach it, so unlike the manual time entry there is no board gate. */
void create_screen_settings_tz();
void tick_screen_settings_tz();

/* The circular wheel keyboard for WiFi password entry (reached by
 * tapping an AP row on the WiFi screen, which prefills the SSID).
 * The v2 hybrid (doc 7.14; the operable reference is the lab's panel #1,
 * docs/keyboard/round-keyboard-lab.html): the 26 slots of the active
 * register tile the ring in equal shares, grouped into 12 fixed
 * frequency sectors (their boundaries never move between registers); on
 * press only the pressed sector's boxes are revealed edge-to-edge across
 * the ring band (the lit box inverts) with a DTMF-style centre preview
 * -- the letter commits only on release, and the hit-test is the exact
 * box under the finger. A 4-key register/shift arc (abc / ABC / 123 / #$,
 * top 240 deg), the bottom 120 deg is the circle-xmark COMMIT key (save +
 * connect) and the trash DISCARD key, a plain centre tap backspaces, and
 * a 400 ms centre long press is the only way back to the WiFi list (v2
 * has no in-ring exit -- the xmark glyph is the commit key). */
void create_screen_settings_wifi_password();
void tick_screen_settings_wifi_password();

/* Shared exit button: the fa-circle-xmark glyph alone (U+F057 -- the
 * filled white circle with the cut-out cross IS the button), used
 * central on the settings hub and bottom-centre on every sub-screen.
 * Returns the tap box (the glyph's natural 96 px, widened by size); a
 * tap on it fires LV_EVENT_CLICKED on it. */
lv_obj_t *settings_create_exit_button(lv_obj_t *parent, int size);

/* The ONE shared clock widget (layout contract 2): called exactly
 * once, from the modem-sleep screen, with BASE 16. */
void create_user_widget_clock(lv_obj_t *parent_obj, int startWidgetIndex);

/* Tick the shared clock from its vars (the minute tick + the attach).
 * The base is 16 for every caller -- the other four moon screens
 * alias the same objects, so there is nothing else to tick. */
void tick_user_widget_clock(int startWidgetIndex);

/* The loadScreen hook (LVGL task): reparent the shared clock widget
 * onto the active moon screen (settings screens keep it where it
 * was -- computed, not rendered) and refresh the clock vars from the
 * RTC so the switch shows the current minute immediately. Called
 * BEFORE the screen switch's atomic flush, so the fresh digits are
 * part of that one frame. */
void ui_clock_attach_to(enum ScreensEnum screenId);

enum Themes {
    THEME_ID_MOON,
};
enum Colors {
    COLOR_ID_MOON,
};
void change_color_theme(uint32_t themeIndex);
extern uint32_t theme_colors[1][1];
extern uint32_t active_theme_index;

void tick_screen_by_id(enum ScreensEnum screenId);
void tick_screen(int screen_index);

void create_screens();

/* Dispatch a settings entry's screen refresh (the hub-icon / entry
 * handlers call it after loadScreen + ui_tick). Exposed for the
 * TEST_WIFI_SCAN_SEC test hook. */
void settings_screen_refresh_for(enum ScreensEnum target);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /*EEZ_LVGL_UI_SCREENS_H*/
```

```c
        remove_style_label_icon_regular, remove_style_label_icon_solid,
    };
    remove_style_funcs[styleIndex](obj);
```

```c
#if defined(EEZ_FOR_LVGL)

#endif

#include "actions.h"
#include "images.h"
#include "moon_ui.h"
#include "screens.h"
#include "ui.h"
#include "vars.h"

#if defined(EEZ_FOR_LVGL)

void ui_init() {
    eez_flow_init(assets, sizeof(assets), (lv_obj_t **)&objects, sizeof(objects), images, sizeof(images), actions);
}

void ui_tick() {
    eez_flow_tick();
    tick_screen(g_currentScreen);
}

#else

#include <string.h>

static int16_t currentScreen = -1;

static lv_obj_t *getLvglObjectFromIndex(int32_t index) {
    if (index == -1) {
        return 0;
    }
    return ((lv_obj_t **)&objects)[index];
}

/* Screen switch (UI_SCREEN_SWITCH_FADE): EVERY screen switch fades
 * the panel's OWN hardware brightness (the CO5300 0x51 command) to
 * black (moon_ui_fade_out, before lv_scr_load), loads, and ramps it
 * back (moon_ui_screen_switched) -- the transition writes no pixels,
 * so it costs nothing on the panel bus. The ONE exception is the
 * both-moon switch (airplane / wifi / the sleep screens share the one
 * moon image): a fade there would only dim the moon, which is the
 * same disk on both screens, so those stay the plain atomic
 * whole-panel display. History: the first
 * screen-load fade rode LVGL's async refresh and the whole panel
 * drained in 25-row QSPI strips (the moon crept in top-to-bottom for
 * over a second on every switch); the overlay fade made each step one
 * atomic whole-panel lv_refr_now, but every step still charged a
 * full-screen re-render + ~175 ms of strip traffic; the brightness
 * ramp needs no pixels at all. */
void loadScreen(enum ScreensEnum screenId) {
    if (currentScreen >= 0) {
        enum ScreensEnum oldId = (enum ScreensEnum)(currentScreen + 1);
        /* Fade every switch except the both-moon one (airplane / wifi /
         * the sleep screens: dimming the shared moon disk to black and
         * back is a fade with nothing to fade). */
        if (oldId != screenId && !(moon_ui_screen_is_moon(oldId) && moon_ui_screen_is_moon(screenId)))
            moon_ui_fade_out(); /* self-guarded (LVGL task, fade on,
                                 * no pipeline owns the buffer) */
    }
    currentScreen = screenId - 1;
    lv_obj_t *screen = getLvglObjectFromIndex(currentScreen);
    lv_scr_load(screen);
    /* Reparent the ONE shared clock widget onto the new moon screen and
     * refresh its vars from the RTC BEFORE the switch's atomic flush, so
     * the switch -- the wake in particular -- shows the current minute
     * in that one frame (the pre-wake value held by the last-ticked
     * screen's labels would otherwise linger until the next minute tick).
     * The panel is still black here for a fading switch (the fade-in runs
     * in moon_ui_screen_switched), so the reparent + label update are
     * invisible. A non-moon (settings) screen keeps the widget where it
     * was -- computed, not rendered. */
    ui_clock_attach_to(screenId);
    moon_ui_screen_switched();
}

void ui_init() {
    create_screens();
    /* The airplane (modem-sleep) screen is the home screen. The boot
     * sweep plays on it: at boot the clock is acquired by the blocking
     * boot sync (app_main, before the UI) and action_wake_screen lands
     * here. The transient WiFi screen is only shown while a sync is in
     * flight (wake / manual / hourly) and drops to airplane on
     * s_wifi_sync_done (ui_tick_timer_cb). */
    loadScreen(SCREEN_ID_MODEM_SLEEP);
}

void ui_tick() { tick_screen(currentScreen); }

enum ScreensEnum ui_current_screen(void) { return (enum ScreensEnum)(currentScreen + 1); }

#endif
```

### `components/ui/ui_px.h`

```c
#ifndef EEZ_UI_PX_H
#define EEZ_UI_PX_H

/* Panel-relative UI scaling.
 *
 * The UI was designed at the S3's 466x466 and scales to the panel by
 * its height (both panels are square). UI_PX() is exact at 466, so the
 * S3 layout is bit-for-bit unchanged; at the P4's 720 it is the
 * 720/466 upscaling of every layout literal. Full-panel extents use
 * UI_PANEL_PX directly.
 *
 * The host simulator compiles the device screens unmodified with
 * -DPANEL_SIZE=N (uisim build.sh), so the panel size comes from there;
 * the device gets it from the BSP (BSP_LCD_H_RES).
 */
#if defined(PANEL_SIZE)
#define UI_PANEL_PX PANEL_SIZE
#else
#include "bsp/display.h"
#define UI_PANEL_PX BSP_LCD_H_RES
#endif

#define UI_PX(x) (((x) * (UI_PANEL_PX)) / 466)

#endif /* EEZ_UI_PX_H */
```

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "vars.h"

char clock_label[6] = {0};
char alarm_label[6] = {0};
char alarm_prefix[4] = {0}; /* "" or the 2-letter weekday ("Mo", ...) */
int32_t clock_seconds;

static const char *TAG = "ui_variables";

const char *get_var_clock_label() { return clock_label; }

void set_var_clock_label(const char *value) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Updating Clock label with value: %s", value);
    snprintf(clock_label, sizeof(clock_label) / sizeof(char), "%s", value);
    clock_label[sizeof(clock_label) / sizeof(char) - 1] = 0;
}

const char *get_var_alarm_label() { return alarm_label; }

void set_var_alarm_label(const char *value) {
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Updating Alarm label with value: %s", value);
    snprintf(alarm_label, sizeof(alarm_label) / sizeof(char), "%s", value);
    alarm_label[sizeof(alarm_label) / sizeof(char) - 1] = 0;
}

const char *get_var_alarm_prefix() { return alarm_prefix; }

void set_var_alarm_prefix(const char *value) {
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Updating Alarm prefix with value: %s", value);
    strncpy(alarm_prefix, value, sizeof(alarm_prefix) / sizeof(char));
    alarm_prefix[sizeof(alarm_prefix) / sizeof(char) - 1] = 0;
}

int32_t get_var_clock_seconds() { return clock_seconds; }

void set_var_clock_seconds(int32_t value) {
    // Apply modulo 60 to keep seconds in 0-59 range
    int32_t clamped_value = value % 60;
    ESP_LOGD(TAG, "Updating Clock seconds with value: %d", clamped_value);
    clock_seconds = clamped_value;
}
```

```c
/**
 * WiFi Connection Manager Component
 * Handles WiFi initialization and connection management with SPIFFS credential storage
 */

#ifndef WIFI_H
#define WIFI_H

#include "esp_err.h"
#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @brief Initialize WiFi connection
 *
 * Initializes NVS, mounts SPIFFS, reads WiFi credentials from /spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt,
 * configures and starts WiFi connection.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success, ESP_FAIL on credential read failure, ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT on connection timeout
 */
esp_err_t wifi_manager_init(void);

/**
 * @brief Write WiFi credentials to /spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt
 *
 * The inverse of the credential read: first non-comment line = SSID,
 * second = password (a comment header is written so the file stays
 * readable by hand). Both must be non-empty and fit the credential
 * limits (SSID < 32 chars, password < 64 chars); the password is never
 * logged.
 *
 * @return esp_err_t ESP_OK on success, ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG/ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE on bad input
 */
esp_err_t wifi_credentials_write(const char *ssid, const char *password);

/**
 * @brief Check if WiFi is connected
 *
 * @return bool true if WiFi is connected and has IP address
 */
bool wifi_manager_is_connected(void);

/**
 * @brief Deinitialize WiFi connection
 *
 * Stops WiFi, cleans up resources and event groups
 */
void wifi_manager_deinit(void);

#define WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS 16

/**
 * @brief One scanned access point
 */
typedef struct {
    char ssid[33];
    int8_t rssi;
    uint8_t auth; /* wifi_auth_mode_t */
} wifi_ap_info_t;

/**
 * @brief Start a background AP scan
 *
 * Runs the scan on a dedicated task. When the radio is down (the
 * normal at-rest state) the task brings it up minimally (init + STA
 * mode + start, no credentials, no connection) and deinit's it again
 * when done; when the manager owns the radio the scan shares it and
 * leaves it running. No-op while a scan is already in progress.
 *
 * Not called `wifi_scan_start`: on the P4 (remote C6) esp_hosted is
 * linked whole-archive and its RPC layer defines a global
 * `wifi_scan_start(ctrl_cmd_t *)` — the two would collide at link time.
 * Renamed on both boards so the source stays single-sourced.
 */
void wifi_scan_begin(void);

/**
 * @brief Whether a scan is currently running
 */
bool wifi_scan_in_progress(void);

/**
 * @brief Copy the last completed scan's results
 *
 * @param out   destination buffer
 * @param max   buffer capacity
 * @return int  number of APs copied (0 until the first completion)
 */
int wifi_scan_get_results(wifi_ap_info_t *out, int max);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif // WIFI_H
```

### `components/wifi/wifi.c`

```c
/**
 * WiFi Connection Manager Component
 * Handles WiFi initialization and connection management with SPIFFS credential storage
 */

#include "wifi.h"
#include "esp_event.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_netif.h"
#include "esp_spiffs.h"
#include "esp_wifi.h"
#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/event_groups.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "nvs_flash.h"
#include "sdkconfig.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static const char *TAG = "WIFI";

#define WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE "/spiffs/wifi_credentials.txt"
#define MAX_SSID_LEN 32
#define MAX_PASSWORD_LEN 64
#define WIFI_CONNECTED_BIT BIT0
#define WIFI_FAIL_BIT BIT1
#define MAX_RETRY 2                     // Reduced retries for faster failure detection
#define WIFI_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS 8000 // 8 second timeout

static EventGroupHandle_t s_wifi_event_group = NULL;
static int s_retry_num = 0;
static bool wifi_connected = false;
#if defined(CONFIG_BOARD_P4)
// The remote (esp_hosted) radio on the 4C board is initialized exactly once
// and never deinit'd: the host-side LWIP netif attach is not re-runnable, so a
// second esp_wifi_init() re-adds the persistent netif and asserts (netif_add
// "netif already added"). Power-cycling the radio is stop/start only. The S3
// (built-in radio) does not need this and deinits/reinits freely.
static bool s_wifi_inited = false;
#endif

// Read WiFi credentials from SPIFFS file
static esp_err_t read_wifi_credentials(char *ssid, char *password) {
    FILE *f = fopen(WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE, "r");
    if (f == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to open %s", WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE);
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Please flash SPIFFS with your credentials file");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    char line[256]; // Large buffer to read entire lines including long comments
    bool ssid_found = false;
    bool password_found = false;

    // Read lines, skipping comments and empty lines
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) != NULL) {
        // Remove newline characters
        line[strcspn(line, "\r\n")] = 0;

        // Trim leading whitespace
        char *trimmed = line;
        while (*trimmed == ' ' || *trimmed == '\t') {
            trimmed++;
        }

        // Skip empty lines and comments (lines starting with #)
        if (*trimmed == '\0' || *trimmed == '#') {
            continue;
        }

        // First non-comment line is SSID. strnlen+memcpy: a plain
        // strncpy/snprintf of the 256-byte line into the 32-byte field
        // trips -Wstringop-truncation / -Wformat-truncation under
        // -Werror=all (the P4's GCC 14 RISC-V toolchain) even though the
        // truncation is the point.
        if (!ssid_found) {
            size_t n = strnlen(trimmed, MAX_SSID_LEN - 1);
            memcpy(ssid, trimmed, n);
            ssid[n] = '\0';
            ssid_found = true;
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Found SSID: %s", ssid);
            continue;
        }

        // Second non-comment line is password (same bounded copy)
        if (!password_found) {
            size_t n = strnlen(trimmed, MAX_PASSWORD_LEN - 1);
            memcpy(password, trimmed, n);
            password[n] = '\0';
            password_found = true;
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Found password (length: %d)", strlen(password));
            break;
        }
    }

    fclose(f);

    if (!ssid_found || !password_found) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to read valid SSID and password from credentials file");
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "The file appears to contain only comments or is empty");
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Please add your WiFi SSID on the first non-comment line");
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "and your WiFi password on the second non-comment line");
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Loaded WiFi credentials from %s", WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE);
    return ESP_OK;
}

// Write WiFi credentials to the SPIFFS file (the inverse of
// read_wifi_credentials: first non-comment line = SSID, second = password).
// Comment header mirrors spiffs/wifi_credentials.example.txt so the file
// stays readable when inspected by hand. The password is never logged.
esp_err_t wifi_credentials_write(const char *ssid, const char *password) {
    if (ssid == NULL || password == NULL) {
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG;
    }
    size_t ssid_len = strlen(ssid);
    size_t password_len = strlen(password);
    if (ssid_len == 0 || ssid_len >= MAX_SSID_LEN) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "SSID not writable: empty or too long (%zu chars, max %d)", ssid_len, MAX_SSID_LEN - 1);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE;
    }
    if (password_len == 0 || password_len >= MAX_PASSWORD_LEN) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "Password not writable: empty or too long (%zu chars, max %d)", password_len,
                 MAX_PASSWORD_LEN - 1);
        return ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE;
    }

    FILE *f = fopen(WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE, "w");
    if (f == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to open %s for writing", WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE);
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    fprintf(f, "# WiFi Credentials\n# Line 1: WiFi SSID\n# Line 2: WiFi Password\n%s\n%s\n", ssid, password);
    int rc = fclose(f);
    if (rc != 0) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to write %s", WIFI_CREDENTIALS_FILE);
        return ESP_FAIL;
    }
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Wrote credentials (SSID %zu chars, password %zu chars)", ssid_len, password_len);
    return ESP_OK;
}

// WiFi event handler
static void wifi_event_handler(void *arg, esp_event_base_t event_base, int32_t event_id, void *event_data) {
    // Auto-connect (STA_START) and the disconnect retry are the MANAGER's
    // behaviour and must only run while the manager owns the radio
    // (s_wifi_event_group != NULL). The AP scan brings the radio up on its
    // own (radio_was_up == false) and must not trigger a connect: on the P4
    // the manager's SSID config persists across the stop-only deinit (the
    // remote radio is never esp_wifi_deinit'ed), so a stray esp_wifi_connect()
    // here would start a real association and make the blocking scan fail
    // with ESP_ERR_WIFI_STATE. The same gating stops the zombie "Retry
    // connecting / connection failed" the airplane/light-sleep deinit used to
    // leave behind.
    if (event_base == WIFI_EVENT && event_id == WIFI_EVENT_STA_START) {
        if (s_wifi_event_group) {
            esp_wifi_connect();
        }
    } else if (event_base == WIFI_EVENT && event_id == WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED) {
        if (s_wifi_event_group) {
            if (s_retry_num < MAX_RETRY) {
                esp_wifi_connect();
                s_retry_num++;
                ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Retry connecting to WiFi...");
            } else {
                xEventGroupSetBits(s_wifi_event_group, WIFI_FAIL_BIT);
            }
        }
        wifi_connected = false;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "WiFi connection failed");
    } else if (event_base == IP_EVENT && event_id == IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP) {
        ip_event_got_ip_t *event = (ip_event_got_ip_t *)event_data;
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Got IP:" IPSTR, IP2STR(&event->ip_info.ip));
        s_retry_num = 0;
        wifi_connected = true;
        // Check if event group still exists before setting bits
        if (s_wifi_event_group) {
            xEventGroupSetBits(s_wifi_event_group, WIFI_CONNECTED_BIT);
        }
    }
}

esp_err_t wifi_manager_init(void) {
    // If WiFi is already initialized (e.g., reconnecting after deinit), clean up first
    if (s_wifi_event_group != NULL) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "WiFi already initialized, reinitializing...");

        // Unregister event handlers first to prevent events during cleanup
        esp_event_handler_unregister(WIFI_EVENT, ESP_EVENT_ANY_ID, &wifi_event_handler);
        esp_event_handler_unregister(IP_EVENT, IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP, &wifi_event_handler);

        // Now safe to deinit
        wifi_manager_deinit();
    }

    // Initialize NVS (safe to call multiple times)
    esp_err_t ret = nvs_flash_init();
    if (ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(nvs_flash_erase());
        ret = nvs_flash_init();
    }
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(ret);

    // Mount SPIFFS for WiFi credentials (check if already mounted)
    esp_vfs_spiffs_conf_t spiffs_conf = {
        .base_path = "/spiffs",
        .partition_label = "storage",
        .max_files = 5,
        .format_if_mount_failed = true // Auto-format if mount fails
    };
    ret = esp_vfs_spiffs_register(&spiffs_conf);
    if (ret != ESP_OK && ret != ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to mount SPIFFS (%s)", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Please ensure SPIFFS partition exists and is properly configured");
        return ret;
    }
    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "SPIFFS mounted successfully");
    }

    // Initialize network interface (safe to call multiple times)
    ret = esp_netif_init();
    if (ret != ESP_OK && ret != ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to initialize netif: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Create default event loop if needed (safe to call multiple times)
    ret = esp_event_loop_create_default();
    if (ret != ESP_OK && ret != ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to create event loop: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        return ret;
    }

    // Create default WiFi STA interface if not exists
    if (esp_netif_get_handle_from_ifkey("WIFI_STA_DEF") == NULL) {
        esp_netif_create_default_wifi_sta();
    }

    // Initialize WiFi
#if defined(CONFIG_BOARD_P4)
    // Re-bringing the (already-inited, stopped) remote radio is set_mode+start
    // below — esp_wifi_init is not re-runnable on the host (see
    // wifi_manager_deinit), so it runs only once.
    if (!s_wifi_inited) {
        wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_init(&cfg));
        s_wifi_inited = true;
    }
#else
    wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_init(&cfg));
#endif

    s_wifi_event_group = xEventGroupCreate();

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_handler_instance_register(WIFI_EVENT, ESP_EVENT_ANY_ID, &wifi_event_handler, NULL, NULL));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(
        esp_event_handler_instance_register(IP_EVENT, IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP, &wifi_event_handler, NULL, NULL));

    // Configure WiFi
    char ssid[MAX_SSID_LEN] = {0};
    char password[MAX_PASSWORD_LEN] = {0};

    ret = read_wifi_credentials(ssid, password);
    if (ret != ESP_OK) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "WiFi credentials not configured. Please set valid credentials.");
        return ret;
    }

    wifi_config_t wifi_config = {
        .sta =
            {
                .threshold.authmode = WIFI_AUTH_WPA2_PSK,
            },
    };
    snprintf((char *)wifi_config.sta.ssid, sizeof(wifi_config.sta.ssid), "%s", ssid);
    snprintf((char *)wifi_config.sta.password, sizeof(wifi_config.sta.password), "%s", password);

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_config(WIFI_IF_STA, &wifi_config));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());

    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "WiFi initialization finished");

    // Wait for connection (with timeout)
    EventBits_t bits = xEventGroupWaitBits(s_wifi_event_group, WIFI_CONNECTED_BIT | WIFI_FAIL_BIT, pdFALSE, pdFALSE,
                                           pdMS_TO_TICKS(WIFI_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS));

    if (bits & WIFI_CONNECTED_BIT) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Connected to WiFi SSID: %s", ssid);
        return ESP_OK;
    } else if (bits & WIFI_FAIL_BIT) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Failed to connect to WiFi SSID: %s", ssid);
        return ESP_FAIL;
    } else {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "WiFi connection timeout");
        return ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT;
    }
}

bool wifi_manager_is_connected(void) { return wifi_connected; }

void wifi_manager_deinit(void) {
    if (s_wifi_event_group) {
        vEventGroupDelete(s_wifi_event_group);
        s_wifi_event_group = NULL;
    }
    esp_wifi_stop();
#if !defined(CONFIG_BOARD_P4)
    esp_wifi_deinit();
#endif
    // The remote radio stays inited on the 4C (esp_wifi_deinit would break the
    // host netif re-attach — see s_wifi_inited). wifi_connected drops either way.
    wifi_connected = false;
}

/* ---------------- AP scan (the WiFi settings screen) ----------------
 *
 * The scan runs on its own task (esp_wifi_scan_start blocks ~3 s) and
 * keeps its results in a static buffer the screen polls. The radio's
 * lifecycle is owned by whoever brought it up: the manager (boot /
 * hourly sync, s_wifi_event_group != NULL) or this task. When we
 * bring it up we deinit it again when the scan is done (back to
 * modem sleep; the credentials file is never touched). */
static bool s_scan_running = false;
static wifi_ap_info_t s_scan_aps[WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS];
static int s_scan_count = 0;
static wifi_ap_record_t s_scan_raw[WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS];

static void wifi_scan_task_fn(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    bool radio_was_up = (s_wifi_event_group != NULL);
    bool we_own_radio = false;

    if (!radio_was_up) {
        /* Minimal radio bring-up: no credentials, no connection. The
         * manager's still-registered event handler will attempt
         * esp_wifi_connect() on STA_START; with no SSID configured it
         * fails fast and its event-group writes are NULL-guarded. */
#if defined(CONFIG_BOARD_P4)
        /* The remote radio is always inited (the manager inits it once; see
         * s_wifi_inited) — bring it up with set_mode+start only. */
        esp_err_t ret = esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA);
        if (ret == ESP_OK) {
            we_own_radio = true;
            esp_wifi_start();
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
        }
#else
        wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
        esp_err_t ret = esp_wifi_init(&cfg);
        if (ret == ESP_OK) {
            we_own_radio = true;
            if (esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA) == ESP_OK) {
                esp_wifi_start();
                vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
            } else {
                we_own_radio = false;
            }
        }
#endif
        if (we_own_radio) {
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Scan: radio brought up");
        } else {
            ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Scan: failed to bring up the radio: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
        }
    }

    wifi_scan_config_t scan_cfg = {
        .show_hidden = true,
        .channel = 0,
    };
    esp_err_t ret = esp_wifi_scan_start(&scan_cfg, true);
    if (ret == ESP_OK) {
        uint16_t ap_cnt = 0;
        esp_wifi_scan_get_ap_num(&ap_cnt);
        if (esp_wifi_scan_get_ap_records(&ap_cnt, s_scan_raw) == ESP_OK) {
            s_scan_count = ap_cnt < WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS ? (int)ap_cnt : WIFI_SCAN_MAX_APS;
            for (int i = 0; i < s_scan_count; i++) {
                size_t len = strlen((const char *)s_scan_raw[i].ssid);
                if (len > 32) {
                    len = 32;
                }
                memcpy(s_scan_aps[i].ssid, s_scan_raw[i].ssid, len);
                s_scan_aps[i].ssid[len] = '\0';
                s_scan_aps[i].rssi = s_scan_raw[i].rssi;
                s_scan_aps[i].auth = s_scan_raw[i].authmode;
            }
            ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Scan done: %d APs", s_scan_count);
        } else {
            s_scan_count = 0;
        }
    } else {
        s_scan_count = 0;
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Scan failed: %s", esp_err_to_name(ret));
    }

    if (we_own_radio) {
        esp_wifi_stop();
#if !defined(CONFIG_BOARD_P4)
        esp_wifi_deinit();
#endif
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "Scan: radio down again");
    }
    s_scan_running = false;
    vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

void wifi_scan_begin(void) {
    if (s_scan_running) {
        return;
    }
    s_scan_running = true;
    s_scan_count = 0;
    if (xTaskCreate(wifi_scan_task_fn, "wifi_scan", 6144, NULL, 5, NULL) != pdPASS) {
        s_scan_running = false;
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Scan task creation failed");
    }
}

bool wifi_scan_in_progress(void) { return s_scan_running; }

int wifi_scan_get_results(wifi_ap_info_t *out, int max) {
    if (!out || max <= 0) {
        return 0;
    }
    int n = s_scan_count < max ? s_scan_count : max;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        out[i] = s_scan_aps[i];
    }
    return n;
}
```
