### `host_sim/CMakeLists.txt`

```ini
# Host simulator: builds the DEVICE core (components/moon) + the generated
# host assets and links a PNG-writing CLI. This is the C-vs-NASA gate:
# the exact runtime path (cheap ephemeris, fixed-point rotation,
# gray->RGB565) rendered on the host, image-diffed against NASA with the
# same metrics as the Python prototype.
#
# The albedo source (moon_assets_gen.c) is GENERATED and stays gitignored
# under assets/images/moon/ (see the moon.assets pipeline):
#   assets/images/moon/.venv/bin/python -m moon.assets
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(moon_sim C)

set(MOON_ASSETS_GEN ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../assets/images/moon/moon_assets_gen.c)
if(NOT EXISTS ${MOON_ASSETS_GEN})
    message(FATAL_ERROR
        "Missing generated asset ${MOON_ASSETS_GEN}.\n"
        "Regenerate it with: assets/images/moon/.venv/bin/python -m moon.assets")
endif()

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()
add_compile_options(-O2)

set(MOON_CORE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../components/moon)
set(MOON_HOST ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})

# The portable core's source set (moon_sim and moon_bench both link it):
# the exact device runtime path (cheap ephemeris, fixed-point rotation,
# gray->RGB565) plus the vendored public-domain ERFA and the generated
# host asset table.
set(MOON_CORE_SRCS
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/moon_astro.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/moon_bake.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/moon_render.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/moon_fixp.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/moon98.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/epv00.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/s2pv.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/pfw06.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/obl06.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/rx.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/rz.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/cp.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/ir.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/rxp.c
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa/rxpv.c
    ${MOON_HOST}/../components/moon/host/moon_host_assets.c
    ${MOON_ASSETS_GEN}
)

set(MOON_CORE_INCS
    ${MOON_CORE}/include
    ${MOON_CORE}/core/erfa
    ${MOON_HOST}
    ${MOON_CORE}/../..
)

add_executable(moon_sim main.c ${MOON_CORE_SRCS})
target_include_directories(moon_sim PRIVATE ${MOON_CORE_INCS})
target_link_libraries(moon_sim PRIVATE m)

# The performance bench (book chapter 19): times the device path's
# steps (geometry, relief build, bake, rotate, shade map, re-project)
# across disk sizes on the host.
add_executable(moon_bench bench.c ${MOON_CORE_SRCS})
target_include_directories(moon_bench PRIVATE ${MOON_CORE_INCS})
target_link_libraries(moon_bench PRIVATE m)
```

### `host_sim/bench.c`

```c
/* Performance bench for the portable moon core: times the device path's
 * individual steps (geometry, relief build, bake, rotate, shade-map
 * build, re-project) on the host. The numbers in the book's Part IV
 * (chapter 19) come from this file + the Python/JS comparators:
 *
 *   host_sim/build/moon_bench --utc 2026-04-15T12:00 --sizes 200 240 320 400 466 618 650
 *
 * Build: the moon_sim target's source set + bench.c (see bench CMake or
 * the book's commands). All times are wall clock, average of --iters
 * bakes (the relief build is reported once, first run only).
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "moon.h"
#include "moon_assets.h"
#include "moon_consts.h"

static double now_ms(void) {
    struct timespec ts;
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (double)ts.tv_sec * 1e3 + (double)ts.tv_nsec / 1e6;
}

/* ISO "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" -> epoch seconds (same civil math as main.c). */
static int parse_iso(const char *s, int64_t *epoch) {
    int y, m, d, h, mi;
    if (sscanf(s, "%d-%d-%dT%d:%d", &y, &m, &d, &h, &mi) < 3)
        return 0;
    y -= m <= 2;
    int era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
    int yoe = y - era * 400;
    int doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
    int doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    *epoch = ((long long)era * 146097 + doe - 719468) * 86400LL + h * 3600LL + mi * 60LL;
    return 1;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    const char *iso = "2026-04-15T12:00";
    int iters = 5;
    int sizes[16], nsizes = 0;
    int no_relief = 0, darkzero = 0, neutral = 0;

    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--utc"))
            iso = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--iters"))
            iters = atoi(argv[++i]);
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--sizes")) {
            while (i + 1 < argc && argv[i + 1][0] != '-') {
                if (nsizes < 16)
                    sizes[nsizes++] = atoi(argv[++i]);
            }
        } else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--no-relief"))
            no_relief = 1;
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--darkzero"))
            darkzero = 1;
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--neutral"))
            neutral = 1;
    }
    if (nsizes == 0)
        sizes[nsizes++] = 400;
    if (neutral)
        moon_gray565_set_warm(0);

    int64_t epoch;
    if (!parse_iso(iso, &epoch)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "bad time '%s'\n", iso);
        return 1;
    }

    /* geometry: average of iters calls (the ERFA series; per frame on
     * the device too -- one per bake). */
    moon_geom_t g;
    double t0 = now_ms();
    for (int k = 0; k < iters; k++)
        moon_geometry(epoch, &g);
    double geo_ms = (now_ms() - t0) / iters;
    printf("utc=%s  geo=%.1f ms/call  relief=%s  darkzero=%d\n", iso, geo_ms, no_relief ? "off" : "on", darkzero);

    const uint8_t *alb = moon_albedo();
    /* relief build: first run only (the device builds it once at boot). */
    const moon_grel_t *grel = NULL;
    double relief_ms = -1;
    if (!no_relief) {
        t0 = now_ms();
        grel = moon_relief();
        relief_ms = now_ms() - t0;
    } else {
        moon_relief(); /* still build it so the no-relief A/B is the bake's */
        grel = NULL;
    }
    if (!alb || (grel == NULL && !no_relief)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "no albedo/relief\n");
        return 1;
    }

    for (int s = 0; s < nsizes; s++) {
        int size = sizes[s];
        int radius = size / 2, center = size / 2;
        uint8_t *frame = malloc((size_t)size * size);
        uint16_t *rgb = malloc((size_t)size * size * 2);

        /* bake: the per-pixel model (bake is the expensive step). */
        t0 = now_ms();
        for (int k = 0; k < iters; k++)
            moon_bake(&g, alb, grel, frame, size, (float)radius, (float)center, (float)center, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H,
                      darkzero, 0.0f);
        double bake_ms = (now_ms() - t0) / iters;

        /* rotate: the spin's per-frame gather (Q15.15 + fused LUT). */
        float th = 0.7;
        t0 = now_ms();
        for (int k = 0; k < iters; k++)
            moon_rotate(frame, size, rgb, size, center, center, center, center, moon_cos15(th), moon_sin15(th));
        double rot_ms = (now_ms() - t0) / iters;

        /* re-project: the dusk's per-frame map gather (one map load/px). */
        uint8_t *map = malloc((size_t)MOON_ALB_W * MOON_ALB_H);
        t0 = now_ms();
        moon_shade_map_build(&g, alb, grel, map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 1, 0.1f);
        double map_ms = now_ms() - t0;
        t0 = now_ms();
        for (int k = 0; k < iters; k++)
            moon_reproject(map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, &g, frame, size, (float)radius, (float)center, (float)center);
        double reproj_ms = (now_ms() - t0) / iters;

        printf("size=%4d  bake=%8.2f ms  rotate=%6.2f ms  mapbuild=%8.2f ms  reproj=%6.2f ms\n", size, bake_ms, rot_ms,
               map_ms, reproj_ms);
        free(frame);
        free(rgb);
        free(map);
    }
    if (relief_ms >= 0)
        printf("relief build (once): %.1f ms (%.0f px DEM)\n", relief_ms, (double)MOON_DEM_W * MOON_DEM_H);
    return 0;
}
```

### `host_sim/check_gate.py`

```python
"""C-simulator gate (Phase 3, step 3 of the approved plan):
"host_sim PNGs vs final_400x400 with the same metrics, within ~2 MAE of the
Python full model."

This runs two diffs over the 32-frame set, both at 5-bit panel fidelity
(the device shows a 466x466 RGB565 panel; gray -> 5-bit is exact 1:1):

  1. C  vs NASA  -- the runtime path (eraEpv00+eraMoon98 ephemeris,
     fixed-point rotation, gray->RGB565) against the NASA SVS 5415 frames.
     Gate: per-frame MAE <= 12 (same metric as the prototype gate).
     Mean content SSIM is reported for context.

  2. C  vs Python model -- porting fidelity. The Python prototype (float
     astropy ephemeris, the same banded relief-DEM lighting as the C core,
     5-bit quantized) is the validated reference; the C core must reproduce
     it within ~2 MAE per frame. Both are pixel-aligned (identical disk
     geometry, no registration), so this is a direct pixel diff of the two
     panels' renders. Gate: per-frame MAE <= 2.

If the C port is faithful (check 2), check 1 inherits the prototype's
NASA agreement -- the residual between the two is exactly the porting
error. Running both keeps the fidelity claim explicit instead of implicit.

Run:  python check_gate.py [--sim build/moon_sim] [--out /tmp/moon-sim-gate]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
MOON_PKG = os.path.normpath(
    os.path.join(HERE, "..", "assets", "images", "moon"))
sys.path.insert(0, MOON_PKG)

from moon import assets as A                 # noqa: E402
from moon import constants as C              # noqa: E402
from moon.astro import geometry              # noqa: E402
from moon.metrics import to_gray             # noqa: E402
from moon.metrics import disk_metrics        # noqa: E402
from moon.register import register_shift     # noqa: E402
from moon.validate import _iso, select_frames  # noqa: E402

REF_DIR = os.path.join(MOON_PKG, "final_400x400")

# Porting-fidelity gate (plan: "within ~2 MAE of the Python full model").
MAE_C_VS_PY = 2.0


def q565(u8: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Exact 1:1 gray -> 5-bit -> gray (the panel's quantization)."""
    q = (u8.astype(np.uint32) * 31 + 127) // 255
    return ((q * 255 + 15) // 31).astype(np.uint8)


def load_gray(path: str) -> np.ndarray:
    im = Image.open(path).convert("L")
    return np.asarray(im, dtype=np.float64)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--sim", default=os.path.join(HERE, "build", "moon_sim"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/moon-sim-gate")
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--json", default="/tmp/moon-research/mooninfo_2025.json")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    rec = json.load(open(args.json))
    frames = select_frames(rec, args.frames)
    alb = A.bake_albedo(A.load_albedo())
    dem, dem_lo, dem_hi = A.bake_dem(A.load_height())
    mps = (dem_hi - dem_lo) / A.DEM_STEPS
    lut = np.asarray(C.TONE_LUT, dtype=np.uint8)

    # --- C output: run the simulator over the frame list -------------------
    list_path = os.path.join(args.out, "frames.txt")
    with open(list_path, "w") as f:
        for i, _ph in frames:
            f.write(_iso(rec[i]["time"]) + "\n")
    # --neutral: the display's warm gray->565 tint is an ARTISTIC choice
    # (see moon_render.c g565_build). The gate validates the PHYSICS
    # (neutral gray vs NASA / vs the Python prototype), so it renders the
    # neutral LUT -- the tint never enters the gate numbers.
    r = subprocess.run([args.sim, "--list", list_path, "--size", "400",
                        "--neutral", "--out", args.out],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print("simulator failed:\n" + r.stdout + r.stderr)
        return 2

    # --- Python model: 5-bit render_from_assets per frame ------------------
    py_dir = os.path.join(args.out, "py")
    os.makedirs(py_dir, exist_ok=True)
    for k, (i, _ph) in enumerate(frames):
        p = A._ref_path(i, MOON_PKG)
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        g = geometry(_iso(rec[i]["time"]))
        raw, d = A.render_from_assets(g, alb, dem, mps)
        out = q565(A.to_uint8(A.tonemap(raw, d, lut)))
        Image.fromarray(out, mode="L").save(os.path.join(py_dir, "py.%04d.png" % k))

    # --- diff both ways ----------------------------------------------------
    rows = []
    for k, (i, phase) in enumerate(frames):
        sp = os.path.join(args.out, "sim.%04d.png" % k)
        pp = os.path.join(py_dir, "py.%04d.png" % k)
        rp = os.path.join(REF_DIR, "moon.%04d.png" % (i + 1))
        if not (os.path.exists(sp) and os.path.exists(pp) and os.path.exists(rp)):
            print("  missing %s / %s / %s" % (sp, pp, rp))
            continue
        sim = load_gray(sp)
        py = load_gray(pp)
        ref_rgba = np.asarray(Image.open(rp))
        ref = np.asarray(Image.open(rp).convert("L"), dtype=np.float64)

        # 1. C vs NASA (registered, disk metrics -- the prototype's metric).
        shifted, _sh = register_shift(sim, ref)
        m = disk_metrics(None, ref_rgba, shifted=shifted)
        # 2. C vs Python model (direct pixel diff, aligned).
        c_vs_py = float(np.mean(np.abs(sim - py)))
        rows.append((i + 1, phase, m["mae"], m["ssim"], c_vs_py))

    print("\n== C-simulator gate (32-frame set) ==")
    print("  frame  phase    C-NASA   SSIM   C-Python")
    for i, phase, mae, ssim, cp in rows:
        flags = (" *" if mae > C.MAE_MAX else "") + (" ~" if cp > MAE_C_VS_PY else "")
        print("  %4d  %6.2f  %6.2f %6.3f   %5.2f%s" % (i, phase, mae, ssim, cp, flags))

    mae_nasa = np.mean([r_[2] for r_ in rows])
    ssim_nasa = np.mean([r_[3] for r_ in rows])
    mae_py = np.mean([r_[4] for r_ in rows])
    n_nasa = sum(1 for r_ in rows if r_[2] > C.MAE_MAX)
    n_py = sum(1 for r_ in rows if r_[4] > MAE_C_VS_PY)
    print("  C vs NASA : mean MAE %.2f (max %.2f, %d frames > %.0f)  "
          "mean content SSIM %.3f"
          % (mae_nasa, max(r_[2] for r_ in rows), n_nasa, C.MAE_MAX, ssim_nasa))
    print("  C vs Python: mean MAE %.2f (max %.2f, %d frames > %.0f)"
          % (mae_py, max(r_[4] for r_ in rows), n_py, MAE_C_VS_PY))

    ok = (n_nasa == 0) and (n_py == 0)
    print("  gate: C-NASA per-frame MAE <= %.0f  AND  C-Python per-frame MAE <= %.0f"
          % (C.MAE_MAX, MAE_C_VS_PY))
    print("  ->  %s" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

### `host_sim/dark_test.c`

```c
/* Throwaway: print C bake geometry + frame bytes at named pixels to settle
 * the dark-side speckle diagnosis. Not part of the gate.
 *
 * Build:
 *   cc -O2 -Imoon/include -I. dark_test.c <core objs> -o dark_test
 * Run: ./dark_test "2026-10-05T12:00" 466 241,414 250,420 233,33
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "moon.h"
#include "moon_assets.h"
#include "moon_consts.h"

static long long days_from_civil(int y, int m, int d) {
    y -= m <= 2;
    int era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
    int yoe = y - era * 400;
    int doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
    int doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    return (long long)era * 146097 + doe - 719468;
}

static int64_t parse_iso(const char *s) {
    int y, mo, d, h = 0, mi = 0;
    sscanf(s, "%d-%d-%dT%d:%d", &y, &mo, &d, &h, &mi);
    return days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * 86400LL + h * 3600LL + mi * 60LL;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 4) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: dark_test ISO SIZE x,y ...\n");
        return 2;
    }
    int64_t epoch = parse_iso(argv[1]);
    int size = atoi(argv[2]);
    int radius = (int)MOON_DISK_RADIUS_PX;
    int center = size / 2;

    const uint8_t *alb = moon_albedo();
    const moon_grel_t *grel = moon_relief();
    moon_geom_t g;
    moon_geometry(epoch, &g);
    fprintf(stderr, "epoch=%s  subsolar=(%.2f,%.2f)  illum=%.3f\n", argv[1], g.subsolar_lon, g.subsolar_lat, g.illum);
    fprintf(stderr, "S=(%.4f,%.4f,%.4f) E=(%.4f,%.4f,%.4f)\n", g.S[0], g.S[1], g.S[2], g.E[0], g.E[1], g.E[2]);
    fprintf(stderr, "right=(%.4f,%.4f,%.4f) up=(%.4f,%.4f,%.4f)\n", g.right[0], g.right[1], g.right[2], g.up[0],
            g.up[1], g.up[2]);

    int sz = size;
    static uint8_t *frame0, *frame1;
    frame0 = malloc((size_t)sz * sz);
    frame1 = malloc((size_t)sz * sz);
    moon_bake(&g, alb, grel, frame0, sz, (float)radius, (float)center, (float)center, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
    moon_bake(&g, alb, grel, frame1, sz, (float)radius, (float)center, (float)center, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 1, 0.0f);

    for (int i = 3; i < argc; i++) {
        int x, y;
        if (sscanf(argv[i], "%d,%d", &x, &y) != 2)
            continue;
        float u = ((float)x - (float)center) / (float)radius;
        float v = ((float)center - (float)y) / (float)radius;
        float r2 = u * u + v * v;
        float w = sqrtf(fmaxf(0.0f, 1.0f - r2));
        float rx = u * g.right[0] + v * g.up[0] + w * g.E[0];
        float ry = u * g.right[1] + v * g.up[1] + w * g.E[1];
        float rz = u * g.right[2] + v * g.up[2] + w * g.E[2];
        float d = rx * g.S[0] + ry * g.S[1] + rz * g.S[2];
        /* dark_zero = 1 now writes the COMPUTED backlit night side (not
         * the flat floor), so a d < 0 pixel is non-zero BY DESIGN -- no
         * BUG marker. */
        fprintf(stderr, "px(%d,%d) u=%.4f v=%.4f d=%.5f  gray[dz=0]=%u  gray[dz=1]=%u\n", x, y, u, v, d,
                frame0[y * sz + x], frame1[y * sz + x]);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

### `host_sim/main.c`

```c
/* Moon host simulator: runs the DEVICE code path (cheap ephemeris +
 * fixed-point rotation + gray->RGB565) and writes PNGs, which are
 * image-diffed against NASA with the same gate as the Python prototype
 * (see check_gate.py).
 *
 * Usage:
 *   moon_sim --utc "2025-06-15T12:00" [--rot deg] [--pole deg] [--out DIR]
 *   moon_sim --utc list.txt          (one ISO [rot] [pole] per line -> sim.NNNN.png)
 *   moon_sim --pole deg              (camera basis rotation about the body
 *                                     pole = the device's dusk spin)
 *   moon_sim --frames N --start ISO --end ISO [--out DIR]  (even spacing)
 *
 * Panel modes: --size 466 (device, r=MOON_DISK_RADIUS_PX) or
 * --size 400 (reference geometry, r=199.3 -- the gate).
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "moon.h"
#include "moon_assets.h"
#include "moon_consts.h"

#define STB_IMAGE_WRITE_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "stb_image_write.h"

/* --- ISO "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" -> epoch seconds (UTC) ---------------------- */
static long long days_from_civil(int y, int m, int d) {
    y -= m <= 2;
    int era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
    int yoe = y - era * 400;
    int doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
    int doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    return (long long)era * 146097 + doe - 719468;
}

static int parse_iso(const char *s, int64_t *epoch) {
    int y, mo, d, h, mi;
    if (sscanf(s, "%d-%d-%dT%d:%d", &y, &mo, &d, &h, &mi) < 3)
        return 0;
    *epoch = days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * 86400LL + h * 3600LL + mi * 60LL;
    return 1;
}

/* --- one frame ---------------------------------------------------------- */
static int g_darkzero = 0; /* --darkzero: the device's night side (the computed
                            * backlit surface, dark_zero = 1) */
static int g_neutral = 0;  /* --neutral: the neutral gray->565 LUT (no warm
                            * display tint) -- the image gate runs with this so
                            * its metrics validate the physics, not the tint */
static int g_pole_deg = 0; /* --pole: camera basis rotation about the body
                            * pole (+z), deg -- the device's dusk spin
                            * (moon_ui.c moon_pole_geometry, copied
                            * 1:1). The pole stays at the top of the
                            * disk; the light source S stays put, so
                            * the terminator sweeps the disk. */

/* The pole spin, host-side copy of moon_ui.c moon_pole_geometry:
 * each basis vector's x/y components are rotated about +z (right ->
 * up for +phi), z invariant. */
static void pole_geometry(moon_geom_t *g, float phi) {
    float c = cosf(phi), s = sinf(phi);
    float x, y;
    x = g->right[0];
    y = g->right[1];
    g->right[0] = c * x - s * y;
    g->right[1] = s * x + c * y;
    x = g->up[0];
    y = g->up[1];
    g->up[0] = c * x - s * y;
    g->up[1] = s * x + c * y;
    x = g->E[0];
    y = g->E[1];
    g->E[0] = c * x - s * y;
    g->E[1] = s * x + c * y;
}

static int render_one(const char *iso, int rot_deg, int pole_deg, int size, const char *out_path, int idx) {
    int64_t epoch;
    if (!parse_iso(iso, &epoch)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "bad time '%s'\n", iso);
        return 0;
    }

    int radius, center;
    if (size == 400) {
        radius = 199;
        center = 199; /* rot=0 must be identity: rot center == gather center */
    } else if (size == 466) {
        radius = (int)MOON_DISK_RADIUS_PX; /* device panel: r=200 disk, 33px margin */
        center = size / 2;
    } else {
        radius = size / 2; /* sweep intermediate: full disk in an S x S bake */
        center = size / 2;
    }

    const uint8_t *alb = moon_albedo();
    const moon_grel_t *grel = moon_relief();
    if (!alb || !grel) {
        fprintf(stderr, "no albedo/relief\n");
        return 0;
    }

    static uint8_t *frame;
    static uint16_t *rgb;
    if (!frame)
        frame = malloc((size_t)size * size);
    if (!rgb)
        rgb = malloc((size_t)size * size * 2);

    moon_geom_t g;
    moon_geometry(epoch, &g);
    if (pole_deg) {
        pole_geometry(&g, (float)pole_deg * 0.017453292519943295f);
    }

    float fr = size == 400 ? 199.3f : (float)radius;
    float fc = size == 400 ? 199.3f : (float)(size / 2);
    float fcy = size == 400 ? 199.5f : (float)(size / 2);
    moon_bake(&g, alb, grel, frame, size, fr, fc, fcy, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, g_darkzero, 0.0f);

    float th = (float)rot_deg * 0.017453292519943295f;
    int32_t c15 = moon_cos15(th);
    int32_t s15 = moon_sin15(th);
    int fsize = size;
    int fcx = center, fcyi = center;
    moon_rotate(frame, fsize, rgb, size, center, center, fcx, fcyi, c15, s15);

    /* RGB565 -> RGB24 for the PNG (the exact panel pixel). */
    static uint8_t *px;
    if (!px)
        px = malloc((size_t)size * size * 3);
    for (int i = 0; i < size * size; i++) {
        /* Decode the exact panel pixel: R5 (5-bit), G6 (6-bit), B5 (5-bit).
         * Green must be read as 6 bits and scaled by /63 -- decoding it as 5
         * bits (/31) would hide the encoder's green-width in the PNG. */
        uint16_t v = rgb[i];
        int r5 = v >> 11, g6 = (v >> 5) & 63, b5 = v & 31;
        px[i * 3 + 0] = (uint8_t)((r5 * 255 + 15) / 31);
        px[i * 3 + 1] = (uint8_t)((g6 * 255 + 31) / 63);
        px[i * 3 + 2] = (uint8_t)((b5 * 255 + 15) / 31);
    }

    char p[512];
    if (idx >= 0)
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/sim.%04d.png", out_path, idx);
    else
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/sim.png", out_path);
    if (stbi_write_png(p, size, size, 3, px, size * 3) == 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "write failed: %s\n", p);
        return 0;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "%s  utc=%s  rot=%d  phase=%.2f%%  ss=(%.2f,%.2f)\n", p, iso, rot_deg, g.illum * 100.0,
            g.subsolar_lon, g.subsolar_lat);
    return 1;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    const char *iso = NULL;
    const char *list = NULL;
    int frames = 0;
    const char *start = NULL, *end = NULL;
    const char *out = "/tmp/moon-sim";
    int rot = 0;
    int size = 400;

    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--utc"))
            iso = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--list"))
            list = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--frames"))
            frames = atoi(argv[++i]);
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--start"))
            start = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--end"))
            end = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--out"))
            out = argv[++i];
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--darkzero"))
            g_darkzero = 1;
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--rot"))
            rot = atoi(argv[++i]);
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--pole"))
            g_pole_deg = atoi(argv[++i]);
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--size"))
            size = atoi(argv[++i]);
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--neutral"))
            g_neutral = 1;
    }

    if (g_neutral)
        moon_gray565_set_warm(0);

    if (mkdir(out, 0755) != 0) {
        /* exists */
    }

    int ok = 0;
    if (list) {
        FILE *f = fopen(list, "r");
        if (!f) {
            fprintf(stderr, "no list %s\n", list);
            return 1;
        }
        char line[256];
        int idx = 0;
        while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) {
            int r = rot, p = g_pole_deg; /* one "ISO [rot] [pole]" per line */
            char *sp = strchr(line, ' ');
            if (sp) {
                *sp = 0;
                r = atoi(sp + 1);
                char *sp2 = strchr(sp + 1, ' ');
                if (sp2) {
                    *sp2 = 0;
                    p = atoi(sp2 + 1);
                }
            }
            line[strcspn(line, "\n")] = 0;
            if (*line)
                ok += render_one(line, r, p, size, out, idx);
            idx++;
        }
        fclose(f);
        printf("%d frames -> %s\n", ok, out);
        return ok == idx ? 0 : 1;
    }

    if (frames > 0 && start && end) {
        int64_t e0, e1;
        if (!parse_iso(start, &e0) || !parse_iso(end, &e1)) {
            fprintf(stderr, "bad --start/--end\n");
            return 1;
        }
        for (int k = 0; k < frames; k++) {
            double t = frames == 1 ? 0.0 : (double)k / (frames - 1);
            int64_t e = (int64_t)(e0 + t * ((double)e1 - e0));
            char iso2[40];
            {
                long long days = e / 86400LL;
                int64_t rem = e % 86400LL;
                if (rem < 0)
                    rem += 86400;
                int h = (int)(rem / 3600), mi = (int)((rem % 3600) / 60);
                /* civil from days */
                long long z = days + 719468LL;
                long long era = (z >= 0 ? z : z - 146096) / 146097;
                unsigned yoe = (unsigned)(z - era * 146097);
                int y = (int)(era * 400 + (yoe - yoe / 1460 + yoe / 36520 - yoe / 146000));
                int doy = (int)(yoe - (y / 4 - y / 100 + y / 400));
                int mp = (int)((5 * doy + 2) / 153);
                int d = (int)(doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1);
                int m = mp + (mp < 10 ? 3 : -9);
                if (m <= 2)
                    y++;
                snprintf(iso2, sizeof iso2, "%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d", y, m, d, h, mi);
            }
            ok += render_one(iso2, rot, g_pole_deg, size, out, k);
        }
        printf("%d frames -> %s\n", ok, out);
        return ok == frames ? 0 : 1;
    }

    if (iso)
        return render_one(iso, rot, g_pole_deg, size, out, -1) ? 0 : 1;

    fprintf(stderr, "usage: moon_sim --utc ISO|--list FILE|--frames N --start S --end E\n"
                    "                [--rot deg] [--pole deg] [--size 400|466] [--out DIR] [--darkzero]\n");
    return 2;
}
```

### `host_sim/newmoon_test.c`

```c
/* Throwaway dev probe: verify the new_moon_epoch() coarse+fine scan
 * (duplicated 1:1 from components/ui/moon_ui.c) against the cheap
 * ephemeris: it must return the darkest epoch of the last ~29.53 d,
 * with illumination near 0 and a sane span.
 *
 * Build:
 *   cc -O2 -Imoon/include -I. newmoon_test.c <core objs> -lm -o newmoon_test
 * Run: ./newmoon_test "2026-10-27T12:00"
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "moon.h"

static long long days_from_civil(int y, int m, int d) {
    y -= m <= 2;
    int era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
    int yoe = y - era * 400;
    int doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
    int doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    return (long long)era * 146097 + doe - 719468;
}

static int64_t parse_iso(const char *s) {
    int y, mo, d, h = 0, mi = 0;
    sscanf(s, "%d-%d-%dT%d:%d", &y, &mo, &d, &h, &mi);
    return days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * 86400LL + h * 3600LL + mi * 60LL;
}

/* 1:1 copy of components/ui/moon_ui.c::new_moon_epoch. */
static int64_t new_moon_epoch(int64_t utc_epoch) {
    moon_geom_t g;
    int64_t best = utc_epoch - (int64_t)(29.53 * 86400);
    float best_illum = 1.0f;
    for (int64_t e = utc_epoch - (int64_t)(6 * 3600); e >= utc_epoch - (int64_t)(29.53 * 86400); e -= 6 * 3600) {
        g.illum = 1.0f;
        moon_geometry(e, &g);
        if (g.illum < best_illum - 1e-6f) {
            best_illum = g.illum;
            best = e;
        }
    }
    int64_t fine_best = best;
    float fine_illum = best_illum;
    for (int64_t e = best + 6 * 3600; e >= best - 6 * 3600; e -= 20 * 60) {
        g.illum = 1.0f;
        moon_geometry(e, &g);
        if (g.illum < fine_illum - 1e-6f) {
            fine_illum = g.illum;
            fine_best = e;
        }
    }
    return fine_best;
}

static void fmt(int64_t e, char *out, size_t n) {
    time_t t = (time_t)e;
    struct tm *lt = gmtime(&t);
    strftime(out, n, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC", lt);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int64_t now = argc > 1 ? parse_iso(argv[1]) : 1761600000;
    char ts[64];
    moon_geom_t g;
    moon_geometry(now, &g);
    fmt(now, ts, sizeof ts);
    printf("now            = %s  illum=%.4f\n", ts, g.illum);
    int64_t nm = new_moon_epoch(now);
    moon_geom_t gn;
    moon_geometry(nm, &gn);
    fmt(nm, ts, sizeof ts);
    double span_d = (double)(now - nm) / 86400.0;
    printf("new moon       = %s  illum=%.4f  span=%.2f d\n", ts, gn.illum, span_d);
    /* Brute-force check on a fine grid over the WHOLE 29.53 d window
     * (now -> now-29.53 d): the scan's result must be within 1 fine step
     * (20 min) of the true minimum. */
    moon_geom_t g0;
    float min_illum = 1.0f;
    int64_t min_e = now;
    for (int64_t e = now; e >= now - (int64_t)(29.53 * 86400); e -= 20 * 60) {
        g0.illum = 1.0f;
        moon_geometry(e, &g0);
        if (g0.illum < min_illum) {
            min_illum = g0.illum;
            min_e = e;
        }
    }
    int64_t off = (nm > min_e) ? nm - min_e : min_e - nm;
    printf("brute-force min = illum=%.4f  |scan-min| offset = %lld s (%.0f min)\n", min_illum, (long long)off,
           off / 60.0);
    return (gn.illum < 0.05f && span_d > 0.5 && span_d <= 29.53 && off < 40 * 60) ? 0 : 1;
}
```

### `host_sim/pole_test.c`

```c
/* Throwaway dev probe: verify the sleep "dusk" pole-spin geometry
 * (duplicated 1:1 from components/ui/moon_ui.c) against the device
 * runtime path:
 *
 *   1. IN-PLANE FOLD: baking the camera basis pre-rotated about the view
 *      axis E by the free-spin angle theta must reproduce the on-screen
 *      pose, i.e. the bake at (right, up) rotated in place by
 *      moon_rotate(theta) -- the light-sleep entry seam. MAE must be
 *      tiny (sub-1-gray over the disk) at several epochs/angles.
 *
 *   2. ENDPOINT: the pole rotation phi* = atan2(-B, -A) (A = E0S0+E1S1,
 *      B = E0S1-E1S0, so E(phi).S = A cos + B sin + C) must sit at the
 *      numeric minimum of E(phi).S over the full circle (the visible
 *      disk as dark as the geometry allows), and the rendered frame at
 *      phi* must show the dark side with some contrast (earthshine +
 *      relief-lit rims, dark_zero = 0) -- the deep-sleep entry frame.
 *      NOTE: this probe keeps dark_zero = 0 to verify the earthshine
 *      MODEL; the DEVICE dusk/endpoint now renders the night side flat
 *      black (dark_zero = 1, T2/T3), so it never displays this contrast.
 *
 * Build:
 *   cc -O2 -Imoon/include -I. pole_test.c <core objs> -lm -o pole_test
 * Run: ./pole_test
 */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "moon.h"
#include "moon_assets.h"
#include "moon_consts.h"

/* Device geometry: 400x400 disk, radius 200, center (200,200). */
#define PX 400
#define RAD 200.0f
#define CTR 200.0f

/* 1:1 copies of components/ui/moon_ui.c. */
static void moon_inplane_geometry(const moon_geom_t *src, float theta, moon_geom_t *dst) {
    *dst = *src;
    float c = cosf(theta), s = sinf(theta);
    float r[3] = {src->right[0], src->right[1], src->right[2]};
    float u[3] = {src->up[0], src->up[1], src->up[2]};
    dst->right[0] = c * r[0] + s * u[0];
    dst->right[1] = c * r[1] + s * u[1];
    dst->right[2] = c * r[2] + s * u[2];
    dst->up[0] = -s * r[0] + c * u[0];
    dst->up[1] = -s * r[1] + c * u[1];
    dst->up[2] = -s * r[2] + c * u[2];
    /* E unchanged (in-plane axis). */
}

static void moon_pole_geometry(const moon_geom_t *src, float phi, moon_geom_t *dst) {
    *dst = *src;
    float c = cosf(phi), s = sinf(phi);
    float a[3] = {src->right[0], src->right[1], src->right[2]};
    float b[3] = {src->up[0], src->up[1], src->up[2]};
    float e[3] = {src->E[0], src->E[1], src->E[2]};
    dst->right[0] = c * a[0] - s * a[1];
    dst->right[1] = s * a[0] + c * a[1];
    dst->right[2] = a[2];
    dst->up[0] = c * b[0] - s * b[1];
    dst->up[1] = s * b[0] + c * b[1];
    dst->up[2] = b[2];
    dst->E[0] = c * e[0] - s * e[1];
    dst->E[1] = s * e[0] + c * e[1];
    dst->E[2] = e[2];
}

static long long days_from_civil(int y, int m, int d) {
    y -= m <= 2;
    int era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
    int yoe = y - era * 400;
    int doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
    int doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
    return (long long)era * 146097 + doe - 719468;
}

static int64_t iso(const char *s) {
    int y, mo, d;
    sscanf(s, "%d-%d-%d", &y, &mo, &d);
    return days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * 86400LL;
}

static int g_fail;

/* Bake the current phase at the plain Earth viewport, then rotate in
 * place by theta (the on-screen free-spin pose). */
static void bake_screen_pose(int64_t epoch, float theta, uint8_t *out) {
    moon_geom_t g;
    moon_geometry(epoch, &g);
    moon_bake(&g, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), out, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
    if (theta != 0.0f) {
        static uint16_t rgb[PX * PX];
        int32_t c15 = moon_cos15(theta), s15 = moon_sin15(theta);
        moon_rotate(out, PX, rgb, PX, CTR, CTR, (int)CTR, (int)CTR, c15, s15);
        /* Decode back to 8-bit gray (nearest): rgb -> g via the gray565
         * LUT is 1:1 for neutral grays, so the max g with g565(g) == v
         * recovers g within the LUT's rounding. */
        for (int i = 0; i < PX * PX; i++) {
            int best = 0, bd = 0xFFFF;
            for (int gr = 0; gr < 256; gr++) {
                int d = (int)rgb[i] - moon_gray565(gr);
                d = d < 0 ? -d : d;
                if (d < bd) {
                    bd = d;
                    best = gr;
                }
            }
            out[i] = (uint8_t)best;
        }
    }
}

int main(void) {
    if (!moon_albedo() || !moon_relief()) {
        fprintf(stderr, "no assets\n");
        return 1;
    }
    const char *epochs[] = {"2026-10-27", "2026-10-20", "2026-11-05"};
    const float thetas[] = {0.3f, -1.1f, 2.4f, 5.9f};
    static uint8_t a[2 * PX * PX], b[PX * PX];
    int64_t now = iso("2026-10-27");

    printf("== 1. in-plane fold (bake at theta-folded basis vs on-screen pose)\n");
    for (unsigned e = 0; e < 3; e++) {
        int64_t epoch = e == 1 ? iso(epochs[e]) : now - 7 * 86400LL * (int)e;
        moon_geom_t g0;
        moon_geometry(epoch, &g0);
        for (unsigned t = 0; t < 4; t++) {
            float th = thetas[t];
            bake_screen_pose(epoch, th, a);
            moon_geom_t gb, gwrong;
            moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, th, &gb);
            moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, -th, &gwrong);
            moon_bake(&gb, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), b, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
            moon_bake(&gwrong, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), a + PX * PX, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0,
                      0.0f);
            /* NOTE: the on-screen pose is moon_rotate's NEAREST-NEIGHBOR
             * gather (an integer 1-px sample of the unrotated bake), while
             * the folded basis bakes the sphere EXACTLY per pixel. The
             * residual is the inherent 1-px sampling difference (large
             * only at the terminator), NOT a geometry error. The sign is
             * verified against the WRONG-sign fold: a mis-signed fold
             * misaligns the terminator by 2*th (tens of gray), so the
             * right sign must be far closer. */
            double sum = 0, sumw = 0;
            int mx = 0, mxw = 0, lit = 0;
            for (int y = 0; y < PX; y++)
                for (int x = 0; x < PX; x++) {
                    float u = (x - 199.5f) / 200.0f, v = (199.5f - y) / 200.0f;
                    if (u * u + v * v > 1.0f)
                        continue;
                    int d = (int)a[y * PX + x] - (int)b[y * PX + x];
                    int dw = (int)a[y * PX + x] - (int)a[PX * PX + y * PX + x];
                    d = d < 0 ? -d : d;
                    dw = dw < 0 ? -dw : dw;
                    sum += d;
                    sumw += dw;
                    if (d > mx)
                        mx = d;
                    if (dw > mxw)
                        mxw = dw;
                    if (b[y * PX + x] > 8)
                        lit++;
                }
            double mae = sum / (double)lit, maw = sumw / (double)lit;
            printf("  epoch=%ld th=%+.2f rad: right MAE=%.2f max=%d | wrong MAE=%.2f max=%d\n",
                   (long)(epoch - now) / 86400, th, mae, mx, maw, mxw);
            /* Inherent 1-px gather mismatch (terminator) + right sign
             * must beat the wrong sign. 2.5x floor: the margin shrinks
             * on an already-dark-starting disk (epoch -14 d, E.S = -0.88
             * at the start: the view is nearly azimuthally symmetric, so
             * a small +/-th fold is almost identical either way). */
            if (mae > 6.0 || maw < mae * 2.5)
                g_fail++;
        }
    }

    printf("== 2. pole-spin endpoint (E(phi).S minimum)\n");
    for (unsigned e = 0; e < 3; e++) {
        int64_t epoch = e == 1 ? iso(epochs[e]) : now - 7 * 86400LL * (int)e;
        moon_geom_t g0;
        moon_geometry(epoch, &g0);
        float A = g0.E[0] * g0.S[0] + g0.E[1] * g0.S[1];
        float B = g0.E[0] * g0.S[1] - g0.E[1] * g0.S[0];
        float phi = atan2f(-B, -A); /* analytic shortest arc to the dark side */
        float fmin = A * cosf(phi) + B * sinf(phi) + g0.E[2] * g0.S[2];
        /* Numeric check: the full circle on a 0.5 deg grid. */
        float best = 1e9f;
        for (int i = 0; i < 720; i++) {
            float p = (float)i * (6.283185307179586 / 720.0);
            float ev = A * cosf(p) + B * sinf(p) + g0.E[2] * g0.S[2];
            if (ev < best)
                best = ev;
        }
        float start = A + g0.E[2] * g0.S[2];                       /* f(0): the on-screen view */
        int frames = (int)lrintf(fabsf(phi) * 57.29577951308232f); /* 1 deg/frame */
        printf("  epoch=%ld d: start E.S=%+.4f  phi*=%+8.2f d  E.S(phi*)=%+.4f  |grid-analytic|=%.5f  frames=%d (%.0f "
               "s @0.5s/f)\n",
               (long)(epoch - now) / 86400, start, phi * 57.29577951308232f, fmin, fabsf(best - fmin), frames,
               frames * 0.5);
        if (phi > 3.1415927f || phi < -3.1415927f || fabsf(best - fmin) > 0.01f || fmin > -0.5f)
            g_fail++;
        /* Render the endpoint frame: the dark side must still show
         * contrast (earthshine ramp + relief-lit rims), dark_zero = 0. */
        moon_geom_t gb;
        moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, 0.0f, &gb);
        moon_pole_geometry(&gb, phi, &gb);
        moon_bake(&gb, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), b, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
        int lit = 0, dark_hi = 0, dark_cnt = 0;
        long long sum = 0;
        for (int y = 0; y < PX; y++)
            for (int x = 0; x < PX; x++) {
                int g = b[y * PX + x];
                if (g > 16)
                    lit++;
                else if (g > 0)
                    dark_cnt++;
                if (g > dark_hi)
                    dark_hi = g;
                sum += g;
            }
        printf("    endpoint frame: lit px=%d  dark-side px>0=%d  dark max=%d  mean=%.1f\n", lit, dark_cnt, dark_hi,
               (double)sum / (PX * PX));
        if (dark_hi < 4)
            g_fail++; /* no contrast: the dark side would be invisible */
    }

    printf("== 3. constant-projection (shade map + reproject) vs per-frame bake\n"
           "    The dusk's promise: a pole spin at a fixed epoch re-projects ONE\n"
           "    pre-shaded body-frame map (no per-frame shadow recompute) instead\n"
           "    of re-baking. The error must be the cell-center-vs-pixel lighting\n"
           "    difference ALONE -- it must not grow with the fold angle (the map\n"
           "    is view-independent: only the basis changes between frames).\n");
    /* Acceptance: the map is a constant, so the re-projected frame differs
     * from the per-frame bake only by the map's CELL-CENTER lighting (the
     * lighting is evaluated once per 0.42 x 0.42 deg cell, not per pixel):
     *   - the mean error must stay small (the lighting is smooth), and
     *   - the spikes (relief-shadow rims straddling a cell boundary) must
     *     be rare, NOT grow with the fold angle (view independence: the
     *     same cells light the same surface points every frame -- they
     *     rotate rigidly with the disk, they cannot flicker), and
     *   - between consecutive frames the re-projected path must move the
     *     image by the SAME amount as the re-baked one (the temporal
     *     delta is the genuine 1 deg roll of the content, identical for
     *     both -- the map adds no frame-to-frame shimmer). */
    static uint8_t shade_map[MOON_ALB_W * MOON_ALB_H];
    for (unsigned e = 0; e < 3; e++) {
        int64_t epoch = e == 1 ? iso(epochs[e]) : now - 7 * 86400LL * (int)e;
        moon_geom_t g0;
        moon_geometry(epoch, &g0);
        /* Build the map ONCE from the unfolded geometry (S is never folded:
         * the folds only touch the camera basis). */
        /* dark_zero = 0: the host gate keeps the earthshine dark side and
         * verifies the re-projected map matches the full bake. The device
         * dusk passes dark_zero = 1 (the computed backlit night side). */
        moon_shade_map_build(&g0, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), shade_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
        const float thetas3[] = {0.3f, -1.1f, 2.4f, 5.9f};
        const float phis3[] = {0.0f, 0.5f, -2.9f, 0.7f}; /* the 3rd = a near-endpoint fold */
        for (unsigned t = 0; t < 4; t++) {
            moon_geom_t gb;
            moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, thetas3[t], &gb);
            moon_pole_geometry(&gb, phis3[t], &gb);
            moon_bake(&gb, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), b, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0,
                      0.0f); /* reference */
            moon_reproject(shade_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, &gb, a, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR);
            double sum = 0;
            int mx = 0, n = 0, big = 0;
            for (int y = 0; y < PX; y++)
                for (int x = 0; x < PX; x++) {
                    float u = (x - 199.5f) / 200.0f, v = (199.5f - y) / 200.0f;
                    if (u * u + v * v > 1.0f)
                        continue;
                    int d = (int)a[y * PX + x] - (int)b[y * PX + x];
                    d = d < 0 ? -d : d;
                    sum += d;
                    if (d > mx)
                        mx = d;
                    if (d > 100)
                        big++;
                    n++;
                }
            double mae = sum / (double)n;
            double big_pct = 100.0 * (double)big / (double)n;
            /* The baseline pair (phi = 0, small theta) measures the inherent
             * map-vs-bake error; every fold must stay close to it. */
            int baseline = (t == 0);
            printf("  epoch=%ld d th=%+.2f phi=%+.2f rad: MAE=%.2f max=%d px>100=%.2f%% %s\n",
                   (long)(epoch - now) / 86400, thetas3[t], phis3[t], mae, mx, big_pct, baseline ? "(baseline)" : "");
            if (mae > 7.0 || big_pct > 2.0)
                g_fail++;
        }
        /* Temporal: the re-projected path's frame-to-frame motion must
         * match the re-baked path's (the same content rolls 1 deg about
         * the pole; the map adds no shimmer of its own). Coarse 10 deg
         * step to amplify the delta; the device steps 1 deg. */
        moon_geom_t ga, gaa;
        moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, 0.0f, &ga);
        moon_pole_geometry(&ga, 0.0f, &ga);
        moon_pole_geometry(&g0, 0.17453293f, &gaa); /* +10 deg */
        moon_reproject(shade_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, &ga, a, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR);
        moon_reproject(shade_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, &gaa, b, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR);
        moon_bake(&ga, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), a + PX * PX, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
        static uint8_t bb[PX * PX];
        moon_bake(&gaa, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), bb, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 0, 0.0f);
        double sr = 0, sb = 0;
        int nr = 0;
        for (int y = 0; y < PX; y++)
            for (int x = 0; x < PX; x++) {
                float u = (x - 199.5f) / 200.0f, v = (199.5f - y) / 200.0f;
                if (u * u + v * v > 1.0f)
                    continue;
                int dr = (int)b[y * PX + x] - (int)a[y * PX + x];
                int db = (int)bb[y * PX + x] - (int)(a + PX * PX)[y * PX + x];
                dr = dr < 0 ? -dr : dr;
                db = db < 0 ? -db : db;
                sr += dr;
                sb += db;
                nr++;
            }
        sr /= nr, sb /= nr;
        double diff = sr > sb ? sr - sb : sb - sr;
        printf("  temporal (10 deg step): reproject f-delta=%.2f bake f-delta=%.2f |d|=%.2f\n", sr, sb, diff);
        /* The map's temporal delta may exceed the bake's by the cell
         * re-sampling, but must stay within ~1.5x of it (same content). */
        if (diff > 0.5 * (sr + sb))
            g_fail++;
    }

    printf("== 4. backlit night side (dark_zero = 1): the device's path\n"
           "    The dusk/static/sweep bake the COMPUTED night side (albedo + relief\n"
           "    lit from -S) instead of the earthshine. The constant-projection\n"
           "    promise must still hold for it: the backlit shade map (built once,\n"
           "    dark_zero = 1 + dk_sup) re-projected through a fold must match the\n"
           "    per-frame backlit bake (same dark_zero = 1 + dk_sup) to cell-center\n"
           "    class, and the endpoint must be a clean backlit disk (no lit rim\n"
           "    sliver -- the 'white ray' kill) with some surface spread (not flat).\n");
    static uint8_t backlit_map[MOON_ALB_W * MOON_ALB_H];
    for (unsigned e = 0; e < 3; e++) {
        int64_t epoch = e == 1 ? iso(epochs[e]) : now - 7 * 86400LL * (int)e;
        moon_geom_t g0;
        moon_geometry(epoch, &g0);
        /* The dusk endpoint + dk_sup (same math as the device's dusk task):
         * phi* minimizes E(phi).S, dk_sup = sqrt(1 - E.S(phi*)^2) = the
         * endpoint disk's max d. */
        float A = g0.E[0] * g0.S[0] + g0.E[1] * g0.S[1];
        float B = g0.E[0] * g0.S[1] - g0.E[1] * g0.S[0];
        float phi = atan2f(-B, -A);
        float fmin = A * cosf(phi) + B * sinf(phi) + g0.E[2] * g0.S[2];
        float dk_sup = sqrtf(fmaxf(0.0f, 1.0f - fmin * fmin));
        /* The backlit map, built ONCE from the unfolded geometry. */
        moon_shade_map_build(&g0, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), backlit_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 1, dk_sup);
        /* Start (phi=0) and endpoint (phi*) folds: reproject vs per-frame bake. */
        const float folds[2] = {0.0f, phi};
        const char *folds_name[2] = {"start", "endpoint"};
        for (unsigned t = 0; t < 2; t++) {
            moon_geom_t gb;
            moon_inplane_geometry(&g0, 0.0f, &gb);
            moon_pole_geometry(&gb, folds[t], &gb);
            moon_bake(&gb, moon_albedo(), moon_relief(), b, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, 1, dk_sup);
            moon_reproject(backlit_map, MOON_ALB_W, MOON_ALB_H, &gb, a, PX, RAD, CTR, CTR);
            /* Pixel classes: 0 = black (out of disk / the sun-lit sliver,
             * clipped to pure black); 0 < g <= 40 = the faint backlit
             * surface (peak 255 * MOON_NIGHT_BACKLIT_K = 25, relief can
             * round a hair higher); g > 40 = the lit crescent (TONE_LUT
             * of the lit side, 137+ at the crescent edge). The 40 split
             * sits well above the backlit peak and well below the lit. */
            double sum = 0;
            int mx = 0, n = 0, lit = 0, backlit_cnt = 0, backlit_hi = 0;
            for (int y = 0; y < PX; y++)
                for (int x = 0; x < PX; x++) {
                    float u = (x - 199.5f) / 200.0f, v = (199.5f - y) / 200.0f;
                    if (u * u + v * v > 1.0f)
                        continue;
                    int d = (int)a[y * PX + x] - (int)b[y * PX + x];
                    d = d < 0 ? -d : d;
                    sum += d;
                    if (d > mx)
                        mx = d;
                    n++;
                    int g = b[y * PX + x];
                    if (g > 40)
                        lit++; /* the lit crescent */
                    else if (g > 0) {
                        backlit_cnt++; /* the computed backlit dark side */
                        if (g > backlit_hi)
                            backlit_hi = g;
                    }
                }
            double mae = sum / (double)n;
            printf("  epoch=%ld d %s: reproject-vs-bake MAE=%.2f max=%d | lit px=%d backlit px>0=%d backlit max=%d\n",
                   (long)(epoch - now) / 86400, folds_name[t], mae, mx, lit, backlit_cnt, backlit_hi);
            /* Cell-center class (the same tolerance as section 3). */
            if (mae > 7.0)
                g_fail++;
            /* At the ENDPOINT the visible disk is fully night (d <= dk_sup):
             * the lit crescent is gone, so NO pixel may read as lit (> 40) --
             * a lit pixel here is the rim sliver (the "white ray") leaking
             * through (the backlit side clips the sun-lit sliver to black).
             * The whole disk must be the faint COMPUTED surface: a large
             * backlit count with backlit_hi exceeding the old flat floor
             * (10) -- the dark side has surface structure, not a flat overlay. */
            if (t == 1) {
                if (lit > 0 || backlit_cnt < n / 2 || backlit_hi < 12)
                    g_fail++;
            }
        }
    }

    printf(g_fail ? "POLE TEST FAIL (%d)\n" : "POLE TEST PASS\n", g_fail);
    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;
}
```

### `host_sim/render_demo.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render the README animation demos: three montages of exact panel frames
rendered by moon_sim (the device's own core, at --size 466).

Deps: the moon_sim binary (cmake --build host_sim/build) + PIL.

Montages (docs/img/, committed):
  boot_sweep.png   one synodic month, new moon -> now (12 frames)
  free_spin.png    the settled free spin: 8 rotations at 45 deg steps
  dusk.png         the pole-axis spin to the dark side (0 -> phi*)

Each cell is downscaled to ~200 px; the full 466 px frames are the exact
RGB565 panel pixels (see the PNG decode in moon_sim main.c).
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import math
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SIM = REPO / "host_sim" / "build" / "moon_sim"
OUT = REPO / "docs" / "img"
FONT_CANDIDATES = [
    "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf",
    "/usr/share/fonts/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf",
]

CELL = 200  # downscale target per frame
PAD = 12
COLS = 4
TITLE_H = 40
LABEL_H = 20

SYNODIC = 29.530588853 * 86400.0  # mean synodic month, seconds
REF_NEW_MOON = datetime.datetime(2026, 1, 18, 11, 57, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)  # JPL


def iso(dt):
    return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M")


def label(dt):
    return dt.strftime("%b %d %H:%M")


def last_new_moon(now):
    k = math.floor((now - REF_NEW_MOON).total_seconds() / SYNODIC)
    return REF_NEW_MOON + datetime.timedelta(seconds=k * SYNODIC)


def render_frame(out_dir, utc, rot=0, pole=0, darkzero=False):
    args = [str(SIM), "--utc", utc, "--rot", str(rot), "--pole", str(pole),
            "--size", "466", "--out", str(out_dir)]
    if darkzero:
        args.append("--darkzero")
    subprocess.run(args, check=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    return out_dir / "sim.png"


def montage(path, title, cells, labels):
    """cells: [PIL.Image] (square), labels: one string per cell."""
    rows = math.ceil(len(cells) / COLS)
    w = PAD + COLS * (CELL + PAD)
    h = TITLE_H + rows * (CELL + LABEL_H + PAD)
    img = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), (0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    try:
        font_title = ImageFont.truetype(next(f for f in FONT_CANDIDATES if pathlib.Path(f).exists()), 22)
        font_cell = ImageFont.truetype(next(f for f in FONT_CANDIDATES if pathlib.Path(f).exists()), 14)
    except (StopIteration, OSError):
        font_title = ImageFont.load_default()
        font_cell = ImageFont.load_default()
    d.text((PAD, 8), title, font=font_title, fill=(255, 255, 255))
    for i, (cell, lab) in enumerate(zip(cells, labels)):
        r, c = divmod(i, COLS)
        x = PAD + c * (CELL + PAD)
        y = TITLE_H + r * (CELL + LABEL_H + PAD)
        small = cell.resize((CELL, CELL), Image.LANCZOS)
        img.paste(small, (x, y))
        d.text((x, y + CELL + 2), lab, font=font_cell, fill=(190, 190, 190))
    img.save(path)
    print(f"{path}: {len(cells)} frames, {path.stat().st_size // 1024} KiB")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--now", default="2026-10-28T12:00", help="demo epoch (ISO, UTC)")
    ap.add_argument("--phi-star", type=float, default=None,
                    help="dusk endpoint in degrees for the demo epoch (device 'dusk started' log or phi_star probe)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    now = datetime.datetime.strptime(args.now, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M").replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    new_moon = last_new_moon(now)
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    frames = OUT / "frames"

    def frame_dir(name, i):
        p = frames / name
        p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return p

    # 1. Boot sweep: new moon -> now, 12 even steps. dark_zero on every
    # frame but the last (the device's montage path: the final frame is the
    # full current phase).
    steps = 12
    t0, t1 = new_moon.timestamp(), now.timestamp()
    cells, labs = [], []
    for k in range(steps):
        t = t0 + (t1 - t0) * k / (steps - 1)
        utc = iso(datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(t, datetime.timezone.utc))
        p = render_frame(frame_dir("boot", k), utc, darkzero=k < steps - 1)
        cells.append(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"))
        labs.append(label(datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(t, datetime.timezone.utc)))
    montage(OUT / "boot_sweep.png", f"Boot sweep -- one synodic month ({label(new_moon)} -> {label(now)})", cells, labs)

    # 2. Free spin: settled pose, 8 rotations at 45 deg.
    cells, labs = [], []
    for rot in range(0, 360, 45):
        p = render_frame(frame_dir("spin", rot), iso(now), rot=rot)
        cells.append(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"))
        labs.append(f"rot {rot}\xb0")
    montage(OUT / "free_spin.png", f"Free spin -- {label(now)} (8 rotations at 45\xb0)", cells, labs)

    # 3. Dusk: pole-axis spin 0 -> phi* (device endpoint, 1 deg/frame).
    phi = args.phi_star
    if phi is None:
        # The endpoint is epoch-specific: pass it with --phi-star (device
        # log 'dusk started: N frames (+N deg about the pole)' or the
        # phi_star probe compiled against components/moon).
        print("pass --phi-star DEG (the dusk endpoint for the demo epoch)")
        sys.exit(1)
    n = 9
    cells, labs = [], []
    for k in range(n):
        pole = round(phi * k / (n - 1))
        p = render_frame(frame_dir("dusk", pole), iso(now), pole=pole)
        cells.append(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"))
        labs.append(f"pole {pole}\xb0")
    montage(OUT / "dusk.png", f"Dusk -- pole spin to the dark side (0 -> {phi:.0f}\xb0)", cells, labs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### `host_sim/stb_image_write.h`

```c
/* stb_image_write - v1.16 - public domain - http://nothings.org/stb
   writes out PNG/BMP/TGA/JPEG/HDR images to C stdio - Sean Barrett 2010-2015
                                     no warranty implied; use at your own risk

   Before #including,

       #define STB_IMAGE_WRITE_IMPLEMENTATION

   in the file that you want to have the implementation.

   Will probably not work correctly with strict-aliasing optimizations.

ABOUT:

   This header file is a library for writing images to C stdio or a callback.

   The PNG output is not optimal; it is 20-50% larger than the file
   written by a decent optimizing implementation; though providing a custom
   zlib compress function (see STBIW_ZLIB_COMPRESS) can mitigate that.
   This library is designed for source code compactness and simplicity,
   not optimal image file size or run-time performance.

BUILDING:

   You can #define STBIW_ASSERT(x) before the #include to avoid using assert.h.
   You can #define STBIW_MALLOC(), STBIW_REALLOC(), and STBIW_FREE() to replace
   malloc,realloc,free.
   You can #define STBIW_MEMMOVE() to replace memmove()
   You can #define STBIW_ZLIB_COMPRESS to use a custom zlib-style compress function
   for PNG compression (instead of the builtin one), it must have the following signature:
   unsigned char * my_compress(unsigned char *data, int data_len, int *out_len, int quality);
   The returned data will be freed with STBIW_FREE() (free() by default),
   so it must be heap allocated with STBIW_MALLOC() (malloc() by default),

UNICODE:

   If compiling for Windows and you wish to use Unicode filenames, compile
   with
       #define STBIW_WINDOWS_UTF8
   and pass utf8-encoded filenames. Call stbiw_convert_wchar_to_utf8 to convert
   Windows wchar_t filenames to utf8.

USAGE:

   There are five functions, one for each image file format:

     int stbi_write_png(char const *filename, int w, int h, int comp, const void *data, int stride_in_bytes);
     int stbi_write_bmp(char const *filename, int w, int h, int comp, const void *data);
     int stbi_write_tga(char const *filename, int w, int h, int comp, const void *data);
     int stbi_write_jpg(char const *filename, int w, int h, int comp, const void *data, int quality);
     int stbi_write_hdr(char const *filename, int w, int h, int comp, const float *data);

     void stbi_flip_vertically_on_write(int flag); // flag is non-zero to flip data vertically

   There are also five equivalent functions that use an arbitrary write function. You are
   expected to open/close your file-equivalent before and after calling these:

     int stbi_write_png_to_func(stbi_write_func *func, void *context, int w, int h, int comp, const void  *data, int
stride_in_bytes); int stbi_write_bmp_to_func(stbi_write_func *func, void *context, int w, int h, int comp, const void
*data); int stbi_write_tga_to_func(stbi_write_func *func, void *context, int w, int h, int comp, const void  *data); int
stbi_write_hdr_to_func(stbi_write_func *func, void *context, int w, int h, int comp, const float *data); int
stbi_write_jpg_to_func(stbi_write_func *func, void *context, int x, int y, int comp, const void *data, int quality);

   where the callback is:
      void stbi_write_func(void *context, void *data, int size);

   You can configure it with these global variables:
      int stbi_write_tga_with_rle;             // defaults to true; set to 0 to disable RLE
      int stbi_write_png_compression_level;    // defaults to 8; set to higher for more compression
      int stbi_write_force_png_filter;         // defaults to -1; set to 0..5 to force a filter mode


   You can define STBI_WRITE_NO_STDIO to disable the file variant of these
   functions, so the library will not use stdio.h at all. However, this will
   also disable HDR writing, because it requires stdio for formatted output.

   Each function returns 0 on failure and non-0 on success.

   The functions create an image file defined by the parameters. The image
   is a rectangle of pixels stored from left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
   Each pixel contains 'comp' channels of data stored interleaved with 8-bits
   per channel, in the following order: 1=Y, 2=YA, 3=RGB, 4=RGBA. (Y is
   monochrome color.) The rectangle is 'w' pixels wide and 'h' pixels tall.
   The *data pointer points to the first byte of the top-left-most pixel.
   For PNG, "stride_in_bytes" is the distance in bytes from the first byte of
   a row of pixels to the first byte of the next row of pixels.

   PNG creates output files with the same number of components as the input.
   The BMP format expands Y to RGB in the file format and does not
   output alpha.

   PNG supports writing rectangles of data even when the bytes storing rows of
   data are not consecutive in memory (e.g. sub-rectangles of a larger image),
   by supplying the stride between the beginning of adjacent rows. The other
   formats do not. (Thus you cannot write a native-format BMP through the BMP
   writer, both because it is in BGR order and because it may have padding
   at the end of the line.)

   PNG allows you to set the deflate compression level by setting the global
   variable 'stbi_write_png_compression_level' (it defaults to 8).

   HDR expects linear float data. Since the format is always 32-bit rgb(e)
   data, alpha (if provided) is discarded, and for monochrome data it is
   replicated across all three channels.

   TGA supports RLE or non-RLE compressed data. To use non-RLE-compressed
   data, set the global variable 'stbi_write_tga_with_rle' to 0.

   JPEG does ignore alpha channels in input data; quality is between 1 and 100.
   Higher quality looks better but results in a bigger image.
   JPEG baseline (no JPEG progressive).

CREDITS:


   Sean Barrett           -    PNG/BMP/TGA
   Baldur Karlsson        -    HDR
   Jean-Sebastien Guay    -    TGA monochrome
   Tim Kelsey             -    misc enhancements
   Alan Hickman           -    TGA RLE
   Emmanuel Julien        -    initial file IO callback implementation
   Jon Olick              -    original jo_jpeg.cpp code
   Daniel Gibson          -    integrate JPEG, allow external zlib
   Aarni Koskela          -    allow choosing PNG filter

   bugfixes:
      github:Chribba
      Guillaume Chereau
      github:jry2
      github:romigrou
      Sergio Gonzalez
      Jonas Karlsson
      Filip Wasil
      Thatcher Ulrich
      github:poppolopoppo
      Patrick Boettcher
      github:xeekworx
      Cap Petschulat
      Simon Rodriguez
      Ivan Tikhonov
      github:ignotion
      Adam Schackart
      Andrew Kensler

LICENSE

  See end of file for license information.

*/

#ifndef INCLUDE_STB_IMAGE_WRITE_H

#ifdef STB_IMAGE_WRITE_IMPLEMENTATION

#if defined(STBIW_MALLOC) && defined(STBIW_FREE) && (defined(STBIW_REALLOC) || defined(STBIW_REALLOC_SIZED))
// ok

#endif

#endif

#endif

#ifndef STBIW_ASSERT
#include <assert.h>
#define STBIW_ASSERT(x) assert(x)
#endif

#define STBIW_UCHAR(x) (unsigned char)((x) & 0xff)

#ifdef STB_IMAGE_WRITE_STATIC
static int stbi_write_png_compression_level = 8;
static int stbi_write_tga_with_rle = 1;
static int stbi_write_force_png_filter = -1;
#else
int stbi_write_png_compression_level = 8;
```
